items.author: Andjela Radmilac
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitfarms paid nearly $11.9 million in October 2025 over machines imported in 2021.
- Its supplier claimed Malaysian origin, but US Customs determined the equipment was Chinese.
- IREN successfully challenged a separate potential $100 million assessment.
Bitcoin miner Bitfarms thought the machines it brought into Washington state in 2021 had been made in Malaysia. Its supplier said so, and the company provided US Customs officials with documents supporting that claim.
Four years later, the company paid the government $11.9 million. US Customs and Border Protection had challenged the machines' declared origin, arguing that they were made in China and subject to a 25% import duty.
Bitfarms disputed the assessment, but its financial statements show it paid in October 2025, after Customs told it the duties were required.
The payment shows a cost that can follow a mining company long after its equipment was delivered and started working. Other miners have faced similar disputes over where their machines were made, with one company recently avoiding a potential $100 million assessment and another still contesting an estimate that reached $130 million.
Those numbers don't add up to a single bill for the industry. Each dispute involves different shipments, documents, and decisions, and the outcomes can look very different even when the companies believe they have evidence supporting their declared origins.
A bill four years in the making
Bitfarms' dispute began in early 2022, when Customs challenged the origin of the machines imported the previous year. The company said its Chinese vendor had represented that the equipment came from Malaysia, while Customs asserted that it was manufactured in China.
The miner submitted supporting documents in the third quarter of 2023 and again in the first quarter of 2025. It also paid $180,000 of the duties in 2024, according to its later filing. As of June 2025, management said it didn't consider a future cash outflow probable and hadn't recorded a provision for the dispute.
That was an accounting assessment based on what the company knew at the time. In August 2025, Customs responded that duties were required, and Bitfarms reported the payment two months later.
Bitfarms disclosed $180,000 of customs duties paid in 2024 and a separate $11.9 million payment to Customs in October 2025, including interest. The filing’s stated duties and interest components do not reconcile to its reported October payment.
The company hasn't disclosed enough to reconstruct every step of the customs process or establish whether it paid under protest. Nonetheless, its filings do show how a dispute over a shipment can remain relevant to a company's finances long after the initial purchase.
Bitfarms has since reorganized under Keel Infrastructure and shifted toward AI and high-performance computing. It paid the customs bill before that transition reached a major milestone: Keel stopped its US Bitcoin mining operations in June 2026 as it prepared sites for other uses.
Other miners have also been shifting power access and data-center sites toward AI, while older import disputes still appear in their financial disclosures.
The money involved can affect how much they have available for equipment and projects, although a disclosed potential charge isn't necessarily money they will have to pay.
Where a Bitcoin mining machine comes from
Import duties can depend on where a product was made, which sounds simple until a machine contains components from several countries and is assembled elsewhere.
US customs forms ask importers to identify the product's country of origin. When production takes place in more than one country, the answer can depend on where the product underwent its last substantial transformation, according to Customs' entry instructions.
The manufacturing process and supporting records can affect the duty owed. The supplier's certificate can support the declared origin, but Customs can still challenge it.
Equipment can also be released and put to work before Customs resolves every issue. Customs uses a process called liquidation to make its final duty calculation for an entry.
Importers can challenge certain decisions through an administrative protest, but deadlines and exceptions depend on the decision being challenged. The public filings don't establish which procedural rules explain every stage of the miners' disputes.
Selling the equipment doesn't automatically settle an importer's customs obligations either. Federal regulations describe duties as a debt owed by the importer, which can be discharged through payment or applicable legal relief.
That doesn't mean the buyer of a secondhand machine automatically inherits the seller's customs bill, since the importer and the terms of any transaction need to be identified separately.
Four Bitcoin miners with different outcomes
IREN received a notice in April 2025 concerning hardware it imported between April 2024 and February 2025. Customs asserted that the equipment was of Chinese origin and assessed a 25% tariff, while IREN said the seller and shipping documents supported a different origin.
The company contested an exposure of approximately $100 million. In October 2026, Customs approved its protests and accepted the declared origin of the covered hardware, IREN reported in its September-quarter filing. No additional tariff, administrative fee, or interest is payable for that matter.
The $100 million was an amount IREN had disputed and no longer has to pay for the covered imports. The company hasn't disclosed enough about the decision to establish whether the same reasoning applies to other shipments or other miners.
CleanSpark has had a mixed outcome so far. In its June-quarter filing, submitted in August, the miner said Customs had approved some of its protests over machines imported in 2024, while other entries remained contested.
If Customs prevailed on the remaining entries, CleanSpark estimated that its total tariff liability for the previously purchased machines could reach approximately $130 million, excluding interest. Management considered a loss improbable and recorded no provision as of June 30.
DarkHorse Technologies, previously known as Sphere 3D, faces a smaller claim that shows how an older equipment purchase can appear in the accounts of a miner with a different name and business plan.
In August, Customs notified DarkHorse that it was asserting Chinese-origin duties on machines purchased in 2022 by a subsidiary acquired in the Cathedra Bitcoin combination.
The company says its subsidiary received certificates from the seller supporting a non-Chinese origin, and it filed a protest in September. Its latest quarterly report puts potential liability at up to $2.3 million, including interest, if Customs prevails. DarkHorse has not recorded a liability.
Company estimates if Customs prevails. CleanSpark's was approximately $130 million excluding interest as of June 30. DarkHorse's was up to $2.3 million including interest in its Sept. 30 report. Reporting dates and interest treatment differ.
DarkHorse is separately selling its legacy mining fleet as it shifts toward AI infrastructure. Its quarterly report estimated $2.9 million in proceeds, with $1.3 million from machines sold by Sept. 30.
Bitfarms reported a payment, IREN's covered assessment has been resolved, CleanSpark's estimate excludes interest, and DarkHorse's includes it. Adding them together would treat a past payment and an avoided charge as outstanding bills.
CleanSpark's remaining protests and DarkHorse's challenge will determine whether either miner faces a further payment on the disputed imports.
IREN's result shows that a challenge can succeed, while Bitfarms' earlier payment shows why investors can't assume that a company's initial accounting assessment will be the final word.
items.title: One Bitcoin miner paid an $11.9M tariff bill four years after delivery

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- The U.S. Treasury auctioned $15 billion of nine-day cash management bills on Nov. 19.
- The bills are due to settle Nov. 24 and mature Dec. 3, taking the borrowing across month-end.
- Treasury had flagged possible month-end borrowing and ended auction day with $891 billion in cash.
The U.S. Treasury auctioned $15 billion of nine-day cash management bills on Nov. 19, its first sale at that exact term since July 2008. The bills are scheduled to settle Nov. 24 and mature Dec. 3, putting the borrowing across the turn of the month.
Treasury had already flagged a possible short bill in its November financing plan. Its operating cash balance on auction day was within the range it had recorded in 2026. The proceeds were due when the bill settled five days later, so the auction-day balance gives a snapshot of Treasury’s cash before the new borrowing arrived.
The sale reopened a bill first issued on June 4. Investors could buy more of the same security, which kept its Dec. 3 maturity date. Treasury reported a high discount rate of 3.91% and a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.97. The ratio measures the face value of accepted and rejected offers Treasury counted, about $60 billion, against the just over $15 billion it awarded.
Treasury auctions cash management bills as needed to meet short-term financing needs. A recent sale ran one day longer. On Oct. 22, Treasury auctioned $25 billion of ten-day bills at a 3.93% high discount rate. Those bills were issued Oct. 26 and matured Nov. 5.
Before the November sale, Treasury’s previous nine-day auction was July 21, 2008, according to its historical auction records. It offered $9 billion at that sale, with a July 22 issue date and July 31 maturity.
Short bills remained in use. The legacy auction series records 29 cash management bill sales with terms of ten days or less after the July 2008 sale, through December 2025. The updated series includes the October and November 2026 auctions.
What Treasury’s cash balance shows
In its Nov. 4 quarterly refunding statement, Treasury said it might issue a short-dated bill around the end of November for cash management. It announced the offering on Nov. 18 and released the results the next day. The auction documents gave investors the dates for paying Treasury and getting repaid. They identified no specific federal expenses tied to the borrowing.
In a Nov. 20 post on X, @0xCVYH likened the sale to an overdraft, said Treasury’s cash had grown tight and argued that the borrowing would help cover end-of-month expenses. The auction schedule confirms that the borrowing spans month-end. The cash data offer a separate check on how unusual Treasury’s balance was at the time.
The Daily Treasury Statement put the Treasury General Account, the government’s operating cash account, at $891.223 billion at the Nov. 19 close, down from $892.310 billion the day before. Across Treasury’s daily balance series through Nov. 19, the 2026 low was $686.969 billion on April 9 and the high was $1.05253 trillion on Oct. 27. Nov. 19 was the latest close available as of Nov. 21. That snapshot gives a sense of scale. Assessing the pressure on Treasury’s cash also requires knowing when receipts and payments are due.
Treasury’s cash before settlement
The nine-day borrowing window starts on Nov. 24, five days after Treasury recorded its auction-day cash balance.
Three Treasury General Account closing balances, in U.S. dollars. The April low and October high cover 2026 through Nov. 19.
The Nov. 19 close sits within Treasury’s observed 2026 range, before investors are scheduled to pay for the new bills.
The chart uses three observed closes through Nov. 19. The two future dates show the announced schedule. The balance comparisons alone cannot identify which expenses Treasury planned to finance.
Treasury’s November financing plan assumed $850 billion in cash at the end of December 2026. It projected possible peaks of $1,025 billion, give or take $50 billion, in late November 2026 and late January 2027 ahead of large expected outflows.
For crypto traders who follow dollar liquidity, Nov. 24 settlement and Dec. 3 maturity mark when cash from the sale is due to move. Investors are scheduled to pay Treasury on the first date and be repaid on the second. As CryptoSlate previously reported, money moving out of Treasury’s account can lift bank reserves, all else equal. The next daily cash and reserve readings can show the combined effect of the auction and the government’s other transactions.
items.title: US Treasury sells $15 billion in first nine-day cash bill auction since 2008

谷歌预告12月2日迈出第一步：Gemini订阅有望接入第三方Agent

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Gemini 4 Neon 发布后，开发者 Kun Chen 发帖称，模型的对话体验让人耳目一新，但谷歌还需要允许用户在任意第三方 Agent 工具中使用 Gemini 订阅。Google AI Studio 与 Gemini API 产品负责人 Logan Kilpatrick 随后回应：「12 月 2 日，我们迈出第一步。」

Harness 指运行 AI Agent 的工具或框架。比如 Claude Code、OpenCode、pi、Hermes 等。开发者希望保留自己熟悉的工作流，直接调用 Gemini 模型，并消耗已有的 Google AI 订阅额度，不必为了使用 Gemini 转投 Antigravity，也不必额外购买 API 额度。

谷歌此前一直限制第三方工具使用 Gemini 订阅。Google Antigravity 官方 FAQ 明确规定，通过 Claude Code、OpenClaw、OpenCode 等第三方工具调用 Antigravity 账号属于违规行为，可能导致账号被封禁。官方目前建议开发者通过 Google AI Studio 或 Vertex AI 的 API Key 接入第三方工具。

评论区已经有开发者点名希望支持 OpenCode、pi、AmpCode 等工具，也有人表示，愿意购买更高档的 Google AI 订阅，但不想为了使用 Gemini 更换整套工作流。

items.content:
MiniMax「零数据保留」翻车：用户提示词里的链接，几天后竟被人打开

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenRouter 开始向部分 MiniMax 用户发送隐私警告：用户发给 MiniMax 模型的提示词和回答，可能被第三方读取。

一名安全研究人员在 2026 年 7 月至 10 月期间，向 MiniMax 模型发送测试请求，并在提示词中埋入只有这次请求才有的特殊网址。结果，请求发出 40 至 130 小时后，这些网址陆续被第三方打开。也就是说，虽然模型早已完成回答，仍然有其他人或系统拿到了提示词里的内容。

测试结果将问题指向 MiniMax。无论用户直接调用 MiniMax API，还是通过 AtlasCloud、Novita、StreamLake 等服务商转发，只要请求最终交给 MiniMax 处理，都出现了提示词中的测试链接被访问的情况。相同服务商转发给其他模型的请求则几乎没有出现同一现象。

OpenRouter 已撤下 MiniMax 相关模型端点的「零数据保留」（ZDR）标签。MiniMax 曾向 StreamLake 表示，10 月 22 日之前 API 启用了内容审核，此后才启用零数据保留。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378567

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- The Nasdaq has lost 18% from its October record, while Nvidia is down nearly 48% and CoreWeave has plunged almost 80% from their respective peaks.
- Polymarket traders put the probability of a defined AI industry downturn by December 31 at roughly 54%, as analysts debate whether the selloff resembles the dot-com crash.
- Bitcoin has fallen below $60,000 and the total cryptocurrency market has shrunk to approximately $2 trillion, extending the damage well beyond technology stocks.
Wall Street's artificial intelligence boom is facing its biggest test yet.
Nvidia plunged 14% on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite lost 5.3%, and the broader S&P 500 entered correction territory as investors questioned whether the trillions of dollars being poured into AI infrastructure will ever produce the expected returns.
The Nasdaq closed at 22,617.73, approximately 18% below its October 6 record closing high of 27,599.79. Its 10% weekly decline was the worst since 2020, while the index has now erased its gains for 2026.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Nvidia with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Nvidia, the company that powered much of the AI rally, finished Friday at $125.53, down 47.5% from its October closing record of $239.24.
The chipmaker lost nearly 23% during the week as the fallout from former CEO Jensen Huang's departure and reports of an SEC accounting investigation added to concerns about the AI business model.
Other AI-linked companies have suffered even steeper losses. CoreWeave, which rents computing capacity to AI developers, closed at $39.51, almost 80% below its 2025 peak, while Oracle has lost roughly 70% from its highs and finished the week at $101.19.
AMD shed 20.5% over the week, closing at $424.39, while Alphabet lost 10.3% to $265.29. The iShares Semiconductor ETF, SOXX, dropped 17.4% during the same period, showing that investors are selling across the companies supplying the AI industry, not merely its most speculative businesses.
The selloff accelerated just as Anthropic completed its historic $81 billion IPO. The Claude developer priced its shares at $83 and closed its first trading session 17% higher, but its stock fell another 9% on Friday as enthusiasm for the offering failed to restore confidence in the wider sector.
With so many stocks in the red, it’s logical that many AI fanboys are starting to get nervous.
Traders on Polymarket have become increasingly pessimistic. Contracts assessing whether the AI industry will experience a defined downturn showed approximately 54% odds by December 31, 2026, and 65% by June 30, 2027, according to Friday's market snapshot.
The market has attracted approximately $4.1 million in trading volume, but its definition of a bubble bursting is more demanding than a falling stock market. At least three specific events must occur within a single 90-day period, including Nvidia closing 50% below its all-time high, SOXX falling 40%, major AI suppliers experiencing similar collapses, or severe financial problems at AI developers.
SOXX has already fallen approximately 43% from its split-adjusted record closing price, satisfying one of the specified price thresholds on paper. Nvidia is approaching another, although crossing either threshold alone would not settle the contract.
Bitcoin and crypto are getting dragged into the selloff
The damage has also spread into cryptocurrencies, undermining expectations that 2026 would bring a sustained recovery. Bitcoin finished the week near $58,895, down 9.8% over the period and more than 50% below its 2025 peak.
The total cryptocurrency market capitalization fell to approximately $2.01 trillion, down from more than $4 trillion at its peak. As Decrypt reported Friday, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to 9, signaling extreme fear and its weakest reading since February.
This was supposed to be the year of the usual pre-halving moon. Instead, for the first time in the history of Bitcoin, the coin is on its way to have two consecutive red years.
Bitcoin has increasingly behaved like other speculative assets sensitive to liquidity conditions, particularly when investors expect borrowing costs to remain elevated.
The pressure is also visible in investment flows. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.2 million in net withdrawals on Thursday, while forced liquidations added to the selling as Bitcoin broke below the psychologically important $60,000 level.
Is this dot-com 2.0? Experts have something to say
Owen Lamont, a portfolio manager at Acadian Asset Management and former University of Chicago finance professor, believes the warning signs have become difficult to ignore. After arguing in January that AI stocks were not yet in a bubble, he told Fortune this week that he now assigns a 70% probability to the U.S. stock market already being in one.
Lamont tracks four warning signs: excessive valuations, widespread belief in a speculative boom, new stock issuance, and investors pouring money into the market. His latest assessment suggests all four are now present, although his issuance figures are heavily influenced by SpaceX's massive IPO earlier this year.
Bank of America's November fund manager survey offers another indication of deteriorating confidence. Investors reduced their technology exposure by the most since 2006, and 52% expect at least one major AI hyperscaler to announce a capital spending cut within six months, Fortune reported.
The European Central Bank has also raised concerns about how AI development is being financed. Its November review estimates that capital expenditure by major American technology companies could reach $5.5 trillion cumulatively by 2030, with growing reliance on debt as infrastructure spending outpaces internally generated cash.
The similarities to the dot-com era are difficult to dismiss: investors are assigning enormous valuations to companies based on projected demand, businesses are racing to build infrastructure ahead of proven profitability, and financial markets are increasingly dependent on a small group of technology companies.
During the original dot-com collapse, the Nasdaq lost approximately 78% between March 2000 and October 2002. The present decline is considerably smaller, but history also offers a reminder that a technology can succeed commercially while the companies financing its expansion lose enormous amounts of market value.
There are important differences, however. Many of today's largest AI beneficiaries, including Nvidia, Alphabet, and Microsoft, operate profitable businesses with substantial existing revenues, unlike numerous internet startups whose valuations depended almost entirely on future growth.
Nvidia's latest quarterly results illustrate the contradiction. The company beat earnings estimates, reported record revenue and net income, and issued stronger-than-expected revenue guidance, yet its shares continued collapsing.
Richard Saperstein, chief investment officer at Treasury Partners, described the downturn as an "AI repricing" in comments to Reuters, citing slowing data center construction and tighter funding conditions. Lawrence Gillum, chief fixed income strategist at LPL Financial, offered a less alarming interpretation, saying the decline was "not a bubble bursting" and arguing that the AI investment cycle still has room to run.
Higher interest rates complicate both arguments. Investors are increasingly expecting the Federal Reserve to raise rates again in December, increasing financing costs for data centers while reducing the appeal of stocks whose valuations depend on profits years into the future.
The balance of evidence points to more than a routine bout of nerves, but less than a confirmed systemic bust. Stocks have repriced faster than the underlying technology has changed.
What happens next depends on whether actual demand for AI can justify the data-center spending spree—and whether the companies financing it can withstand tighter credit. The real test isn't simply whether Nvidia can keep selling chips. It's whether its customers can turn all that computing power into profits.
Right now much of the AI hype is just… hype. Markets are moving more by the perceived potential of AI in the future and not so much by what AI is actually doing right now.
Crypto investors have seen this before with ICOs, the TPS wars, the metaverse, the NFT fever and more. For many of them, the distinction may offer little comfort.
Bitcoin's slump shows how quickly markets can stop distinguishing between promising technologies and overpriced bets when confidence disappears. The dot-com crash didn't kill the internet; it killed the assumption that every internet company would make its investors rich.
AI may be the next world-changing technology to prove that being right about the future is not the same as making money from it.

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Kraken’s BTC/CAD pair touched C$24,250 on November 21 and reached nearly the same low in the next 15-minute interval.
- At 13:06 UTC, the last BTC/CAD trade in Kraken’s ticker was C$82,099.
- Kraken blamed heavy selling across its CAD pairs and said executed trades would stand.
Bitcoin hit C$24,250 on Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market on Saturday, Nov. 21. The next 15-minute trading interval came within C$1.40 of that low. Kraken said executed trades would stand after heavy selling pushed its Canadian-dollar pairs below prices elsewhere.
The C$24,250 low was about 71% below the Canadian-dollar conversion on CryptoSlate’s Bitcoin price page at 09:40 UTC. The comparison puts an earlier Kraken trade alongside a later reference value. CryptoSlate displayed a price of US$57,809 and a converted value of C$82,708 at that check.
Kraken’s Canadian-dollar pair had already reached C$61,880 during the 15 minutes starting at 21:00 UTC on Friday. The trading intervals beginning at 06:00 and 07:00 UTC Saturday reached lows of C$50,000 and C$33,750, respectively.
The interval starting at 08:00 UTC opened at C$32,000, ranged from C$24,250 to C$49,999 and ended back at C$32,000. Kraken recorded 976 trades totaling about 22.38 BTC across those 15 minutes. How much Bitcoin changed hands at the lowest price remains unclear.
The next interval reached C$24,251.40 before closing at C$37,000. Kraken’s 09:40 UTC ticker still showed C$24,250 as the 24-hour low. The best bid was C$40,900 and the best ask was C$42,557. Kraken reported a high of C$88,964 and volume of about 658.51 BTC for the rolling 24-hour window. The bid and ask show where buyers and sellers were quoting at the time of the check.
Canadian dollars per Bitcoin. Each label gives the start of a selected 15-minute interval in UTC.
What Kraken’s dollar market showed
In the 09:40 UTC ticker, Kraken’s USD/CAD last price was C$0.7304 per U.S. dollar. Multiplying the exchange’s BTC/USD last price of about US$57,796 by that rate gives about C$42,214 per Bitcoin. That was close to C$42,557, the last price Kraken reported for its BTC/CAD pair in the same response.
The comparison shows how different the prices looked using Kraken’s own currency markets. A U.S. dollar traded for fewer Canadian dollars on Kraken, so using Kraken’s rate in place of the broader market conversion brought the implied Bitcoin price much closer to the direct CAD trade. The last trades in the three markets may have occurred at different times. The calculation gives an indicative price, and any actual order would depend on the price and quantity available at execution.
The low prices extended beyond Bitcoin. Kraken’s ticker at 09:40 UTC showed a 24-hour low of 30 Canadian cents per U.S. dollar. Over the same window, USDC fell as low as C$0.49 and USDT reached C$0.0022. Ether and Solana reached lows of C$796 and C$32 on their respective CAD pairs.
Traders watching the CAD pair reported different prices as it moved. At 06:21 UTC, the X account @grebby described an equivalent of about US$39,000 and said a deposit attempt failed. In a 07:15 UTC update, @grebby put the equivalent at US$27,000 and said they had bought and withdrawn Bitcoin. The purchase, execution price and withdrawal remain unverified.
At 08:19 UTC, @alistairmilne described a price of about C$30,000.
As of 09:40 UTC, Kraken’s status page listed no CAD spot-market incident. The incident log showed scheduled U.S. futures maintenance ending at 02:03 UTC, and a separate Banking Circle notice concerned euro and sterling transfers.
Kraken Support said heavy selling pushed its CAD pairs below other markets from around 20:00 UTC on Nov. 20. It said orders were processed correctly, its security team found no sign of a breach or compromised accounts, and executed trades would stand. At 13:06 UTC, the last BTC/CAD trade in Kraken’s ticker was C$82,099.
items.title: Kraken says trades stand after Bitcoin sold at $24,250 Canadian

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027 despite a surge in development activity and faster testing cycles.
- Developers gave Ethereum's largest upgrade just 320 days to launch, although the previous three upgrades required 433 to 475 days.
- Unresolved security concerns and late specification changes threaten further delays as developers prepare for a crucial December test.
Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.
On Nov. 20, Ethereum Foundation researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the upgrade, which the foundation had targeted for the first half of 2026, cannot reach mainnet before mid-January 2027, after delays disrupted its testing schedule.
In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached new highs.
He said:
“Nobody did a bad job, but I think we fooled ourselves, twice.”
His findings show that Glamsterdam was assigned the shortest development timeline in years despite being Ethereum's most ambitious upgrade by several measures.
Glamsterdam exposes limits of faster development cycle
According to Wahrstätter, monthly contributions to Ethereum's technical specifications have increased between twofold and 3.5-fold since 2024, reflecting a substantial acceleration in development activity.
The improvement has extended to testing. Glamsterdam completed 12 development networks, or devnets, in 160 days, compared with seven devnets over 285 days for Pectra, an earlier Ethereum upgrade.
However, Wahrstätter argued that the acceleration has created another problem: developers can now produce specifications, code and tests faster than their colleagues can review them and understand their implications.
That challenge has become more pronounced with Glamsterdam's unprecedented size. The upgrade contains approximately 6,080 lines of execution-layer specifications, compared with 2,318 for Prague, the previous record.
In a separate count of proposal specifications, Wahrstätter put two of Glamsterdam's most important changes, enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS) and block-level access lists (BALs), at approximately 11,900 and 9,300 lines, respectively. The other 16 proposals collectively represent about 3,600 lines.
The complexity is also reflected in EIP-8037, a proposal that changes how Ethereum charges for creating new blockchain state. Although its specifications contain roughly 1,700 lines, the proposal requires approximately 30,000 lines of tests, more than any other proposal included in the upgrade.
Together, this illustrates why faster code production has failed to produce a corresponding acceleration in network upgrades.
Indeed, Wahrstätter's historical analysis showed that every Ethereum upgrade since Dencun has taken more than 400 days from finalizing its scope to reaching mainnet. For context, the three most recent upgrades took between 433 and 475 days, even though their technical scope was smaller than Glamsterdam's.
Ethereum set its shortest upgrade target in years for Glamsterdam
Despite that record, Glamsterdam was given a development target of just 320 days, substantially shorter than the timelines achieved by previous upgrades.
Wahrstätter found that virtually every Ethereum upgrade with an announced target had missed its deadline. Fusaka was the exception, but only after developers removed Ethereum Object Format (EOF), a major component originally planned for inclusion.
Pectra similarly required developers to divide its original scope across separate upgrades.
Glamsterdam took a different approach. Developers kept adding proposals to successive testing environments while work on its two main components, ePBS and BALs, continued.
Unlike earlier upgrades, the team made no comparable reduction in scope to protect its development timeline.
Consequently, Glamsterdam reached public testing before its specifications had stabilized, creating additional work at a stage when developers would ordinarily be preparing for deployment.
Wahrstätter's analysis showed that Ethereum upgrades between Altair and Deneb recorded no specification changes after their first public testnet.
Pectra recorded two changes, while Fusaka recorded one. Glamsterdam registered 10 in just six weeks.
The difference also appeared in client development. Work on Pectra declined substantially after public testing began, whereas Glamsterdam-related activity increased 34% following its Sepolia activation, alongside a 25% rise in client commits.
Those late changes became particularly consequential after security researchers identified problems involving EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, which alter how Ethereum charges for certain operations.
The proposals could disrupt assumptions embedded in existing smart contracts, prompting developers to postpone Glamsterdam's Oct. 26 activation on the Hoodi testnet.
The setback has pushed Glamsterdam's expected interval between its first public testnet and mainnet activation beyond 100 days, compared with the 4- to 10-week window typical of previous upgrades, according to Wahrstätter.
During their Nov. 19 meeting, Ethereum developers tentatively targeted Dec. 16 or 17 for Hoodi testing, with mid-January 2027 emerging as the earliest possible mainnet date if the specification stays unchanged.
Wahrstätter argued that preventing further delays would require developers to base release targets on historical performance and set firm deadlines for dropping unfinished features and completing specifications before public testing begins.
He also questioned treating successful devnet deployments as evidence that proposals were sufficiently mature for inclusion in an upgrade. He said:
“I'm sure we can ship faster, but for that, we must ship smaller.”
The next decision comes Nov. 26, when Ethereum's core developers are expected to determine whether Glamsterdam can proceed with its proposed December Hoodi activation.
A further postponement would place additional pressure on a release schedule that has already extended well beyond its original target.
items.title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam delay reveals a troubling pattern behind its biggest network upgrades

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Hong Kong has published a bill to expand crypto licensing requirements to custody, advisory, dealing and management services under the SFC’s oversight. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since July amid a broader selloff in US stocks, while European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde warned that differing rules could fragment Europe’s tokenized securities markets.
Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules
Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration, extending oversight beyond trading platforms.
On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing to regulate four activities, including virtual asset dealing, advisory, management and custody. Firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from or register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).
The proposed amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance would subject providers to fit-and-proper checks and other regulatory requirements. Banks and stored-value facility licensees supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would also have to register with the SFC to offer virtual asset services.
SFC chief executive Julia Leung said the proposal would strengthen investor protections and provide clearer paths for responsible innovation. The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.
In October, Hong Kong said it would introduce legislation covering those four activities before the end of 2026, following consultations on the proposed framework.
The expanded regime has raised implementation concerns. In January, the Hong Kong Securities & Futures Professionals Association warned that introducing licenses without transitional arrangements could force existing businesses to suspend operations while their applications are reviewed. The association called for a six- to 12-month grace period.
Bitcoin falls below $60K for first time since July amid broader market selloff
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, extending its recent losses amid a broader selloff in technology stocks and other risk assets.
Bitcoin (BTC) had fallen as low as $58,811 before recovering slightly to trade around $59,503, down 5.6% over the past 24 hours as of 16:52 UTC on Friday, according to CoinGecko data. The cryptocurrency has fallen 13.8% over the past week and nearly 30% over the past month.
The decline came amid a broader selloff in US equities. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 5.28% at 22,617.73, while the S&P 500 fell 3.69% to 6,910.77 on Friday, according to Yahoo Finance.
Shares of Anthropic (ANT), which made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, closed down 8.50% at $88.91 amid concerns over valuations and spending in the artificial intelligence sector.
Lagarde warns Europe could miss chance to unify tokenized markets
European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde warned Friday that Europe needs common rules for tokenized securities before incompatible standards take hold across trading platforms.
Speaking at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress, Lagarde said blockchain technology lets firms issue, trade and settle securities on a single platform. The global markets for tokenized assets was worth about 23 billion euros in March, five times its size a year earlier, she said.
Europe could build a single market for those assets, Lagarde said, but if platforms adopt different rules as they grow, they may be unable to settle trades with one another. She said lawmakers have a role alongside the ECB.
“Common rules will be needed too, and those lie with legislators,” she said.
The Eurosystem launched Pontes in September, giving financial institutions a way to settle tokenized securities trades in central bank money. Earlier in November, the European Stability Mechanism used Pontes to settle a 1 billion euro (about $1.1 million) digital bond.
Through a second project, Appia, the Eurosystem is working with market participants on common standards for tokenized securities. It plans to publish a blueprint in 2028.

观点：美股45天蒸发6万亿美元并非AI泡沫破裂，2025年4月的抄底反攻或将重现

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，美股自 10 月 6 日创下历史高点以来，经历了长达 31 个交易日的连续下跌，日均蒸发约 2250 亿美元，累计损失高达 6 万亿美元市值。在此期间，宏观与产业利空交织：美国中期选举民主党大胜，令市场担忧激进的 AI 监管政策将落地；美联储在通胀高企背景下持续加息，大幅推高了 AI 基础设施建设的债务成本；同时英伟达创始人黄仁勋离职、AMD 遭做空机构指控走私芯片等黑天鹅事件，重创了半导体板块。此外 Anthropic 超千亿美元规模的史上最大 IPO，在短时间内抽干了市场的流动性，引发从股票、黄金到加密货币的全资产无差别抛售。

然而市场分析机构 The Kobeissi Letter 指出，这并非 AI 泡沫的破裂，而是一场对悲观预期定价过度的正常回调。数据显示尽管大型科技公司第三季度资本支出达到创纪录的 2019 亿美元，引发了对自由现金流的担忧，但标普 500 成分股第三季度每股收益（EPS）同比增长了 31.9%，创下至少四年来的最强增速，且实际盈利已连续 13 个季度超预期。当前科技股的远期市盈率已暴跌至 2020 年 3 月以来最低，英伟达的远期市盈率甚至降至 9 倍，表明市场对其高达 7500 亿美元的远期营收指引完全不予采信。

市场情绪目前已达危机级别，VIX 恐慌指数自 10 月低点翻倍，对冲基金科技股净流出创十年来新高。当前资产估值已计入了持续高利率、严厉监管、AI 投资回报不佳以及核心企业长期不确定性等多重最坏情况，反而为 2027 年预留了巨大的正向惊喜空间。虽然不排除短期内波动持续和进一步下探的可能，但风险收益比正变得极具吸引力。一旦市场流动性恢复，资金将迅速轮动回拥有强劲资产负债表和加速盈利增长的高质量科技股，重现类似 2025 年 4 月的抄底反攻。

items.content:
ECB seeks industry partners for tokenized deposits, securities experiments
Industry groups have until Dec. 11 to apply for the ECB’s first experimental exercises under its Appia initiative, with later submissions reviewed on a rolling basis.
The European Central Bank (ECB) is seeking financial market participants to help explore tokenized deposits and securities as part of its efforts to build an integrated European financial ecosystem using blockchain technology.
On Friday, the ECB invited industry groups to participate in analytical work and experiments under its Appia initiative, identifying three priority areas, including tokenized deposits and related payments, tokenized securities and shared network governance.
According to the ECB, interested participants must apply as part of a collective initiative comprising independent legal entities rather than individually. Groups can apply for one or more workstreams, with proposals evaluated based on factors including expertise, practical experience, technical readiness and expected contributions.
Applications for the first experimental exercises are due by Dec. 11, while later submissions will be assessed on a rolling basis.
The initiative builds on the Eurosystem’s broader Appia roadmap, which aims to develop a unified European tokenized financial ecosystem anchored in central bank money. The ECB plans to publish a blueprint outlining findings and a proposed framework in 2028.
The invitation comes as ECB President Christine Lagarde warned that Europe risks missing an opportunity to establish an integrated market for tokenized securities if incompatible standards emerge across platforms.
Lagarde urged policymakers to establish common rules to prevent fragmentation as blockchain-based financial infrastructure develops across the region.
Related: ECB warns legislative delays could postpone digital euro launch
items.title: ECB seeks industry partners for tokenized deposits, securities experiments

分析：BTC极端投降引发百亿美元亏损潮，七日已实现亏损113亿美元创本轮最高读数

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，CryptoQuant 分析师 Darkfost 指出，比特币创下 55,122 美元阶段新低后，市场正在经历极端的投降式抛售。随着价格急跌，盈亏比（7 日总和）已骤降至 0.12，创下本轮回调以来最低水平。11 月 20 日单日已实现亏损高达 29 亿美元，连续七个交易日的已实现亏损总额更是突破 113 亿美元，创下本轮熊市以来的最高读数之一。净已实现盈亏跌至约-23,800 枚 BTC，同样打破了今年 2 月的负值纪录。

在这场恐慌中，不同群体的受损情况引人注目。短期持有者（STH）承受了最大规模的抛压，实现亏损约 17,400 枚 BTC；而长期持有者（LTH）也遭遇了本轮熊市以来最沉重的一次打击，实现亏损约 10,300 枚 BTC。分析师强调，这正是极端投降的真实写照，许多缺乏耐心与信念的投资者正在离场，而这种剧烈波动正促使筹码完成从弱手向强手的转移。

items.author: Andjela Radmilac
items.content:
Quick Take
- Binance says it will decline withdrawals to MEXC and review incoming deposits.
- FinCEN's US transfer ban for covered institutions starts Dec. 10.
- How other exchanges handle MEXC transfers is still unconfirmed.
You can send crypto from MEXC to Binance, see that the transaction went through on the blockchain, and still be unable to trade with that deposit when you log in to Binance.
That's what Binance told customers to expect while it reviews deposits from MEXC. Try to move money the other way, and Binance says it'll refuse to send it in the first place.
The US order barring covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC takes effect Dec. 10, but Binance announced its policy a month earlier and cited the Treasury's finding.
MEXC can keep matching buy and sell orders in the markets it still serves, while one of the world's largest exchanges has already told traders it will restrict what they can move between the two.
The government went after the transfer
On Nov. 6, the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) found that MEXC was a foreign financial institution of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.
The agency acted under Section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, and its order in the Federal Register prohibits transfers to and from MEXC through covered US financial institutions.
The prohibition has no scheduled end and covers MEXC's foreign operations and successor entities. It reaches crypto as well as conventional money, and FinCEN names Bitcoin explicitly.
Foreign financial firms can make dollar payments through banks that hold accounts with US banks, an arrangement known as correspondent banking.
FinCEN considered restricting those accounts but concluded that doing so would leave other kinds of transfers untouched. Instead, it chose to prohibit transfers that pass through a covered institution, even when MEXC has no account with the institution handling the payment.
Exchanges and payment providers outside that group may adopt their own restrictions, but those policies require separate confirmation.
FinCEN estimates that MEXC handled at least $16.7 billion in likely illicit activity in the five years through May 2026. The agency's figures include about $129 million it says MEXC directly facilitated with Garantex after the Russian crypto exchange was sanctioned, and about $4.1 million involving its successor, Grinex, after it too was sanctioned.
FinCEN also cites transfers linked to Iran and North Korea, along with proceeds from cybercrime. The agency acknowledges that legitimate customers use MEXC and says the financial risks it identified warrant restricting transfers involving the exchange itself.
In its Nov. 7 public response, MEXC said it was operating normally, and customer assets remained secure. It said it had opened an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls and intended to engage with regulators.
Reports noted net outflows from tracked MEXC wallets after the announcement.
What happens when other exchanges stop moving MEXC money
Binance can refuse to send a withdrawal because it controls the account the money would leave.
Yet, when crypto comes from another platform, the network can process the transaction without asking the recipient's permission.
FinCEN acknowledges that limitation in the order, and Binance's notice shows what the exchange can do once the funds arrive: it can withhold credit while it reviews the transfer and potentially restrict or close the customer's Binance account.
Any funds left at MEXC stay in that account unless the customer moves them separately.
The business risk for exchanges becomes more serious if customers and professional market makers, the firms that keep buy and sell orders available, lose more ways to fund their accounts or move out the proceeds.
Moving balances between exchanges is part of how those firms keep money available where they need it.
MEXC says changes at third-party issuers ended its Asia-Pacific card program on Nov. 11 and its Global Card on Nov. 18.
Global Card customers can no longer use their cards for purchases. MEXC says it will credit balances left on the cards to customers' spot accounts within three business days of a Nov. 21 snapshot.
That would leave customers with an exchange balance rather than a working payment card, because spending it with a card requires an issuer.
In France, MEXC had announced its wind-down in October, before the Treasury acted. Its schedule for French accounts stopped euro deposits and withdrawals on Nov. 18, while crypto withdrawals remain available until March 5, 2027.
Trading restrictions begin in batches, and French accounts enter withdrawal-only mode on Jan. 25.
On Nov. 20, DefiLlama displayed more than $1 billion in MEXC spot trading over 24 hours. That figure measures trading across the platform, including customers outside France, and says little about whether an individual French account can accept deposits, place new orders, or withdraw its remaining funds.
After Dec. 10, the practical reach of FinCEN's order will depend partly on which banks and exchanges handle a trader's money and which restrictions those firms apply.
Binance has already told customers how it intends to handle MEXC transfers. Other firms may take different approaches, which traders will discover when they try to withdraw a balance, deposit it somewhere else, or spend it through a payment service.
items.title: Binance can hold MEXC deposits even after the blockchain clears them

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
US lawmakers propose up to 30% rewards for prediction market whistleblowers
Whistleblowers could receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases exceeding $1 million in penalties.
Two US lawmakers have proposed paying whistleblowers up to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases, seeking tips about suspected insider trading.
On Friday, Democratic Representatives Sean Casten and Ted Lieu announced the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026. The bill would establish a Department of Justice program rewarding people whose original information helps resolve enforcement actions.
Under the proposal, whistleblowers would receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions from covered federal fraud cases involving prediction market platforms, provided that the sanctions exceed $1 million. The rewards would come from the DOJ’s Assets Forfeiture Fund, with the Attorney General determining payouts based on the significance of information and assistance.
The bill would permit anonymous submissions through lawyers and prohibit employer retaliation against whistleblowers.
The lawmakers cited concerns about government insiders profiting from bets on military operations and presidential speeches, including on platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.
The latest proposal follows Senate passage of the DEATH BETS Act on Thursday, which would prohibit federally regulated prediction markets from offering contracts tied to war, assassination, terrorism and death.
In March, lawmakers introduced separate legislation to prevent officials from using nonpublic information to trade prediction market contracts. In May, House lawmakers sought records from Kalshi and Polymarket over suspected insider trading linked to military actions.
Related: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket investment: Reuters
items.title: US lawmakers propose up to 30% rewards for prediction market whistleblowers

⚡️分析：Tether非现金储备中黄金、比特币占比较高，若持续下跌USDT恐面临资不抵债

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，加密分析师 @fozzydiablo 近日援引 Tether 最新公开的 Q3 2026 储备报告（报告数据截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日）指出，Tether 非现金储备正经历价值重修，若黄金、比特币、美股等相关持续下跌，USDT 恐面临抵押不足状况。

储备报告显示，Tether 总资产 1914.5 亿美元，负债 1835 亿美元，超额缓冲仅 79.5 亿美元。其总资产中约 27%（520 亿美元）为非现金资产：黄金 191 亿美元、BTC 84 亿美元、股票 42 亿美元、担保贷款 142 亿美元。

分析指出，鉴于当前市场正经历价值重估，BTC 已跌超 30%、黄金跌约 15%，非现金资产市值显著缩水。仅黄金+BTC 的下跌就已消耗大部分缓冲。若再对贷款等资产施加约 15–20% 折扣，Tether 将接近陷入资不抵债状态。

这也解释了 S&P Global Ratings 为何在 11 月 18 日的报告中将 USDT 维持美元锚定能力的评分维持在 5 分（「weak」/弱），这是其 1-5 分稳定币稳定性评估量表中的最低档，与 2025 年 11 月的评估结果相同。

链上数据显示，Tether 近期正持续销毁 USDT，流通量近 20 天已下降约 50 亿美元。

字节进一步整合Seed与火山方舟：方舟团队更名Seed MaaS，吴迪同时掌管两大部门

动察 Beating AI 快讯，字节跳动再次调整 AI 组织架构。Seed 模型体系新设二级部门 Seed Model-MaaS Infra，原火山方舟团队更名为 Seed MaaS，两个部门均由吴迪负责。吴迪直接向 Seed 基础设施负责人项亮汇报，同时向火山引擎负责人谭待汇报业务。

此前，Seed 负责研发豆包等基础模型，火山方舟则负责把这些模型提供给企业调用，同时也提供 DeepSeek、智谱等第三方模型。两边虽然一直有合作，但分属不同业务体系。现在由吴迪同时负责，火山方舟可以更直接地把企业客户遇到的问题反馈给 Seed，让研发团队有针对性地改进模型。

字节今年已经连续调整 AI 架构。7 月，飞书与火山引擎整合企业销售体系，统一向企业销售 AI 产品和云服务。8 月，Seed 又重组预训练数据、强化学习和模型后训练团队。

火山方舟已经是字节收入规模最大的 AI 业务。今年上半年火山引擎 MaaS 业务收入达到 48 亿元，毛利率超过 55%。字节也从年中开始更加重视这项业务的实际收入，而不再只追求模型调用量。

Bitcoin Core披露节点消息处理漏洞，已发布修复版本

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，Bitcoin Core 披露一个可能暂时阻塞节点处理区块和交易的漏洞，编号为 CVE-2026-117348，严重程度被评为中等。

攻击者可先向节点发送缺少大量父交易的孤儿交易，再在单条消息中重复公告其交易标识 5 万次，使节点在十余秒内无法处理其他节点发来的消息。

该漏洞由 Spiral 的 Project Loupe 自动化大模型扫描发现。Bitcoin Core 30.5、31.3 和 32.1 版本已包含修复；受影响的 29.x 系列已停止维护，不再获得修复。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378532

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Variational says its $110 million Series B will help lift Omni’s trading limits and expand its swap markets.
- Omni’s in-house market maker takes the other side of every customer trade and can hedge separately with outside dealers.
- Omni’s rules allow a forced close when its market maker runs short of margin, even if the trader meets their margin requirement.
Variational raised $110 million and plans to use it to lift trading limits on Omni, its derivatives platform.
The company is recruiting more dealers as it expands into more stock, index, commodity, and currency markets. Omni traders will still rely on a single counterparty to pay their gains.
Bain Capital Crypto led the Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, Variational announced on Nov. 18. CEO Lucas Schuermann said in the company’s release that stocks, indexes and commodities already accounted for more than half of Omni’s daily volume.
Variational said that an unnamed tier-one market maker already supplies liquidity for swaps. It is seeking institutions that can quote equities, commodities and currencies around the clock.
The Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP) is Variational’s in-house market maker, which quotes a price and takes the other side when a customer trades. It can then hedge that exposure with a traditional dealer or on another venue.
More dealers can help OLP quote more markets and take on more exposure, but the customer still settles with OLP.
At 20:10 UTC on Nov. 20, Omni’s public market table showed $94.6 million in open interest on the Nasdaq-100 swap and $57.1 million on the gold swap.
Variational had set the initial caps at about $10 million per market when the two swaps launched in September. It said then it planned to lift each cap to $50 million or more. The company put potential capacity under its initial dealer agreements at more than $1 billion across the arrangements.
Under the standard schedule, both swaps trade from midnight to 5 p.m. and from 6 p.m. through 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on weekdays. They close on weekends, and holidays can change trading hours.
During a closure, orders and liquidations wait until the market reopens, while around-the-clock swap trading remains a goal.
Variational reported over $1.3 billion in Omni open interest with the round. Entropy Advisors’ on-chain dashboard shows a series that includes OLP alongside one that counts only traders’ positions. On its traditional-markets chart, OLP’s side equals the traders’ side.
Omni’s public API counts both sides in the platform total and counts only traders in its per-market long and short figures. The Series B release leaves its counting basis unspecified, so lining it up with the dashboard would require matching the series and the observation time.
When the market maker runs short of margin
Each Omni trader and OLP post collateral to a separate on-chain settlement pool for that pair, and a vault holds USDC to supply OLP’s margin.
OLP uses its own capital when hedging outside the platform, leaving customers’ collateral in their pools.
If OLP cannot safely maintain margin in an extremely volatile market or needs to free up margin during a severe liquidity squeeze, its counterparty liquidation rules allow a forced close. The position closes for both sides at the settlement price even if the trader has kept up their own margin.
Variational says customers’ posted collateral stays in the protocol if an outside venue loses OLP’s funds. If OLP itself becomes insolvent, gains that accrue from then on can go unpaid, including gains a trader has realized on Omni.
items.title: Variational’s $1.5 billion trading business has a catch even profitable traders cannot escape

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules
Hong Kong’s securities regulator says the proposal would strengthen investor protections, with the bill set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.
Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration, extending oversight beyond trading platforms.
On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing to regulate four activities, including virtual asset dealing, advisory, management and custody. Firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from or register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).
The proposed amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance would subject providers to fit-and-proper checks and other regulatory requirements. Banks and stored-value facility licensees supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would also have to register with the SFC to offer virtual asset services.
SFC chief executive Julia Leung said the proposal would strengthen investor protections and provide clearer paths for responsible innovation. The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.
In October, Hong Kong said it would introduce legislation covering those four activities before the end of 2026, following consultations on the proposed framework.
The expanded regime has raised implementation concerns. In January, the Hong Kong Securities & Futures Professionals Association warned that introducing licenses without transitional arrangements could force existing businesses to suspend operations while their applications are reviewed. The association called for a six- to 12-month grace period.
Related: Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms
items.title: Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules

⚡️社区激辩加密牛市为何「迟到」，AI泡沫破裂、流动性紧缩或为主因

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，比特币今日午间跌破 5.6 万美元，加密社区中「四年周期规律」遭遇前所未有的信仰动摇。对此社区激辩本轮加密牛市为何「迟到」，BlockBeats 整理主流观点如下。

包括 KobeissiLetter 联创在内的多位分析师指出，AI 泡沫破裂是加密 10 月以来暴跌首因，分析师称当前美股 AI 股票出现多个类似 2008 年金融危机的迹象，包括杠杆过高、信贷收紧、流动性开始消失，警告可能不止于股市，银行系统信心也可能受影响。这一论断在美股周五暴跌后迅速传播并得到广泛认可，由此传导至加密市场，导致周五、周六的大幅调整。

第二，供需角度来讲，加密 ETF 正在由买方转为卖方，近期持续资金流出，Strategy 因股价低于持仓 BTC 价值而无法继续买，这些都导致加密供需情况正在恶化。同期，稳定币流通量持续减少导致整体流动性抽离也是加密流动性紧张的一大旁证。

最后，美联储再加息预期、美国中期选举后政局动荡、美伊冲突不确定性等宏观因素也严重影响了投资者对于加密投资的信心。

items.content:
GMGN联创Haze：加密市场当前或是周期投资者寻找超额收益的时刻

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，GMGN 联合创始人 Haze 在 X 平台发文表示，加密市场再次进入「死亡状态」。自 2017 年进入加密市场以来，自己已经历过多轮类似的悲观情绪周期，每次市场下跌都会出现「加密市场已经完了」的论调，并试图为价格下跌寻找原因，但没有任何主流资产会永远上涨或下跌。

所谓的「死亡状态」恰恰是周期投资者以及希望通过二级市场获取超额收益者的重要时刻。当资产价格足够便宜时买入，等待市场上涨；当市场开始普遍讨论资产为何上涨，且不再关注价格时卖出。投资者不一定能买在最低点或卖在最高点，但仍有机会从市场周期中获利。

其同时强调，以上并非针对特定资产的投资建议，而是其长期以来对市场周期的观察。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Spark showed $60,484 available for immediate stUSDS withdrawals on Nov. 20, about 0.04% of vault assets.
- Borrower repayments and new USDS deposits can give stUSDS holders more liquidity to redeem their shares.
- Sky Frontier Foundation said users swapped more than $2 billion of USDS for USDC through a separate facility on Nov. 19.
Sky’s stUSDS lending vault had $60,484 worth of USDS available for immediate withdrawals at 17:50 UTC on Nov. 20, about 0.04% of the vault’s $161.6 million in total assets, according to Spark.
Spark’s dashboard showed about $161.5 million in USDS out on loan at the time, and those loans account for nearly all of the vault’s reported value.
A holder could redeem only from the portion available in USDS. For example, a saver with $100,000 worth of stUSDS could not have redeemed that entire position directly at the time of the reading, even if nobody else withdrew first.
Savers deposit USDS and receive stUSDS tokens representing their position, and the pool lends USDS to borrowers who put up SKY tokens as collateral. Spark’s dashboard displayed a 29.74% annual percentage yield at the time.
Sky explains that the yield varies with lending conditions. Funds in use earn a rate tied to what borrowers pay, and unused USDS earns the Sky Savings Rate.
What frees up USDS for withdrawals in Sky
When borrowers repay, the USDS they return can become available for withdrawals. New deposits can also add USDS to the pool before borrowers pay down their loans.
When nearly all of the pool is already lent out, a holder may have to wait for more USDS to come in before redeeming their full position.
Sky says the module has no mechanism to liquidate borrowers early to free up funds for depositors. The loan collateral is in SKY, while holders redeem their stUSDS shares for USDS available in the vault.
Sky Frontier Foundation separately said on Nov. 20 that users exchanged more than $2 billion of USDS for USDC the previous day through Sky’s Peg Stability Module. The foundation said the facility continued to swap the two stablecoins at a one-to-one rate during the Nov. 19 activity.
The swap facility serves users who already have USDS to exchange. An stUSDS holder using the vault would first have to redeem for USDS before using that route to get USDC.
The amount a vault depositor can withdraw depends on how much USDS is in the lending pool when the redemption is attempted.
items.title: Sky offers nearly 30% yield but 99.96% of its lending vault is unavailable for immediate withdrawals

Arthur Hayes: Why Is Bitcoin Sold First When Markets Turn Risk-Off?

On November 17, 2026, Maelstrom CIO Arthur Hayes said on the New Era Finance podcast that Bitcoin and crypto remain risk assets. Because crypto markets operate around the clock, investors facing losses elsewhere often sell their readily accessible crypto holdings first to meet margin calls or repay bank loans. This leaves Bitcoin exposed to selling during global risk-off events, particularly when stress is concentrated in technology stocks. Even if investors expect eventual bailouts to drive prices higher, they may still need cash now to avoid liquidation in less liquid positions.

WuBlockchain notes that Arthur Hayes has a mixed track record of market predictions and frequently revises his views. Readers should focus on his analytical framework rather than treating specific price targets or timelines as investment guidance. — link

Gemini 4 Neon写代码被夸，Antigravity却狂烧Token：谷歌承认缓存问题，承诺重置额度

动察 Beating AI 快讯，谷歌的 Gemini 4 Neon 编程能力获得不少开发者好评，配套编程工具 Antigravity 却因 Token 消耗异常遭到集中投诉。

11 月 21 日凌晨，Antigravity 负责人 Varun Mohan 承认，Neon 的缓存命中率偏低，尤其是模型两次调用间隔较长时，缓存容易被清除。谷歌正在大幅扩大缓存池，预计将命中率提高约 4%，让用户在相同配额内至少多完成 20% 的工作。完成后还将重置用户额度。

编程智能体每次调用模型时，都需要让模型获得此前的对话、代码和工具执行结果。缓存能让模型直接复用已经处理过的内容，不必重复计算。一旦缓存失效，几十万 Token 的历史内容就可能被重新处理，导致额度消耗大幅增加。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378507

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
Thinking Machines发布Inkling 2 Mini：264亿参数，跑分追平Qwen3.8-27B

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Thinking Machines 刚开源的 Inkling 2 Small 有 5940 亿参数，运行至少需要 500GB 显存。不少开发者嫌它太大，Thinking Machines 于是推出更小的 Inkling 2 Mini，总参数降至 264 亿，每次生成 Token 激活 34 亿个不同参数，终于能在普通笔记本上运行。

Mini 采用和 GPT-6 Astra 一样的循环 Transformer 架构。模型只有 24 层网络，但中间 12 层会重复运行 3 次。相当于每生成一个 Token，都要经过 48 层计算，却只需要存储 24 层的权重。通过重复使用同一组参数，让模型不用继续扩大体积，也能进行更复杂的推理。

Artificial Analysis 综合评分达到 20.1 分，与 Qwen3.8-27B 持平，但单项评测成本约为后者的六分之一，耗时约为四分之一。Thinking Machines 公布的测试结果显示，DeepSWE v1.1 编程任务通过率达到 48.2%，超过 Qwen 的 42.2%；但在 AutomationBench-AA 办公自动化任务测试中，得分为 41.8%，仍低于 Qwen 的 48.2%。

循环架构也带来一个问题：模型可以在内部完成更多推理，不必把每一步思考都写出来，外界可能更难检查它的推理过程。Thinking Machines 专门训练了一个可以调整循环次数的研究模型。实验发现，循环次数越多，模型不依赖文字推理就能完成的任务越复杂，但暂时没有发现思维链的可监控性明显下降。

Inkling 2 Mini 已开放完整权重，采用 Apache 2.0 许可证。官方版本约占 20GB，可在 32GB 内存的 Mac 上离线运行。Unsloth 也推出了低比特量化版本，16GB 内存设备就能运行。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378504

items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[cjboco]: You can opt out of most of everything here. Sure, it appears to be a dark pattern opt out process. Sucks, been using these guys for years, hate to see them go this route.  https://preferences.backblaze.com/

[olalonde]: I know it sucks but it's worth pointing out that Backblaze explicitly distinguishes personal information from the files customers upload. Their CCPA FAQ[0] says that uploaded files are not included in the definition of personal information and that they do not sell or share those files. [0]  https://help.backblaze.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040703654-Ca...

[munch-o-man]: good thing all my data with this is encrypted from my end haha.  Also, just gonna pimp out  https://github.com/afreidah/s3-orchestrator  shamelessly here...if you put it between your clients and the backend it is easy to have your data in multiple places and a cloud migration is as simple as having your clients make requests to b2 through s3-orchestrator, add your new backend you want to migrate to in the config and set the replication-factor to 2, your clients keep writin...

[throwaway_ab]: Is the data the info about your account and computer environment details? (Location, name, os, apps running on your computer, etc...) Or is it actually the data you are backing up? Are they reading your files to mine for data to sell? Or both? I think selling any of this data, account, environment, actual files, all of this is abhorrent.

[freeli]: Also note: at least on MacOS, the Backblaze backup install process creates a world-readable directory that contains a world-readable file that lists ALL files to be backed up across all users. This is a security issue if you have a multi-user setup and you don't want your filenames leaked across users. Any user on the system can read this file list. Backblaze was uninterested in discussing this issue.

CertiK与哥伦比亚大学研究人员发布TensorLean，全球首次完成DeepSeek与FlashAttention生产级AI算子形式化验证

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，CertiK 公布了与哥伦比亚大学研究人员共同取得的 TensorLean 技术成果，完成全球首次生产级 AI 算子形式化验证。这项突破让数学证明能够用于经过复杂性能优化的真实 AI 计算代码，为大模型厂商在提高训练速度、降低推理成本时，提供更严格的正确性保证。

研究团队对 149 个已编译的 GPU 内核实例进行了评估，并通过形式化证明验证了其中 83 个符合相应的 Lean 规格。此次研究覆盖不同代际的 GPU 架构，并涉及 DeepSeek 的 DeepGEMM 和广泛使用的 FlashAttention 算子库。团队共在 6 个库中发现 38 个正确性问题，其中 DeepGEMM 有 2 个，FlashAttention 有 23 个。

这项研究成果为形式化验证在真实 AI 计算中的应用提供了实例。随着大模型持续进行性能优化和硬件适配，底层代码也需要不断调整。TensorLean 可支持开发者在代码更新后重复验证正确性，帮助降低计算错误、训练返工及算力浪费的风险。

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，中国国家安全部公众号发文指出，当前侵犯公民个人信息犯罪正呈现链条升级、手段翻新、流向复杂等新特征，数据流转跨境化趋势明显。具体而言，境外「社工库」提供查询，境外服务器存放数据，并利用虚拟货币结算资金，导致大量公民个人信息被违规转移出境，既为跨境违法犯罪输送「弹药」，也对我国数据安全构成现实威胁。

文章还指出，相关黑灰产链条已由个体零散作案转向流水线式协同作案，窃取手段趋于自动化、批量化，并衍生出信息查询、非法跟踪、「开盒」滋扰等服务。个人财产信息外泄还会催生精准电信网络诈骗、敲诈勒索等下游犯罪。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Fluidkey says it restored its web, iOS and Android apps and requires version 1.79.22 before users can send funds.
- Bitquery traced at least $1.6 million to incident-linked wallets across six chains and identified a likely user withdrawal.
- Users can check transfers and balances at known addresses while Fluidkey prepares to contact affected users individually.
Fluidkey said it restored its privacy wallet on Nov. 20, a day after taking it offline following unauthorized transfers.
Sending funds requires an app update, and users who spot an unfamiliar transfer can look up their own receiving address or transaction hash on the relevant blockchain.
The company announced the return of its web, iOS, and Android apps in v1.79.22. It said older versions would stay offline and told users to open Settings and select Update to re-enable transactions.
Fluidkey attributed the incident to flaws in a third-party logging tool and said users’ private keys stayed on their devices, and said it took services offline on Nov. 19. In its update that evening, it said it had seen no further unauthorized transactions since the shutdown and was working with SEAL 911 to investigate and trace funds.
Its initial warning to avoid the site and app came before the new version was available.
Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery traced roughly $1.6 million in payouts to wallets it linked to the incident across six chains, including Base and Ethereum.
The independent Fluidkey drain tracker, maintained by pepebndc, put the total near $1.63 million across seven chains in its Nov. 20 morning snapshot. That estimate includes suspected destinations and excludes likely owner withdrawals.
Bitquery says the tracker labeled one Polygon payout as an owner withdrawal, linking it to the incident after following the recipient’s activity on Base.
The firm also separated the incident-linked payments from about $349,000 sent to wallets with an established history during its hour-long scan.
That group includes ordinary payments before the drain and about $277,000 sent during it to an older wallet across Ethereum and Base. Bitquery interpreted the latter as one user moving their own funds, and left another $65,000 unclassified.
What FluidKey users can check now
If you have a receiving address or transaction hash, look it up in a block explorer for the relevant chain. The ethereum.org guide to block explorers explains how those records are organized.
Compare the time, amount, and destination with your own records and check the balance at your known address. The chain records the transfer, but the record alone cannot establish who authorized it.
Fluidkey’s standing recovery guide describes SARA as a last-resort option for verifying addresses or accessing funds. It warns that moving funds outside the regular app may impair app functionality.
In its incident update, Fluidkey said it would contact affected users individually and publish a full post-mortem. It warned about impersonation and said its staff would never contact users privately through social media, and directed users to its official website for support.
items.title: Fluidkey’s $1.6 million hack exposes a security risk even when private keys never leave users’ devices

⚡️美股恐慌情绪再度升温，UVIX昨日涨超27%，溢价率高达57.47%

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 21 日，伴随 Anthropic IPO 后持续回落和 AI 交易降温，美股恐慌情绪再度升温，2 倍做多 VIX 短期期货 ETF UVIX 昨日暴涨 27.61%，报收 72.79 点。

注：VIX 指标普 500 隐含波动率，俗称恐慌指数；越高说明市场越恐慌、预期波动越大。UVIX 则是跟踪一篮子 VIX 短期期货，目标是提供这类指数单日约 2 倍的涨跌幅。

需要指出的是，目前 UVIX 溢价率已达 57.47%，现价 72.79 远高于单位净值 46.224。这不是正常状态，说明二级市场价格被投机和供需推高，追高风险很大；也可能伴随申购受限、流动性问题。

Anthropic数学家宣称证明「数学界第一神山」黎曼猜想，市场质疑其「利好」发布动机

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 发布声明，称自己与 AI 模型 Claude 合作，找到了黎曼猜想及广义黎曼猜想（GRH）的证明方法，并同步公布超过 1700 万行 Lean 形式化代码。由于声明发布恰逢 Anthropic 上市次日，这项数学突破也引发了外界对发布时间及商业动机的讨论。

Alpöge 将证明以 Lean 语言写成，分为 14 个压缩文件发布。与此同时，他与 Claude 生成的文字版证明超过 25 万页，但因篇幅过长、难以阅读而没有公开。

对此，2006 年菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩在个人博客发文称，初步分析显示，这份证明似乎综合运用了朗兰兹纲领和算术几何领域的现代研究成果，验证工作预计还需要一段时间。

Investigation: Only $32M Recovered Three Weeks After $6.4B Binance Hack, $2.82B Frozen

According to blockchain investigator SomaXBT, three weeks after the $6.4 billion Binance hack, approximately $2.82 billion has been frozen, $2.67 billion remains under attacker control, and only $32 million has been recovered. The attackers still hold 18,270 BTC stolen directly from Binance, which remains untouched. Over 5,100 BTC has been transferred through THORChain, while 1,482 BTC has entered CoinJoin mixing, primarily via the kruw coordinator. The FBI previously attributed the attack to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor. — link

⚡️USDT兑USDC比价出现轻微折价，本周标普曾对USDT锚定能力给予警告

【CertiK 与哥伦比亚大学研究人员发布 TensorLean，完成生产级 AI 算子形式化验证】

Foresight News 消息，CertiK 公布了与哥伦比亚大学研究人员共同取得的 TensorLean 技术成果，完成生产级 AI 算子形式化验证。这项突破让数学证明能够用于经过复杂性能优化的真实 AI 计算代码，为大模型厂商在提高训练速度、降低推理成本时，提供更严格的正确性保证。研究团队对 149 个已编译的 GPU 内核实例进行了评估，并通过形式化证明验证了其中 83 个符合相应的 Lean 规格。此次研究覆盖不同代际的 GPU 架构，并涉及 DeepSeek 的 DeepGEMM 和广泛使用的 FlashAttention 算子库。团队共在 6 个库中发现 38 个正确性问题，其中 DeepGEMM 有 2 个，FlashAttention 有 23 个。这项研究成果为形式化验证在真实 AI 计算中的应用提供了实例。随着大模型持续进行性能优化和硬件适配，底层代码也需要不断调整。TensorLean 可支持开发者在代码更新后重复验证正确性，帮助降低计算错误、训练返工及算力浪费的风险。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- DBS and Circle announced a direct channel for eligible institutions in Asia to mint and redeem USDC through the bank.
- The partners describe USDC settlement through DBS as near-instant and available around the clock for minting and redemption.
- The releases gave no client start date, detailed eligibility rules, fees or transaction limits for the bank route.
DBS and Circle announced a partnership on Nov. 18 to let eligible institutions in Asia turn USDC back into US dollars directly through DBS.
For treasury teams that hold the stablecoin, the bank route would offer an alternative to selling it on an exchange or elsewhere in the secondary market.
The partners described near-instant, round-the-clock settlement when clients mint or redeem USDC through DBS. The announcements describe the conversion itself and give no timetable for when clients could use the resulting dollars for other payments.
How USDC redemption through DBS would work
Under the arrangement announced by DBS, an eligible institution could request dollars for its USDC through the bank. A treasury team could choose between the two routes based on the transaction it needs to make and the terms available.
The arrangement would also let eligible clients use dollars to mint, or obtain newly issued, USDC through DBS.
DBS had announced a separate service with Kinexys by JPMorgan on Nov. 16, connecting tokenized dollar deposit accounts in Singapore and the US so institutions can move dollars between them.
The Circle partnership adds a way for eligible clients to convert between dollars and a stablecoin.
DBS and Circle said the partnership builds on their participation in Project BLOOM, an initiative led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. Its work includes helping different forms of tokenized money operate across financial networks.
The companies gave no market-by-market rollout or detailed eligibility rules, and they also left the onboarding process, supported blockchains, fees, and transaction limits unspecified.
The round-the-clock settlement the companies described would address one part of an after-hours conversion.
To decide whether to use the route for a payment or other treasury need, an institution would still need to know whether its account qualifies, what size redemption DBS will handle, and what the transaction will cost.
items.title: DBS is building two paths for 24/7 dollars with JPMorgan and Circle using USDC

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Binance’s annualized RLUSD base rate rose from 4.48% to 6.37% for the seven days through Nov. 20.
- A constant 10,000 RLUSD balance would have earned about 54% more XRP in the final week than the week before at base rates.
- The renewed 600,000 XRP pool gives holders a reason to keep RLUSD on Binance, while reward funding remains undisclosed in its notices.
Binance’s base reward rate for holding Ripple USD (RLUSD) rose from 4.48% to an annualized 6.37% for the seven days through Nov. 20.
At a steady qualifying balance of 10,000 RLUSD, the estimated weekly payout rose from 8.25 XRP to 12.72 XRP as the exchange also used a lower price to convert the reward into XRP.
A separate 600,000 XRP rewards campaign began at 00:00 UTC on Nov. 20. The new round runs through Dec. 18 and gives eligible customers a reason to keep more RLUSD on Binance.
How Binance calculates the reward
Binance’s distribution table shows base APRs of 4.84% on Oct. 30 and 5.29% on Nov. 6, with XRP conversion references of $1.2379 and $1.2072 for those payouts. The base rate fell to 4.48% on Nov. 13, with a $1.0413 reference, before climbing to 6.37% on Nov. 20 as the reference dropped to $0.9603.
On a constant qualifying balance of 10,000 RLUSD, Binance’s seven-day formula estimates rewards of $9.28, $10.15, $8.59, and $12.22 across the four weeks before conversion.
Dividing by each week’s reference and rounding down to two decimal places gives 7.49, 8.40, 8.25 and 12.72 XRP.
Each column is the annualized base APR Binance reported for the seven days ending on that distribution date, excluding reward multipliers.
The estimated payout rose about 54% in XRP from the third week to the fourth. The higher base rate increased the dollar value under the formula, and the lower conversion price turned each dollar of reward into more XRP.
Users qualify through net RLUSD balances in eligible Spot, Funding, Flexible Earn, or Margin accounts. For each day, Binance uses the lowest balance it finds in hourly snapshots, then averages those daily lows over seven days.
Eligible participants generally receive XRP in their main Spot account. The formula rewards maintaining a balance through the week because a low reading counts for the entire day.
The renewal also applies a 1.1x boost to eligible RLUSD in Flexible Earn and 1.2x to qualifying balance increases above a baseline from the prior two weeks. The portion that meets both tests can earn 1.3 times the base reward.
What would show lasting demand
Funding records and any trades used to source the rewards could establish whether the program led to a fresh market purchase. Once the tokens were credited, recipient balances, trades, and withdrawals could show how much of the reward stayed on Binance.
To see whether the RLUSD balances lasted, the comparable figures would be qualifying holdings before, during, and after a rate change.
In a separate measure, XRPLDashboard’s signed snapshots show RLUSD outstanding on the XRP Ledger rose by 31.4 million, from about 714.4 million to 745.8 million, in the 24 hours through 02:00 UTC on Nov. 20.
The snapshots measure net issuance across the ledger and provide no breakdown of flows to Binance or the balances that qualified for rewards.
The new campaign’s first distribution is scheduled for Nov. 27, and the exchange plans to post the effective rate after that distribution. Aggregate payout and balance figures would show how much of the pool Binance used and how much RLUSD qualified for rewards.
Ripple USD is -0.01% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #25 by market cap.

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin’s dollar hashprice fell about 6% between the Nov. 16 and Nov. 20 readings of Luxor’s index.
- With half the blocks mined, MineOrNot estimated a difficulty increase that would reverse about 84% of the Nov. 14 cut.
- An 8.47% difficulty rise would lower the electricity rate that mining revenue can cover if Bitcoin’s price and block rewards hold steady.
Bitcoin miners’ expected dollar revenue for the same computing power fell about 6% from Nov. 16 to Nov. 20 in two readings of Luxor’s revenue index.
A difficulty cut had lifted expected Bitcoin earnings earlier in the month, but with the next adjustment now tracking higher, less efficient machines could soon need cheaper electricity to cover their power bills.
Simple Mining’s Nov. 20 reading of Luxor’s hash price index put gross mining revenue at $28.58 per petahash per second (PH/s) per day, with Luxor’s Nov. 16 roundup listing $30.45.
To estimate a machine’s gross daily revenue, multiply the hash price by the machine’s computing power in PH/s. One PH/s equals 1,000 terahashes per second.
The slide also appeared in CloudMineCrypto’s daily series, which estimates revenue from Bitcoin blocks. In its partial Nov. 20 reading, dollar hash price had fallen to about $28.90 from $30.30 per PH/s per day on Nov. 16, while the coin rate held near 0.00047 BTC.
The paired readings explain why a miner can earn roughly the same amount of Bitcoin for a day of work and still have fewer dollars to pay an electricity bill.
Bitcoin’s Nov. 14 adjustment lowered difficulty by 9.13%, from 148.36 trillion to 134.82 trillion. Holding the reward per block steady, the same amount of work could then earn about 10% more Bitcoin. Luxor’s Nov. 16 roundup found that the BTC hash price had risen from 0.00042763 a week earlier to 0.00046839 BTC per PH/s per day.
Over the same period, the dollar hash price fell from $31.95 to $30.45.
The expected coin payout depends on the block subsidy, transaction fees, and how hard it is to find a block. The dollar payout also depends on Bitcoin’s price, since fees accounted for only a small fraction of block rewards in both data sets.
Luxor reported a weekly average of 0.0229 BTC in fees per block on Nov. 16, and the partial Nov. 20 data imply about 0.022 BTC in fees on top of the 3.125 BTC subsidy.
How much Bitcoin miners can afford to pay for power
As of Nov. 20, MineOrNot counted 1,008 blocks, halfway to the next adjustment. Blocks were arriving about every nine minutes and 14 seconds, compared with Bitcoin’s ten-minute target.
If that pace persists, MineOrNot estimated difficulty would rise 8.47% to about 146.24 trillion around Nov. 27.
If Bitcoin’s price, the subsidy, and average fees per block stay fixed, an 8.47% rise in difficulty would lower the $28.58 benchmark to about $26.35 per PH/s per day. A 10% increase would put it near $25.98 and bring difficulty almost back to its pre-cut level.
For a machine using 30 joules per terahash, the observed benchmark translates to a power-only break-even rate of 3.97 cents per kilowatt-hour.
With an 8.47% increase in difficulty, the same machine’s ceiling would fall to 3.66 cents. A machine using 13.5 joules per terahash can absorb higher electricity rates, with its ceiling falling from 8.82 cents to 8.13 cents under the same assumptions.
At a hypothetical electricity rate of 3.8 cents per kWh, the less efficient machine would just cover its power bill at the Nov. 20 benchmark. At that same rate, it would fall short after an 8.47% increase in difficulty. The more efficient machine would cover electricity at that rate in both cases.
The calculation divides gross daily revenue by daily electricity use. A miner at the ceiling has already used all its expected revenue on electricity. Pool fees and any separate hosting charges can lower the rate it can afford, and the operator’s contract and downtime will shape its actual costs.
items.title: Bitcoin miners face a new profitability cliff as difficulty heads for an 8.5% jump
