items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin fell to a four-month low of $61,196 as $819.57 million in liquidations swept derivatives markets, affecting more than 170,000 traders.
- Bullish bets accounted for nearly 87% of liquidations, while rising volatility and $3.47 billion in November ETF outflows intensified selling pressure.
- With $12.7 billion in short-side exposure above Bitcoin, traders face a potential short squeeze if prices rebound or deeper losses if $61,250 fails.
Bitcoin fell to its lowest level in four months as an $820 million liquidation wave swept the derivatives market. The leading cryptocurrency fell to $61,196 on Nov. 20 before recovering to $61,901 as of press time, according to CryptoSlate data.
This price performance extended a sell-off that has repeatedly punished traders betting on a market recovery. Data from CoinGlass showed that 170,824 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, with total liquidations reaching $819.57 million.
CoinGlass rolling-window snapshot provided Nov. 20, 2026. Each bar combines long and short liquidated positions in its stated period. The 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h windows overlap; do not sum bars. The screenshot reports 170,824 traders liquidated during 24h. Exact capture time is not visible, and subsequent live dashboard values differ.
Bullish positions accounted for $712.33 million, or nearly 87% of the total, while short liquidations reached $107.24 million.
Bitcoin accounted for $221.86 million in liquidations, followed by Ethereum at $122.49 million. The selling extended to derivatives tied to traditional assets, including gold, which recorded $62.53 million in liquidations.
Percentage of each displayed heatmap category's liquidated position value attributable to longs in the supplied CoinGlass 24h snapshot. Only four categories had readable long-share labels. Figures are rounded to one decimal place as printed in the screenshot; categories without readable percentages are omitted.
The largest individual liquidation occurred on Bybit, where a BTCUSD position worth $9.26 million was forcibly closed.
The market turmoil has also triggered a sharp increase in expected volatility.
Block Scholes' 30-day Bitcoin Implied Volatility Index (BSIV) climbed to 51.6%, up 8.4 percentage points over the past week. Ethereum's equivalent reading reached 66.4%, while Solana's rose to 77.7%, reflecting growing expectations of sharp price swings across major cryptocurrencies.
Meanwhile, Bitcoin's 30-day at-the-money implied volatility reached 45.8%, its highest level since June, as options traders repriced risk after the latest downturn.
Block Scholes BSIV, 30-day constant maturity. Historical observations are approximate values digitized from the supplied chart (usually rounded to 0.5 percentage point), sampled every three days plus notable peaks and troughs. Selected dates are replaced with explicitly reported Block Scholes readings; November 20 endpoints are 51.6%, 66.4% and 77.7% for BTC, ETH and SOL. Full underlying daily export was unavailable. Not realized volatility.
Notably, the pressure has also extended beyond derivatives markets.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded another $582.3 million in net outflows Thursday, bringing November's cumulative withdrawals to approximately $3.47 billion.
These continued ETF withdrawals have weakened a major source of Bitcoin demand at a time when leveraged traders are also being forced to reduce exposure.
Tightening liquidity spreads selling pressure across financial markets
Bitcoin's latest decline has coincided with broader weakness in financial markets, as investors have sold technology stocks and traditional safe-haven assets.
Gold has declined for five consecutive sessions, according to Bitunix, with weekly losses potentially exceeding 9%.
The exchange's analysts attributed the simultaneous weakness in Bitcoin and gold to persistent inflation, elevated borrowing costs, and increasing demand for cash as investors reduce leverage.
The selling has also affected the artificial intelligence sector despite Anthropic's successful stock market debut.
André Dragosch, Bitwise Europe's head of research, said the AI company's heavily oversubscribed initial public offering should not be interpreted as a recovery signal for risk assets.
He argued that monetary tightening and intensifying competition among AI companies remain significant headwinds, while large capital raises could absorb liquidity that might otherwise flow into other markets.
Dragosch warned that a potential 50-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December could intensify short-term pressure on financial markets.
However, he suggested that monetary tightening could be approaching its peak, pointing to changes in bond yields and market expectations as signs that investors are beginning to anticipate an eventual policy shift.
He identified Bitcoin as a potential early indicator of changing liquidity conditions, given its sensitivity to monetary policy and investors' risk appetite.
Bitcoin's $12.7 billion short buildup puts $60,000 support in focus
Against that backdrop, Bitcoin's derivatives market is showing signs of a significant shift in positioning, with leveraged bullish bets being cleared while bearish exposure accumulates above prevailing prices.
James Lavish, co-managing partner of Bitcoin Opportunity Fund, said the sustained decline had effectively wiped out accumulated monthly leveraged long exposure.
He wrote:
“Literally every single ounce of monthly leveraged longs in bitcoin has been blown out, and $12.7 billion of leveraged shorts are now stacked above.”
The buildup raises the possibility of a sharp reversal if Bitcoin recovers, as rising prices could force bearish traders to close their positions and accelerate buying pressure.
However, the immediate market structure still favors sellers.
Analysts at Bitunix said Bitcoin's open interest declined 2.7%, indicating traders continued to reduce leveraged exposure. Both spot and futures cumulative volume delta (CVD), a measure of buying and selling activity, showed net selling, with aggressive sell orders accounting for approximately 51% of trading activity.
The exchange's analysts also identified concentrated bearish positioning on Hyperliquid, where the Super Printing Machine trading group reportedly holds $778 million in Bitcoin short positions against $94.03 million in longs.
The imbalance creates additional short-squeeze potential if prices recover, although weaker spot demand and declining open interest suggest that buying pressure has yet to return convincingly.
For now, Bitunix identified buying interest between $61,250 and $61,400, with another demand zone around $60,550 to $60,600.
This means a sustained break below $61,250 could expose Bitcoin to further declines toward $60,000. Conversely, a recovery above $62,265 to $62,720, accompanied by improving buying activity, could begin to put pressure on accumulated bearish positions.
items.title: Bitcoin hits four-month low as $820 million liquidated and $12.7 billion short squeeze risk builds

items.author: Cointelegraph by Adrian Zmudzinski
items.content:
DBS bets it can lose the deposit and keep the client
The Singapore bank earned a record $208 million in transaction services fees in the third quarter — now it’s helping companies turn deposits into stablecoins they can spend without it.
If a supplier wants USDC on a Sunday, an eligible company can now get Circle’s stablecoin directly from DBS.
That gives the bank a conversion option its client might otherwise take to a crypto exchange. If the treasurer needs to move dollars between the company’s Singapore and US accounts that weekend, DBS can also handle that through its new tokenized deposit link with JPMorgan.
Once the company holds USDC, its treasurer can pay the next invoice without involving DBS. For shareholders, the payoff depends on how often that treasurer comes back, what DBS earns when the money moves and how much operating cash the company leaves on deposit.
Related: Binance hacker moves nearly $600M in ETH, routes funds through THORChain, Chainflip
The Monetary Authority of Singapore issued 100 million Singapore dollars ($77.6 million) of four-week bills on Nov. 6, and the dealers paid in wholesale Singapore dollar central bank digital currency. Here DBS participated as a securities dealer. MAS plans to expand trials in 2027 to explore how institutions could use the bills as collateral.
DBS’s quarterly results put a figure on the business it has to defend. Transaction services generated a record 268 million Singapore dollars in fees in the third quarter, up 8% from a year earlier, before either November deal.

XMR1被盗约1300万美元因托管商遭入侵，已删除服务器仍留存部署密钥

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，XMR1 相关人士、Wagyu 核心成员 PerpetualCow 发布复盘称，此次约 1300 万美元被盗事件比此前预想更严重。其表示，项目所用托管商 1984. hosting 当天遭遇入侵，客户数据及内部服务器文件均被获取。XMR1 的部署密钥存放在一台他已删除的旧服务器上，但日志和文件仍被保留，攻击者据此取得密钥。他提醒，部分托管商在用户删除服务器后仍会留存数据与日志。

PerpetualCow 称，因此次事件受损的用户将由他本人赔偿，Wagyu 将择期重新上线。其稍早还表示，损失主要集中在持续买入被抛售 XMR1 的做市商，兑换用户并未受损，1984 已因严重网络攻击暂时停止全部服务。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378457
items.title: XMR1被盗约1300万美元因托管商遭入侵，已删除服务器仍留存部署密钥

数学家称与Claude共同攻破黎曼猜想证明，尚未经独立验证

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 在个人网站发布声明，表示相信自己与 Claude 共同找到了黎曼猜想的证明，并称该方法还可推广至广义黎曼猜想，相关论证已用形式化证明工具 Lean 完成，且不附加额外假设，相关文件已公开。黎曼猜想由 Bernhard Riemann 于 1859 年提出，是千禧年七大数学难题之一。

Alpöge 为普林斯顿大学数学博士、哈佛学会前 Junior Fellow，目前在 Anthropic 工作。声明中称，在证明最后阶段 Claude 的进展已远超他本人。由于论证极为庞大，完整文字草稿据称超过 25 万页，目前先公开了 Lean 形式化文件。此外，目前仍只是作者本人宣布证明成功，尚未经过数学界独立验证。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378456

⚡️Sky澄清「PSM模块涉5.18亿美元非法关联交易」：单日兑换超20亿美元仍保持1:1锚定

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，Sky 针对有关锚定稳定模块 PSM 的负面报道发表正式声明称，当天协议用户通过 PSM 将超 20 亿美元 USDS 兑换为 USDC，为该模块迄今最大单日流出之一。兑换全程按 1:1 完成，模块内 USDC 从未低于 8 亿美元，随后回升至超 11 亿美元。协议抵押品约 93 亿美元，始终高于流通中的 USDS 和 DAI。去中心化金融风险分析机构 Block Analitica 复核后认为，此前负面报道多项核心说法存在误导或缺少上下文。

声明称，约三分之二被标记交易发生在 LitePSM 启用前的原 MakerDAO PSM，在 LitePSM 上占成交量不足 0.03%。报道中的 5.18 亿美元被指相关交易横跨五年，占 PSM 累计超 9600 亿美元成交量不足 0.06%。将该模块描述为「从可冻结的 USDC 中退出」并不被数据支持，大部分被标记交易经由聚合器进入 PSM，似乎并未经过 sky. money 或 spark. fi。

声明称，流通中的 USDS、sUSDS 和 DAI 均由 93 亿美元抵押品足额支撑。PSM 目前持有 10.7 亿美元 USDC，与 Sky Agents 的稳定币合计 23 亿美元。过去 12 个月，协议总收入 4.12 亿美元，同比增长 7.8%，净收入 1.31 亿美元，同比增长 48.5%。

此前，链上风控机构 Inca Digital 的调查显示，Sky 的 PSM 曾处理 422 个与黑客、钓鱼活动或受制裁实体等有关联的钱包交易，累计约 5.18 亿美元，其中 1.019 亿美元与朝鲜相关活动直接关联。调查称，相关储备约有 27 亿枚 USDC 集中在同一以太坊地址，若 Circle 因法院命令或执法请求冻结该地址，正常储备也可能无法动用，从而中断双向兑换。这是调查提出的风险情景，并非储备已被冻结。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378455

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- Coinbase Borrow opened to eligible New York customers on Nov. 16, extending the service to the state it initially excluded.
- Lenders on Morpho supply the USDC. Coinbase says those retail loans sit off its balance sheet, separate from its institutional loan book.
- New York customers can borrow against Bitcoin, Ethereum or Solana, with variable rates, processing fees and collateral liquidation risk.
Coinbase opened its crypto-backed borrowing service to eligible New York customers on Nov. 16. The exchange runs the service in its app, and lenders on Morpho supply the USDC.
Morpho announced the expansion on Nov. 17. Its product-wide snapshot put outstanding Coinbase Borrow loans at $1.63 billion in USDC, backed by about $3 billion in crypto collateral.
Coinbase Chief Financial Officer Alesia Haas drew the accounting distinction on the company’s Oct. 29 analyst call. She said:
“We also are growing retail loans, but those are off balance sheet through our partnership with Morpho.”
Coinbase’s quarterly filing shows about $2 billion in institutional loan receivables at Sept. 30. Haas said Coinbase funds that book with corporate cash and with crypto or USDC that consenting institutional clients lend to Coinbase for it to lend onward.
Who supplies the money
For a Bitcoin-backed loan, Coinbase converts the pledged Bitcoin to its cbBTC wrapped version, and sends it to a Morpho smart contract on Base. Participants supplying USDC to Morpho’s lending markets provide the capital available for borrowers to draw.
Morpho says Coinbase Borrow has originated more than $3 billion since it launched in January 2025, including loans borrowers may already have repaid. The $1.63 billion figure measures what was still outstanding in the Nov. 17 snapshot.
Morpho co-founder Merlin Egalite sees a role for established financial firms in that arrangement. He told CryptoSlate:
“Banks and fintechs don’t disappear in this model. They own the customer relationship, distribution and compliance, while the network handles the plumbing.”
Alea Research’s third-quarter benchmark attributed 62% of the roughly $2 billion increase in Morpho’s outstanding loans to chains and collateral associated with Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle and Kraken.
Alea groups loans by the blockchain or collateral they use. For example, its Coinbase category covers loans backed by Coinbase-branded collateral on Base, across all interfaces. The groupings show where the debt sits and which assets back it, and they can include loans that originated outside the companies’ apps.
The trade-offs for borrowers
Jacob Frantz, Coinbase’s head of yield and investment products, framed the appeal in terms of what customers can do with assets they already hold. He told CryptoSlate:
“People ultimately want more flexibility baked into their financial services, without compromising trust.”
Coinbase’s New York terms limit eligible collateral to Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana and offer variable-rate loans only. The rate can move as supply and demand change in the lending market, and Coinbase may add a platform fee.
Each draw also carries a processing fee that gets added to the loan balance and accrues interest.
Coinbase says variable-rate loans have no set term or minimum payments. Borrowers can repay part or all of a loan at any time, but they need to watch the amount they owe relative to the collateral's value.
A drop in the collateral price or a rise in the balance as interest accrues can push the loan to the point of liquidation.
Coinbase also lists risks involving the lending protocol’s security and liquidity and its own wallet.
items.title: The DeFi protocol powering $1.6 billion in Coinbase loans as crypto lending goes mainstream

以太坊Glamsterdam升级推迟至2027年1月，因合约部署费用大幅提高

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，以太坊核心开发者在本周例会上表示，原计划于今年 12 月进行的 Glamsterdam 升级，最早不会在 2027 年 1 月中旬前上线，更可能在 1 月下旬或 2 月初推出，以便给受影响的应用团队留出修复时间。以太坊基金会和外部安全研究人员已联系超 50 家受影响公司，多数公司表示，若升级规则保持不变，可在 1 月中旬前完成代码修补。

此次升级旨在提升网络吞吐能力，但会大幅提高在链上创建永久性数据的费用。部署新智能合约的基础 gas 将从 32,000 升至 183,600 并另行收取代码存储费用。按旧费用假设编写的程序可能在交易中途耗尽 gas 而失败。安全研究人员已发现约 200 个潜在问题，以太坊基金会开发者 Marius van der Wijden 上周估计，受影响程序可能多达 1.5 万个。开发者暂定于 12 月 14 日当周在 Hoodi 测试网进行演练，是否推进将在 11 月 26 日的下次会议上决定。应用方需在 12 月中旬前修复最严重问题，其余问题则需在 1 月 10 日前完成。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378450

SpaceX旗下Cursor考虑弃用中国AI模型，众议院报告施压引发替代潮

动察 Beating AI 快讯，据 CNBC 报道，SpaceX 旗下 AI 编程平台 Cursor 正考虑因「地缘政治风险」逐步淘汰中国开发的开放权重 AI 模型。报告指出，Cursor 的编程模型 Composer 2 正是基于月之暗面的 Kimi K2.5 构建。SpaceX 于今年 8 月以隐含 600 亿美元的估值完成对 Cursor 的收购。该报告经过数月调查，发现成本、定制化能力及接近前沿的性能，是推动美国科技公司采用中国模型的核心原因，这引发了华盛顿的担忧。

报告指出，美国目前缺乏在「市场价格和性能」上具备竞争力的开源权重替代品。为此报告建议启动一项「美国国家开放权重倡议」，整合公共算力与评估基础设施。此外还呼吁在 10 月禁止 DeepSeek 进入联邦民事机构系统的基础上，进一步禁止联邦信息系统及联邦合同使用中国开发的 AI 模型。除 Cursor 外，Airbnb 和 DoorDash 也因使用中国 AI 模型接受了调查。与此同时，美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）本周一发布了临时最终规则，声称目标防止中国公司通过海外数据中心远程访问美国 AI 芯片并利用其进行模型蒸馏。

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
AMD shed $67 billion in market value on Thursday after short-seller Hunterbrook claimed in its publication The Bear Cave that AMD had a “China problem,” invoking Nvidia’s chip-smuggling scandal and $2 trillion collapse.
Down 7.7% in a single trading session — plus another 1% after-hours — it would have been easy to call the AMD short-sale a success were it not for Andrew Left’s upcoming prison sentencing, set for December 8.
A federal jury convicted Left, founder of one of the earliest activist short-selling outfits Citron Research, on 13 of 17 criminal charges relating to a multi-million dollar scheme.
According to Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva, “Left used his expertise to profit at the expense of retail investors, ordinary people who owned the stocks he targeted.
“He callously boasted that it was like ‘taking candy from a baby.’”
Read more: Andrew Left of Citron Research gets torched by GME… again
Hunterbrook on AMD’s ‘China problem’
Attempting to distance itself from Left, Hunterbrook claimed AMD maintained a questionable business relationship with Aivres, a China-connected server maker that was also involved in Nvidia’s alleged avoidance of US export controls.
The hedge fund attached to Hunterbrook was short the chipmaker before publishing the bearish reports, and it stood to benefit from yesterday’s stock price decline.
Citron Research, for years, published market-moving stock reports and profited from the impact of those reports.
In addition to the Aivres relationship, Hunterbrook claimed that Chinese server vendor IEIT Systems kept folding newer AMD startup code into its server software. This is despite the fact that the US Commerce Department blacklisted IEIT in March 2025.
AMD quickly denied this. “The claims misrepresent AMD’s business practices and relationships,” a spokesperson said, assuring the public that “AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations.”
Hunterbrook disclosed, “Hunterbrook Capital is short AMD and long a basket of comparable securities.”
In other words, it had constructed a portfolio that stood to benefit from AMD’s idiosyncratic decline, regardless of the broad movement of its sector.
According to the US Justice Department, “In advance of his tweets and reports, Left would enter limit orders to trade in the opposite direction of his public recommendations.”
AMD crashes as critics allege circular financing
Via its Bear Cave, Hunterbrook also accused AMD of circular financing, claiming “AMD finances its own customers much the way Nvidia does.”
It didn’t mince words, saying, “If Nvidia is the Central Bank of AI, then AMD is more like the Silicon Valley Bank of AI.”
That derogatory reference invokes Silicon Valley Bank’s sudden and spectacular bankruptcy.
AMD’s loops of related-party financing spin through Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, and around the AI industry.
For example, AMD agreed to put $1 billion into Meta’s share offering. In turn, Meta committed to the first gigawatt of a six-gigawatt AMD GPU deal that Electronics Weekly valued at $60 billion.
AMD also agreed to buy $2.5 billion of Anthropic stock at the IPO price this week, while Anthropic plans to return favors by spending over $20 billion on AMD compute.
The company also co-led a round for TensorWave, which expressed its gratitude by announcing that it will use AMD chips in its OpenAI deal.

items.content:
Quick Take
- MIT researchers linked air pollution from power plants supplying US data centers to an estimated 650 premature deaths in 2023.
- Pollution traveled across state lines, leaving communities with few data centers facing some of the highest estimated death rates.
- As AI infrastructure expands, researchers warn that new facilities could impose health costs on distant communities unless power sources are considered.
Air pollution from power plants supplying US data centers contributed to an estimated 650 premature deaths in 2023, researchers found.
An MIT-led study published Nov. 19 found that pollution associated with data center electricity demand traveled across state boundaries, exposing communities with relatively few facilities to elevated health risks.
The findings follow separate Harvard University research estimating that major US data centers generated 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions over a 12-month period, highlighting the environmental costs accompanying the artificial intelligence industry's expansion.
Data center pollution reaches communities hundreds of miles away
The MIT researchers examined how data centers' electricity demand influenced power generation and air pollution across the contiguous United States in 2023.
Their findings, published in Environmental Research Letters, attributed 513 premature deaths to fine particulate pollution and another 137 to ground-level ozone.
Together, those deaths represented approximately 5.3% of the country's estimated mortality linked to electricity-related air pollution.
How data center power use affects downwind air
The 2023 model followed electricity demand across the grid and tracked how the resulting emissions moved through the air.
Contiguous US, 2023. The study estimated 513 premature deaths from fine particles and 137 from ground-level ozone.
The place that draws the power and the place exposed to its pollution can be in different states.
The diagram illustrates the study’s mechanism without mapping any single plant or route. The chart shows modeled counts for 2023 grid electricity and excludes onsite backup generation.
Virginia and Texas accounted for the largest data center electricity demand, consuming 33.9 and 21.8 terawatt-hours, respectively. However, Iowa, Nevada, South Dakota, and Kansas recorded some of the highest estimated death rates per resident, despite several having relatively few data centers.
The geographical imbalance reflects how America's interconnected electricity grid distributes the environmental consequences of growing power demand.
For example, electricity consumption by Virginia data centers can increase generation at coal and natural gas plants in the Ohio Valley. Emissions from those facilities subsequently travel through the atmosphere, where they can combine with ammonia from agricultural activities in the Midwest to form harmful fine particles.
These pollutants are associated with heart attacks, strokes, and respiratory illnesses.
The researchers also found that rural populations faced significantly higher estimated mortality risks than urban communities, extending the health consequences beyond the regions hosting major computing facilities.
The analysis tracked how power plants responded to data center electricity demand and used atmospheric models to estimate where the resulting pollution accumulated.
Harvard research exposes broader environmental costs of AI expansion
A separate Harvard-led study published Nov. 16 in Nature Sustainability examined electricity consumption and carbon emissions across 403 major US data centers between May 2024 and April 2025.
The researchers estimated that the facilities consumed approximately 82 terawatt-hours of electricity, equivalent to 1.8% of total US electricity consumption.
That demand was associated with approximately 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, with fossil fuels accounting for roughly 54% of the electricity generation attributed to the facilities.
Depending on assumptions about electricity demand, estimated emissions ranged from 21 million to 31 million metric tons.
The study also found that the facilities' average carbon intensity was approximately 314 grams of carbon dioxide per kilowatt-hour, compared with the national electricity generation average of 348 grams.
The Harvard findings add to concerns about the environmental costs of hyperscale computing infrastructure as technology companies expand capacity to meet growing demand for AI services.
While Harvard examined greenhouse gas emissions, MIT traced how electricity generation contributes to air pollution and premature mortality.
The findings intensify scrutiny of where new data centers are built and how their electricity is generated.
MIT researchers urged planners to consider air-quality consequences across affected regions, including communities far from the facilities, when deciding where to locate new computing infrastructure.
items.title: AI data center boom linked to 650 premature US deaths as pollution spreads across states

美银：感恩节后美股大概率迎短期技术性反弹，大级别行情需满足三大条件

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，美银首席投资策略师 Michael Hartnett 在最新报告中指出，全球股市广度已恶化至极端的「超卖」状态，感恩节后美股大概率将迎来一波技术性反弹。但他强调这仅是短期的喘息，并非趋势反转。当前价格层面的抛售并未带来仓位层面的出清，过去一周全球股票基金仍流入 666 亿美元，且基金经理调查显示现金水位仅 3.6%，资产配置者普遍做多股票，市场需要看到更多仓位层面的出清，才能给出全面买入的许可。

要演变成大级别行情，市场必须同时看到三大宏观条件：十年期美债收益率跌破 4.5%、WTI 原油跌破 70 美元/桶，以及美元在疲软数据后确认见顶。美银同时警告，市场严重低估了硬着陆风险。支撑经济的家庭股票财富本季度已缩水约 5 万亿美元，超大规模云厂商的 AI 资本开支预估达 1.3 万亿美元，但自由现金流为负 2830 亿美元。

Hartnett 将接下来的市场概括为「两个问题的市场」：加息何时结束，以及是否赶在衰退之前。若美联储将股市视为「大到不能倒」，信用和股市的下跌本身就能短路加息周期；若转向抗击通胀的「硬汉」，硬着陆风险将大幅上升。在此之前，最优策略是保住本金，等待「恐惧」更明显地浮现。

GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors are very red post-ANT IPO; BTC at $61.6k
- ANT pops to $105 on IPO, settles at $97 ($88 premarket)
- Apple teases its own autonomous AI agent
- BTC ETFs record $582M in outflows, now over $1B on the week

Anthropic Wins, Markets Sell Off
The largest base IPO deal ever priced at $83 a share Wednesday night, opened Thursday morning at $111.50, and briefly pushed Anthropic’s fully diluted valuation past $2 trillion. The stock finished at $97.17, up 17% from the offer and down 13% from where it opened (it has since fallen about 15% to $88).
A 17% first-day gain on an $81.34 billion raise is a successful listing by any normal standard.
The rest of the market did not fare as well.
The Nasdaq fell 2.06%. The S&P 500 dropped 1.9%. The Dow lost 2.17% and closed below 50,000 for the first time since June. Tech had rallied before the bell on the listing and reversed by the afternoon.
MD fell 7.73%. Nebius dropped 7.8%. CoreWeave lost 5%. Nvidia slid 3.4% despite beating earnings last week. Oracle, Micron, Broadcom and Microsoft all finished lower. The biggest AI listing in history happened, and AI infrastructure was the worst place to be holding.
Joe Maher at Capital Economics put it plainly: “Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO has failed to rekindle enthusiasm for tech stocks.”
Crypto went with it. Bitcoin fell to $61,500, its lowest since early July. That’s a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be the longest run since the nine-week stretch in 2022. Eth hit the $1,750 level, down 28% in thirty days. Gold fell to a fourteen-month low. Silver dropped 3%.
When Bitcoin, equities and gold all sell off on the same session, the common factor is usually the discount rate.
That’s the Fed. Chris Waller spent this week making the case for fifty basis points in December, and the minutes showed he isn’t alone. FxPro’s Alex Kuptsikevich described the market as spooked by “the spectre of a double rate hike” and pointed out Bitcoin is now more than 7% below its 200-week moving average, the deepest it has traded below that line in three years.
So where does this leave us heading into next week?
Start with what an $81 billion IPO actually does to a market. That money came from somewhere. Add the separate $26 billion private placement from Nvidia, Google, AMD and four other suppliers, and roughly $107 billion of capital got committed to a single name in one day. Kuptsikevich raised the possibility that the listing absorbed the riskiest money in the system, and that if so, some of it rotates back out once the allocation settles.
That’s the bull case for crypto over the next few weeks. It requires the Fed to cooperate.
For the bear case, one can simply look at SpaceX.
SpaceX priced at $135 in June, opened at $150, and closed its first day up 19%. Then it kept running, hitting $225.64 four days later, up 67% from the offer. The unwind started the following session. By June 22 it had fallen 16% in a single day and sat 31% off the high. By mid-July it traded below its IPO price. By late July it was down roughly 50% from the peak.
That would project out to a market low around Christmas time, which is actually how the 2018 midterm cycle played out. Will history repeat itself? We will find out soon enough. In the interim, expect volatility.

items.content:
Lagarde warns Europe could miss chance to unify tokenized markets
The ECB president said Europe’s market for tokenized securities could split into platforms that cannot settle trades with one another.
European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde warned Friday that Europe needs common rules for tokenized securities before incompatible standards take hold across trading platforms.
Speaking at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress, Lagarde said blockchain technology lets firms issue, trade and settle securities on a single platform. The global markets for tokenized assets was worth about 23 billion euros in March, five times its size a year earlier, she said.
Europe could build a single market for those assets, Lagarde said, but if platforms adopt different rules as they grow, they may be unable to settle trades with one another. She said lawmakers have a role alongside the ECB.
“Common rules will be needed too, and those lie with legislators,” she said.
The Eurosystem launched Pontes in September, giving financial institutions a way to settle tokenized securities trades in central bank money. Earlier in November, the European Stability Mechanism used Pontes to settle a 1 billion euro (about $1.1 million) digital bond.
Through a second project, Appia, the Eurosystem is working with market participants on common standards for tokenized securities. It plans to publish a blueprint in 2028.
Related: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027
items.title: Lagarde warns Europe could miss chance to unify tokenized markets

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- Institutional investors can buy Bitcoin before redeeming tokenized money-market funds, with dealers advancing stablecoins to execute trades.
- The arrangement could accelerate Bitcoin purchases by unlocking trading liquidity from tokenized fund holdings without waiting for bank settlements.
- The model depends on dealer inventory, conversion limits and settlement speed, even as stablecoin supply contracts at its fastest pace since 2022.
An institutional investor can ask a market maker to buy Bitcoin before the investor has turned tokenized fund shares into cash.
Greg Guttas, head of over-the-counter trading at Flowdesk, told CryptoSlate that the desk could pay with its own stablecoins and settle with the client later against the fund holding.
Securitize and Ethena opened a new route for fund holders on Nov. 12 with a facility for BlackRock’s USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund (BUIDL) that exchanges fund shares for stablecoins outside banking hours. That gives eligible investors a way to raise trading cash themselves.
In Guttas’s example, a dealer would supply the cash for the Bitcoin purchase upfront.
The question of what dealers can spend is sharper after a drop in stablecoin supply. Glassnode reported that aggregate stablecoin supply fell $14.2 billion in the 30 days through Nov. 9, the fastest contraction since June 2022.
The marketwide total leaves open how much an individual desk has on hand and what it would commit to a client’s trade.
Who pays for the Bitcoin first
Guttas described how an over-the-counter desk could handle a purchase for a client holding tokenized money-market fund shares:
“The market maker in that scenario could use their own stablecoin balances to buy the BTC immediately and then redeem the tokenized MM funds after the fact.”
That sequence would give the client time to settle using the fund position, while the dealer would spend the stablecoins first and wait for settlement to recover them. Until then, those funds would be unavailable for another purchase.
The longer it takes to turn fund shares into settlement cash, the longer the desk has to carry the exposure. Guttas said larger conversions can hit size limits, and weekends can complicate access.
In January 2025, QCP disclosed that it facilitated a six-month Bitcoin basis trade for Securitize Credit using BUIDL as collateral.
A basis trade aims to capture the difference between spot and futures prices, but QCP’s account leaves the funding currency for the Bitcoin leg and the settlement timing undisclosed.
How fund shares turn into trading cash
The Securitize and Ethena facility works in both directions for BUIDL. Eligible investors can exchange their fund shares for supported stablecoins, including USDC, or use those stablecoins to acquire BUIDL.
That route can give a fund holder cash to trade on a weekend.
The facility opened with $50 million of inventory, split between $25 million in USDC and $25 million in BUIDL. Securitize said up to another $50 million may become available within about an hour as liquidity is used, subject to terms and availability, bringing the maximum facility capacity to $100 million.
The relevant starting figure for a holder seeking stablecoins at launch was the $25 million in USDC, while the BUIDL side of the inventory serves investors converting stablecoins into fund shares.
Since February, prequalified BUIDL investors have been able to request quotes through Securitize’s UniswapX integration from approved participants, including Flowdesk, Tokka Labs and Wintermute.
The quoted size depends on the liquidity approved counterparties offer when an investor asks. Once a quoted swap executes, both sides settle together on-chain.
Circle’s USYC, a separate fund token restricted to eligible non-US investors, redeems into USDC in one block below its instant-redemption threshold, with per-block time varying by network.
Above that threshold, Circle lists same-day or next-day settlement, with separate arrangements available for additional immediate liquidity.
What the stablecoin supply figure leaves open
Katana CEO Matthew Fisher told CryptoSlate he looks at exchange balances, stablecoins posted as collateral in lending and perpetual futures markets, and how much traders borrow against them.
Those measures help show where stablecoins are being used for trading and leverage, but a balance on an exchange can sit there without becoming a Bitcoin order. Fisher advised watching the deployed number.
How large a trade an institution could finance depends on the dealer’s available inventory, the terms it offers, and how quickly the fund position can be converted into settlement cash. The arrangement would put existing stablecoins to work earlier in the trade.

items.content:
In brief
- MoonPay has applied to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for a national trust bank charter, according to Bloomberg.
- The proposed MoonPay National Trust Bank, based in Miami Beach, Florida, would help the company grow its custody business and expand its stablecoin services.
- The OCC has already granted final approval to Coinbase, Circle and Ripple, but the wave of crypto charters faces opposition from banks and Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA).
Crypto payments firm MoonPay has applied for a U.S. national bank charter, joining a growing list of crypto companies seeking a federal banking license.
The proposed MoonPay National Trust Bank would be based in Miami Beach, Florida, according to the company's November 17 application to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Bloomberg reported on Thursday. The charter would help MoonPay grow its custody business and expand its stablecoin services, according to the application.
MoonPay confirmed the move on Thursday, tweeting that it was "proud to share" that it had applied for a U.S. national bank charter with the OCC.
today we are proud to share that MoonPay has applied for a US National Bank Charter with the OCC 🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/XGHBPx84v0
— MoonPay 🟣 (@moonpay) November 19, 2026
Unlike a full-service bank, a national trust bank can hold and manage assets for clients, but can't take deposits or lend money. The OCC did not immediately respond to Bloomberg's request for comment.
From payments to institutions
Founded in 2019, MoonPay is best known for providing on- and off-ramps between fiat currencies and crypto. It has been expanding into new areas including AI, having launched a crypto wallet designed for AI chatbots, let users buy crypto through ChatGPT, and acquired AI trading copilot startup Dawn Labs.
ETH price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
It has also been courting institutions. In April, it acquired Sodot, a Tel Aviv-based crypto key management firm, to form the basis of MoonPay Institutional, a unit serving banks, asset managers and trading firms. The unit is led by former acting Commodity Futures Trading Commission chair Caroline Pham.
A rush for charters
MoonPay is the latest crypto firm to seek a federal charter under President Donald Trump's administration. Earlier this month, Coinbase joined Circle and Ripple in receiving final OCC approval for a national trust bank, after Ripple won approval for a trust bank behind its RLUSD stablecoin. Jack Dorsey's Block has also applied for a charter to custody Bitcoin, while World Liberty Financial, the crypto venture tied to the Trump family, won conditional approval for its own trust company in August.
The approvals have drawn pushback. A banking group has sued over Block's application, accusing crypto firms of seeking "side door" access to banking, while Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) has argued that the OCC's approvals of Coinbase and Ripple were illegal, a claim the crypto industry has disputed.
Warren is expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, and is expected to examine World Liberty's charter as part of a wider look at Trump-linked crypto ventures.

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin fell below $62,000 on Friday, its lowest level since early July, as more than $720 million in leveraged positions were wiped out across crypto in 24 hours.
- Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582 million in net outflows on Thursday, their largest since October, taking November's total to almost $3.5 billion.
- Glassnode said the average Bitcoin holder is only just in profit, while CoinShares expects Bitcoin to trade between $60,000 and $90,000 for much of 2027.
Bitcoin slid below $62,000 on Friday, extending a weeklong sell-off as investors pulled money from spot Bitcoin ETFs and braced for another interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve.
The leading cryptocurrency was trading at around $61,780, down 2.8% over the past day and 10% over the past week, after touching a 24-hour low of $61,273—its lowest level since early July—according to CoinGecko data. It has fallen more than $2,000 since struggling to hold $64,000 earlier this week, and has also formed a so-called death cross, a bearish chart pattern.
The drop triggered $727 million in liquidations across crypto markets over the past 24 hours, about 86% of which were long positions betting on higher prices, according to CoinGlass. Bitcoin accounted for just under $202 million of the total, with more than 151,000 traders liquidated.
ETF exodus
Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.2 million in net outflows on Thursday, their largest single-day outflow since October 30, according to SoSoValue data. The funds have lost more than $1.1 billion so far this week and almost $3.5 billion in November, while their total net assets have fallen to $76.6 billion.
"Within crypto, the most telling sign is this month's outflow from spot Bitcoin ETFs, which suggests investors are choosing to stay on the sidelines for now," Neil Steinhardt, head of Nexo U.S., told Decrypt.
Treasury yields above 5% and expectations that the Fed will raise rates in December have weighed on assets that don't pay interest, including Bitcoin and gold, Steinhardt said. "Because the pressure appears tied to the rate backdrop, and that backdrop has shifted before, a turn in yields or the dollar would likely be the first signal that appetite is returning," he added, pointing to the December 4 jobs report and the Fed's December 9 meeting as the next checkpoints.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller has called for a larger, half-point increase at that meeting, unless policymakers signal another rise in January. Traders are betting on a smaller move: CME FedWatch puts the odds of a quarter-point hike on December 9 at 99.2%, with the chance of a half-point increase falling to almost zero from more than 9% on Thursday morning.
Holders near break-even
The decline has left the average Bitcoin holder only just in profit. Bitcoin is still trading above its realized price, the average price at which every coin on the network last moved, but the margin is thin, onchain analytics firm Glassnode tweeted on Friday. A break below would put holders in loss for the first time since early 2023, it said.
The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit.
bitcoin:native trades above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network. The margin is thin: MVRV sits just above 1.
A break below would put holders in loss for the first time since early 2023. pic.twitter.com/rPOTbZS1NF
— glassnode (@glassnode) November 20, 2026
CoinShares head of research James Butterfill sees the slide as part of a longer downturn. "I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another," he said in a note published on Thursday, pointing to selling by large holders since late 2025, expectations of higher rates and weakness in tech stocks.
CoinShares' base case is for Bitcoin to trade between $60,000 and $90,000 through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives the Fed room to ease, Butterfill said.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Binance hacker moves nearly $600M in ETH, routes funds through THORChain, Chainflip
OnChain Lens tracked nearly $600 million in ETH transfers over two days as the Binance hackers moved the stolen funds through fresh wallets and cross-chain protocols to obscure their trail.
Wallets linked to the Binance hack moved nearly $600 million in Ether over two days, with some of the stolen funds routed through cross-chain swap protocols, according to blockchain analysts.
The attackers moved about $594 million in Ether (ETH) to fresh wallets, $248 million on Thursday and another 197,460 ETH, worth approximately $346 million, on Friday. Attackers routed part of the funds through cross-chain protocols THORChain and Chainflip, according to blockchain data provider Onchain Lens.
About $5 million was routed through Chainflip, while THORChain accounted for most of the cross-chain activity tracked by blockchain analyst SomaXBT, according to estimates he shared in a Friday X response. Onchain analyst Specter also estimated that only a “small portion” of the funds moved through Chainflip, which has said it screens deposits for illicit funds, although it previously acknowledged gaps in those checks.
North Korean hackers have previously used THORChain to launder funds stolen from some of the largest crypto hacks, including the $1.4 billion Bybit hack in February 2025 and the $388 million Bitget hack in September 2026. TRM Labs and Chainalysis have linked the $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor.
Following the latest transfers, the Binance hackers’ publicly tracked addresses held approximately 224,722 ETH, worth about $394 million, according to blockchain data platform Arkham.
THORChain’s 24-hour swap volume soared to $239 million on Friday, pushing the protocol’s earnings to $243,000, according to THORChain’s dashboard.
Related: Binance hackers move 81% of stolen Solana, route funds via THORChain

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Coinbase is aiming to launch its own prediction market contracts in the U.S. in the first half of 2027, according to Bloomberg.
- The exchange currently offers prediction markets through Kalshi, and has been building its own clearing and trading infrastructure.
- Its prediction markets passed $200 million in annualized revenue in the third quarter, making them one of Coinbase's fastest-growing products.
Coinbase is planning to launch its own prediction market contracts in the U.S. in the first half of 2027, as it looks to take more control of one of its fastest-growing businesses.
The exchange plans to offer the in-house event contracts to both retail and institutional customers, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter.
A Coinbase spokesperson told Bloomberg the company had "nothing new to announce today," and pointed to plans it set out in October to expand its prediction markets and improve their economics by building its own clearing and other infrastructure. The spokesperson did not address the timing of an in-house launch.
From Kalshi to in-house
Coinbase rolled out prediction markets across the U.S. through a partnership with Kalshi, after unveiling the product alongside stock trading last year. Offering its own contracts would give Coinbase more say over which markets it lists, and let it keep more of the revenue from trades.
The exchange has been laying the groundwork for its pivot. In December 2025, it agreed to buy prediction markets startup The Clearing Company, and in September 2026 it received approval from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) for its own clearinghouse. Coinbase already runs a regulated derivatives exchange.
A 'less correlated' revenue stream
Prediction markets have become a bright spot for Coinbase as crypto trading slows. The business passed $200 million in annualized revenue in the third quarter, with daily traders up more than 60% from the previous quarter, and revenue growing 82% a quarter on average since launch, the company reported in October.
"Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility," CFO Alesia Haas said at the time. On an analyst call the same day, Haas said Coinbase's new clearinghouse meant it "can launch our own contracts, and we can also then earn better economics," while continuing to offer contracts through partners such as Kalshi. Asked when, she said: "We have not shared a timeline."
The products have faced legal challenges from states that argue some event contracts amount to unlicensed gambling. Coinbase sued three states over their attempts to regulate prediction markets, and New York sued Coinbase and Gemini over their offerings in April.
Last week, a Louisiana judge temporarily barred more than 30 prediction market providers, including Coinbase's derivatives arm, from offering event contracts in the state, after Attorney General Liz Murrill sued them on November 12, Forbes reported. The CFTC has sued Louisiana in federal court to block the order, and a hearing on a longer injunction is set for November 30.
Disclosure
Decrypt's parent company, Dastan, operates its own prediction market, Decrypt Predict.

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin fell on 77% of major Nasdaq down days since January 2024, averaging a nearly 2% decline, according to DWF Labs.
- Bitcoin lost 39% while semiconductor stocks gained 85%, suggesting it missed the AI rally but remains exposed to broader market selloffs.
- The Fed's concerns over AI debt and complex financing raise questions about Bitcoin's resilience if an AI selloff spreads across Wall Street.
DWF Labs reported on Nov. 19 that Bitcoin fell on 77% of US trading days when QQQ, an ETF that tracks the Nasdaq-100, lost at least 1%.
The analysis covers the period from the start of US spot Bitcoin ETF trading on Jan. 11, 2024, through Nov. 13, 2026. DWF put Bitcoin’s average decline on large Nasdaq down days at about 2%.
In the Federal Reserve’s October meeting minutes, released Nov. 18, almost all participants discussed what could happen if returns on artificial intelligence investments disappointed. Most pointed to rapid growth in AI-related debt and the complex, opaque structures used to finance much of it.
From September 2025 through the end of the study’s data on Nov. 13, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) gained 85% while Bitcoin fell 39%, according to DWF Labs.
If an AI selloff spreads from chip stocks to the wider Nasdaq-100, Bitcoin’s record on those down days becomes more relevant than its trading during the chip rally.
What the Fed said about AI market risks
At the Oct. 27-28 meeting, many participants discussed the potential consequences of AI-related assets losing value if investors became less confident about the returns.
A few noted that exposure was becoming concentrated among a small number of firms, raising questions about how the buildout was financed and what the projects themselves might earn.
Fed staff flagged two structures that could amplify losses if returns disappointed.
One was off-balance-sheet leases, which can leave firms committed to future payments that do not appear on their balance sheets. The other was circular financing among AI-related firms, which ties their funding to one another.
Investors who borrowed to buy assets might have to sell holdings to reduce their debt, while fund managers might also need to sell to meet withdrawals. In the most severe scenarios, sales by vehicles such as hedge funds, bond mutual funds and target-date funds could make it harder for markets to absorb trades.
Elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage were the biggest vulnerabilities in the staff assessment. Strong bank and household balance sheets offered a buffer against more severe outcomes, and several participants noted the staff’s finding that banks were well capitalized.
Some participants saw gaps in the picture, and several questioned whether supervisors had enough data on banks’ indirect exposure through nonbank institutions, such as credit lines to private credit funds.
The minutes describe a stress scenario in which an asset-price decline compounds through financing commitments, leverage and the need to raise cash.
The connection for Bitcoin investors would depend on whether those pressures move beyond AI-related firms and pull down the wider market.
An AI stock selloff could hurt Bitcoin
DWF Labs measured Bitcoin’s performance on days when a fund tracking the Nasdaq-100 dropped at least 1%.
The report found a similar pattern before US spot Bitcoin ETFs began trading. From 2020 until the January 2024 launch, Bitcoin fell on 74% of the Nasdaq-100 proxy’s large down days, and it fell on 77% from the launch through Nov. 13, 2026.
Yahoo Finance’s adjusted closes show 91 Bitcoin declines across 118 days when QQQ fell at least 1% in the latter period. Bitcoin’s average log return across all 118 days was -1.93%, including days when Bitcoin rose or held steady as well as days when it fell.
QQQ’s return runs from the prior US trading session’s close. Bitcoin’s return runs across consecutive calendar-day closes, with its daily candle ending at midnight UTC, three to four hours after the US stock market closes.
Closing prices alone don't capture the order of moves, and Bitcoin can keep moving for several hours after the US trading session ends, so the comparison includes part of that post-close window.
CME Group research found that Bitcoin and US stocks often moved more closely together in periods of market stress. One possible explanation is the need for cash, since an investor reducing borrowing or covering losses can sell Bitcoin alongside stocks to raise it.
DWF’s results subtracted QQQ’s daily return from Bitcoin’s and SOXX’s returns. On that measure, the two had a correlation of negative 0.30 from March 2026 through the end of the sample. When chip stocks beat the Nasdaq-100 proxy, Bitcoin tended to lag it.
From September 2025 through Nov. 13, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) gained 85% and Bitcoin fell 39%.
- Semiconductor ETF (SOXX)
- Bitcoin (BTC)
A separate analysis by Block Scholes researcher Thahbib Rahman found that broader market moves explained part of a recent Bitcoin decline. His firm found little evidence that investors sold Bitcoin specifically to buy AI assets.
What Bitcoin investors should watch
The Fed held rates in October, and almost all participants judged further increases likely under their baseline outlooks.
US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from September, and the advance estimate showed nominal retail and food services sales up 0.2%, within its margin of error, while industrial production fell 0.4%.
In the Philadelphia Fed’s November manufacturing survey, regional activity fell to 6.3 from 20.9 as the prices-received index rose to 47.0, the highest since June 2022.
Investors should watch whether declines spread across the Nasdaq-100 and how Treasury yields and the Fed rate outlook respond.
A chip-sector drop with little effect on the index would signal Bitcoin differently than a selloff that reaches the rest of the market. Bitcoin’s response would show how closely it is moving with equities in that episode.
items.title: Bitcoin missed AI stocks’ 85% rally but could still face the fallout if the boom unravels

items.content:
OpenAI跟进Anthropic防蒸馏措施：GPT-6.2思维链也上锁了

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenAI 开始给 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 的隐藏思维链加锁，防止其他模型通过 API 偷走推理过程，用来训练自己的模型。这套机制与 Anthropic 先前推出的防蒸馏措施高度相似。

10 月底，《The Information》援引知情人士报道称，DeepSeek 和月之暗面在训练新模型时，大量使用了 GPT-6 Astra 的输出。此前，国内 AI 公司曾大量蒸馏 Claude，但 Anthropic 不断加强封堵，促使部分厂商把目标转向 OpenAI。

蒸馏就是让一个模型学习更强模型的输出，以较低成本获得类似能力。如果能拿到完整的思维链，连模型如何拆解问题、一步步得出答案都能学走，比只看最终答案更有价值。

Anthropic 今年 6 月已经给 Claude 的加密思维链加上「上下文锁」。OpenAI 如今也采用类似机制：在多轮对话中，每段推理都与生成它之前的历史消息绑定。如果开发者修改旧提示词、工具配置或对话内容，API 就可能丢弃改动位置之后的推理项，防止攻击者通过篡改上下文诱导模型泄露内部思考。

OpenAI 公布的自测结果显示，在尝试提取上一轮隐藏推理的攻击中，GPT-6 Astra 的平均攻击成功率高达 54%，GPT-6.2 Astra 降至 0.2%，Sol 为 0.5%。

正常开发者也会受到影响。修改旧消息或压缩聊天记录，可能导致 Agent 丢失之前的推理成果，增加 Token 消耗和响应延迟。OpenAI 因此建议尽量保留原始对话历史，并使用官方提供的上下文压缩接口。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378424

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
VanEck to end Gemini ETF custody deals, keeps Coinbase
VanEck plans to end Gemini’s custody agreements for three crypto ETFs in February 2027, while Coinbase will continue serving as a custodian for the funds.
VanEck is cutting ties with Gemini as a custodian across three cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs), ending a relationship that began with its first spot Bitcoin ETF.
VanEck notified Gemini on Monday that it would terminate custody and clearing agreements for its Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Solana (SOL) ETFs, according to separate filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Thursday.
The agreements will end “on or about” Feb. 16, 2027, while Coinbase Custody, which already serves the funds, will continue providing custody services.
The move raises questions about Gemini’s position in the US spot crypto ETF market, where Coinbase serves as custodian for many of the largest funds. The filings did not disclose the reasons for the terminations.
VanEck to also end Gemini’s Solana staking arrangement
The termination extends beyond cryptocurrency custody. VanEck’s Solana ETF (VSOL) filing also covers a Gemini staking services agreement, raising questions about how the fund will handle staking after the transition.
Staking allows tokenholders to earn rewards by helping secure a proof-of-stake (PoS) blockchain such as Solana. For ETFs that stake their holdings, the service can provide an additional source of returns for the fund.
Cointelegraph contacted VanEck and Gemini for comment on the reason for terminating the agreements and the potential impact on the Solana ETF’s staking operations, but had not received a response by publication.
Winklevoss brothers helped pioneer spot Bitcoin ETFs
Gemini’s founders, Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, were among the earliest proponents of spot Bitcoin ETFs in the United States, filing to launch the Winklevoss Bitcoin Trust in July 2013. US regulators did not approve the first spot Bitcoin ETFs until January 2024, more than a decade after the brothers’ initial filing.
Gemini became the original Bitcoin custodian for VanEck’s spot Bitcoin ETF when the fund launched in January 2024, before VanEck added Coinbase Custody in June that year.
Related: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low
VanEck’s Bitcoin ETF (HODL) is considerably smaller than the largest US spot Bitcoin funds, holding about $880 million in assets under management, compared with $47.6 billion for BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) and $10.6 billion for Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC), according to Wallet Pilot data as of Thursday.
Gemini has also provided custody services for crypto ETFs in Canada and Australia. In the US, it continues to serve as a custodian for at least one smaller fund, the 7RCC Spot Bitcoin and Carbon Credit Futures ETF (BTCK), which identified Gemini and BitGo as its Bitcoin custodians in a September 2026 regulatory filing.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Ethereum is considering Dec. 16 or 17 for Glamsterdam's Hoodi test after postponing an earlier October activation.
- Auditors identified 200 compatibility findings across wallets, bridges and exchanges, including risks of locked funds and disrupted operations.
- A Nov. 26 decision will determine whether December testing proceeds, with proposed rule changes potentially delaying mainnet activation until May.
Ethereum developers are leaning toward retaining Glamsterdam's gas rules despite 200 findings that could disrupt existing smart contracts.
During a Nov. 19 core developers meeting, participants expressed broad support for proceeding with the current specifications rather than introducing changes that could push the network upgrade into April or May 2027.
Developers tentatively targeted the week of Dec. 14 for testing on Ethereum's Hoodi network, potentially allowing a mainnet activation as early as mid-January. However, the schedule remains unconfirmed as teams address compatibility problems affecting existing applications.
Ethereum's scaling ambitions expose problems across existing applications
Glamsterdam is designed to significantly expand Ethereum's capacity, potentially increasing its block gas limit from 60 million to 200 million, a more than threefold increase.
According to Ethereum research firm Ethlabs, the expansion would give applications more room to operate directly on Ethereum's main network while reducing congestion and transaction fees during periods of heavy demand.
However, achieving that capacity requires changing how Ethereum charges for certain computing operations and data storage.
Two proposals, EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, introduce new gas pricing and accounting rules that could invalidate assumptions built into existing smart contracts.
A ChainSecurity assessment identified 200 compatibility findings across its investigations and work coordinated by the Ethereum Foundation.
Of these, three were classified as high severity, 30 as medium and 167 as low. None was rated critical.
The assessment identified potential disruptions affecting bridges, exchanges, wallets, staking platforms, governance systems, and other infrastructure supporting Ethereum applications.
Most findings can be addressed through configuration changes, but 24 require smart contract upgrades or migrations. Potential consequences include interrupted operations, locked funds, and errors in reward accounting.
The problem stems partly from applications that rely on fixed gas allowances to perform specific operations. Under Glamsterdam's proposed rules, those allowances may no longer be sufficient to complete the same work.
Recent Juicebox V6 simulations demonstrated the consequences. Some transactions were recorded as successful even though internal payments failed or were skipped under the tested rules.
Ethlabs acknowledged that changing gas prices is necessary to support Ethereum's expansion but distinguished those changes from accounting modifications that introduced unexpected behavior.
The research firm argued that protocol developers must convince application developers of the upgrade's safety.
Developers resist changes that could push Glamsterdam to May
Despite the findings, Ethereum developers remain divided over whether modifying Glamsterdam's specifications would meaningfully improve compatibility.
The Besu client team advocated exploring a targeted revision to EIP-8037 to preserve existing smart contract behavior.
However, Ansgar Dietrichs and several other developers questioned whether a narrow adjustment would resolve enough problems to justify additional testing and development delays.
Marius van der Wijden also warned that changing how gas refunds are handled could disrupt contracts that depend on receiving those refunds during transaction execution.
The disagreement leaves developers choosing between allowing affected applications time to adjust to the existing specifications and redesigning parts of the upgrade to preserve more of their current behavior.
The Ethereum Foundation, alongside security researchers, has contacted more than 50 affected companies. During the meeting, Rahul reported that high-impact projects had completed or were expected to complete fixes by mid-December.
Other affected projects reported remediation schedules extending to Jan. 10, making mid-January the earliest viable mainnet activation window without specification changes.
A late-January or early-February rollout was also discussed as a more realistic possibility.
However, Dietrichs outlined substantially longer timelines if developers postpone their decision to investigate alternative rules.
Waiting until January to decide whether to retain the existing specifications could push activation into late February or early March. Adopting specification changes then could extend the rollout to April or May.
Such delays would also affect Ethereum's broader upgrade schedule, including preparations for Hegotá, which developers are discussing in connection with the network's post-quantum security transition.
The competing priorities have strengthened support for maintaining Glamsterdam's current design.
Developers are now considering a Hoodi activation around Dec. 16 or 17, after an earlier October test was postponed over compatibility concerns.
A final decision is expected during the next All Core Developers Consensus call on Nov. 26, when execution and consensus teams will determine whether to proceed with the December test.
Developers advocating changes have been asked to present specific alternatives, supported by impact analysis and auditor feedback, before that meeting.
Approval of the Hoodi schedule would effectively commit Ethereum to testing Glamsterdam's existing rules, leaving affected application teams to complete their fixes before the upgrade reaches mainnet.
items.title: Ethereum targets December Glamsterdam test despite 200 findings that could delay upgrade

items.content:
Bitcoin nears repeat of chart pattern that preceded 2023’s $25K retest
Bitcoin’s 21-day moving average fell below its 200-day average, and analyst Keith Alan expects a second bearish crossover by Sunday.
Bitcoin (BTC) could repeat a pair of bearish moving-average crossovers that preceded its retest of $25,000 in September 2023, according to analyst Keith Alan.
Key points:
- Bitcoin’s 21-day simple moving average (SMA) crossed below the 200-day SMA on Thursday. Alan expects the 50-day to cross below the 100-day before the weekly close.
- The two crossovers came four days part before the BTC/USD retested $25,000 support in September 2023.
- Bitcoin fell to a 20-week low of $61,231 on Friday after Thursday’s tech sell-off on the day of Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut.
Alan says Bitcoin’s crossover pattern “should not be ignored”
New analysis from Keith Alan, cofounder of crypto trading platform Material Indicators, compares this week’s Bitcoin chart with a similar setup in 2023.
On Bitstamp’s BTC/USD daily chart, the 21-day simple moving average (SMA) crossed below its 200-day equivalent on Thursday. The move last occurred in early November 2025, around one month after Bitcoin’s latest all-time high of $126,200, in the early stages of the current bear market. The 50-day SMA crossed below the 200-day SMA later that month, forming a conventional death cross.
Alan expects the 50-day SMA to cross below the 100-day SMA by the end of the week.
“We’ve only seen this happen once before in Bitcoin’s history, and it should not be ignored,” he summarized in a post on X.
BTC/USD one-day chart with 21-, 50-, 100- and 200-day SMAs. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The only other time in Bitcoin’s history that the two pairs of moving averages both produced a so-called “death cross” in the same period was between August and September 2023. BTC/USD retested support near $25,000 on Sept. 11.
Alan describes this double bottom as the start of a rally that took Bitcoin to its 2023 high of $44,700 in early December — an increase of 80%.
“One occurrence is by no means a large enough sample to consider a reliable pattern, or expect similar returns/drawdowns, however the timing, placement, and candle characteristics have enough similarities that we can’t ignore it either,” he said.
BTC/USD one-day chart with 21-, 50-, 100- and 200-day SMAs. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
BTC price hits new 20-week low near $61,200
Previously, Cointelegraph reported on Bitcoin losing support at the 200-week SMA for the first time since mid-August. The trend line typically functions as support during bull-market retracements, but it can act as resistance when Bitcoin rebounds from below it.
Related: Institutions pile back into US Bitcoin ETFs in Q3 after selling streak
BTC/USD fell to $61,231 on Friday, its lowest level since July 3, a day after Anthropic’s record IPO and Nasdaq debut. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index finished Thursday’s trading session down 2.25% at 23,879 points, its lowest daily close since April 14.
Anthropic shares traded around $91.50 before Friday’s open. It closed Thursday at $97.17, 20% below the day’s $115 peak.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Meta Muse 隐私问题接连曝光：乱读加密消息、疑似串号，甚至擅自花钱

动察 Beating AI 快讯，路透社查看了 Meta 员工的 20 多条内部反馈，发现 AI 智能体 Muse 出了不少离谱的问题。

一名员工只是在跟 Muse 聊钓鱼天气，它却突然报出两笔银行余额：Capital One 账户有 2722.58 美元，嘉信理财账户有 5899.57 美元。该员工表示，自己从没提供过银行信息，也没跟 Muse 聊过银行的事，怀疑它把别人的信息发给了自己。

另一名员工发现，Muse 突然提醒她回复姐姐在 Signal 上的私信。但她根本没有把 Signal 连接到 Muse，也不记得授权它读取其他应用。

路透社随后联合 Signal 和 AI Now Institute 进行了测试，确认 Muse 确实能绕过官方连接器，读到 Signal 的聊天内容。

在 Android 手机上，Muse 可以通过通知权限读取私信；在 Mac 上，它能调用系统辅助功能和截图工具，直接查看聊天界面。相同操作在 iPhone 上没能成功。

Muse 把用户之前授予的系统权限，用到了用户根本没想到的地方。即使没有连接 Signal，它也能通过这些权限拿到聊天内容。

Muse 还闯过其他祸。有员工反映，它擅自预订了不能退款的 Airbnb 住宿。还有人称，它把自己的宠物保险从每月 200 美元升级到了 888 美元，钱也没能追回来。

Meta 回应称，这些只是个别事件。那些看起来像是把别人信息发错账号的消息，很多其实是 AI 自己编出来的，公司已经修复了相关问题，员工测试的部分功能也并未向普通用户开放。

items.content:
In brief
- CryptoUK has urged the FCA to make clear that building or governing a DeFi protocol does not, on its own, count as carrying on a regulated activity.
- The trade group broadly backed the FCA's draft guidance on which crypto activities need authorization, but said parts go further than the underlying legislation.
- It also asked for a public register of UK-recognized stablecoins, and for the FCA to raise rules that disadvantage UK firms with the Treasury.
The UK's main crypto trade association has called on the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) to make sure that developers and governance participants in decentralized finance protocols are not treated as regulated firms by default.
CryptoUK set out its position in a response to the FCA's consultation paper CP26/36, which proposes guidance on the "perimeter" of the UK's new crypto regime: which activities fall inside it and need FCA authorization, and which don't. The group, which says it represents more than 150 crypto companies, submitted its response on Wednesday, November 18, the day the consultation closed, and published it a day later.
Yesterday, CryptoUK submitted its response to the Financial Conduct Authority’s Consultation Paper CP26/36, which proposes amendments to the Perimeter Guidance Manual (PERG) to reflect the FSMA 2000 (Cryptoassets) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026.
The consultation… pic.twitter.com/oOrZgAWscP
— CryptoUK (@CryptoUKAssoc) November 19, 2026
"Software development, maintenance, security work and participation in decentralised governance should not, by themselves, establish that a person carries on a regulated activity," CryptoUK wrote. That would be consistent with the FCA's "clear controlling person" approach to DeFi, under which regulation should hinge on who effectively controls a financial service, it argued.
'Guidance should track the legislation'
CryptoUK said it "broadly" supports the draft guidance, which reflects further amendments to the UK's crypto legislation that the government laid in September. The FCA aims to publish its final guidance in January 2027. It welcomed new exclusions from the regime for temporary settlement and payment arrangements, assets backing UK-recognized stablecoins, proprietary trading and market making, and technical service providers.
But in several places, the draft "goes further than the legislation," the group said. It pointed to a proposed link to the UK based on where a protocol is developed or governed, requirements in the exclusions for payments and proprietary trading, and indicators that would narrow the exclusion for technical services. The FCA has acknowledged that the timing of the latest amendments created uncertainty for some firms, and said it will give applicants extra time where questions over the technical services exclusion held up their applications for authorization.
ETH price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
The group asked the FCA to publish a public record of stablecoins that qualify under the UK regime, to clarify how stablecoins differ from electronic money, and to include more examples of activities that typically fall outside the perimeter.
CryptoUK also urged the FCA to raise with the Treasury outcomes that put UK firms at a disadvantage, citing the treatment of UK technical providers that offer access to regulated overseas trading venues, and of payments using stablecoins issued abroad. The UK should align with the EU's MiCA framework "where appropriate," it said. The response was prepared with law firm CMS and signed by CryptoUK policy director Nick Brooks.
A regime taking shape
The consultation is part of the FCA's work to build out the UK's crypto rulebook. The regulator finalized its core rules for crypto firms in June, ahead of a regime due to take effect on October 25, 2027, and later issued guidance two weeks before its authorization window for crypto firms opened. It has also set out a shared vision for tokenization with the Bank of England.

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Coinbase Advanced offers USDC-settled Deribit options to eligible customers in supported markets outside the United States.
- Deribit’s USDC options accounted for 1.97% of October options turnover across its reported settlement categories.
- Two matched calls showed tighter spreads in USDC and larger best offers in the coin-settled books.
Coinbase has opened a portion of Deribit’s options market to eligible customers outside the US, with contracts in Coinbase Advanced settling in USDC and falling into a product category that accounted for about 2% of Deribit’s October options turnover.
In two matched calls sampled on Nov. 19, USDC contracts had narrower spreads, while coin-settled contracts offered buyers more size at the best price.
On the same day, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong announced on X that crypto options were live for non-US users.
The Coinbase Advanced options guide names Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Hyperliquid, and XRP. All six use linear contracts, where traders pay the premium in USDC and in-the-money positions ultimately settle in the same stablecoin.
Coinbase directs customers to check eligibility in the app and complete derivatives onboarding where the service is offered. Coinbase had described a phased rollout in its earlier integration guidance.
The options rollout follows Coinbase’s Oct. 1 migration of its International Exchange (ICE) business to Deribit. The latest change lets eligible Coinbase Advanced users trade options from their existing Coinbase account, including through the app, on the infrastructure that already powers their international perpetuals.
Turnover and live quotes
Deribit’s October turnover report puts USDC options at $1.35 billion of $68.6 billion in total reported options turnover, or 1.97%. The BTC- and ETH-settled categories accounted for about $67.25 billion combined.
Deribit reports the inverse categories in dollar terms even though the contracts settle in their underlying coins.
October turnover in billions of U.S. dollars was 58.71 for BTC-settled options, 8.53 for ETH-settled options and 1.35 for USDC-settled options across assets.
The USDC category covers multiple assets, so 1.97% describes activity for the venue’s full linear category before the announcement. The price and size a customer can trade depend on the orders available for the individual strike and expiration.
CryptoSlate sampled two Nov. 27 calls on Deribit between 20:11:50 and 20:12:36 UTC on Nov. 19, matching underlying asset, strike and expiration across settlement currencies. In both cases, the USDC book had the narrower quoted gap between the highest bid and lowest ask. The coin-settled book showed more size at the price a buyer could take.
For the $64,000 Bitcoin call, the USDC book showed a 25 USDC spread and 10 BTC of underlying exposure offered at the best ask. The BTC-settled book showed a spread equivalent to $31.03 and 25.9 BTC available at its best ask.
For the $1,800 Ethereum call, the USDC book showed a 0.80 USDC spread and 150 ETH at the best ask. Its ETH-settled counterpart showed a spread equivalent to $0.88 and 1,642 ETH offered at its best ask.
The size advantage flipped for sellers trading at the best bid. At that price, buyers were seeking 20.01 BTC and 116.1 ETH of exposure in the USDC books, compared with 12.8 BTC and 29 ETH in the coin-settled books.
The two Bitcoin quotes were about 20 seconds apart, while the Ethereum quotes were about 15 seconds apart.
CryptoSlate converted coin-denominated premiums using the index price in each Deribit order-book response and compared USDC with dollars at approximate parity.
Prime opens both sets of contracts
Coinbase said on Nov. 4 that global options and perpetuals were live on Prime for eligible institutions in the US and other supported markets. Its Prime product list includes USDC-settled linear options and inverse options priced and settled in BTC or ETH, both allowing long and short positions.
Institutions must qualify as Eligible Contract Participants, complete the application and portfolio activation, and sign the clearing and Deribit agreements. Orders route through Coinbase Financial Markets and a foreign broker’s risk controls to Deribit’s matching engine.
The Prime venue terms list USDC, BTC, and ETH as collateral, with standard or portfolio margin by portfolio and settlement currency. Daily settlement takes place at 08:00 UTC, and the Global Derivatives portfolio’s margin is kept separate from spot and US derivatives.
Armstrong pointed to Coinbase Pro for US retail traders, but his post left open when those customers can trade and whether they’ll be able to reach the coin-settled books.

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
杨立昆让世界模型学会「如果当时」：只看一次结果，就能推算另一种选择

动察 Beating AI 快讯，杨立昆创办的 AMI Labs 联合布朗大学研究人员发表新论文《Counterfactual World Models》，让 JEPA 世界模型能够根据一次行动的真实结果，推算如果当时换个动作会怎样。这种能力叫「反事实推演」。

比如船向东航行，实际被暗流推偏了 2 米。模型虽然不知道暗流有多强，却能比较向东和向西两种航向的预测结果。它再把两种预测的差距，加到船实际到达的位置上，就能估算如果当时向西航行会在哪里。整个过程只有向东航行一次真实观测，向西的结果完全由模型推算。

在四个物理仿真环境中，团队借助额外训练的转换模块评估，反事实预测的 R² 从 38%–46% 提升至 86%–96%。在另一项事后规划测试中，模型找到原本能完成目标的动作的比例达到 35%–69%，对照方法只有 14%–23%。

这套方法有一个关键前提：动作和外部干扰的影响大致可以叠加。如果物体发生碰撞，或者电机故障导致不同指令受到的影响不同，预测可能失准。目前研究仍限于仿真环境，尚未验证真实机器人的实际控制效果。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/378400

⚡️马斯克开始与MAGA切割，「后悔」为共和党候选人投入超过4亿美元

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 20 日，美国中期选举后，亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克开始调整对共和党的公开表态。他不仅对民主党籍得克萨斯州当选州长吉娜·希诺霍萨（Gina Hinojosa）释放善意，还对自己为共和党候选人投入超过 4 亿美元表示后悔，并称如果能够重新选择，自己会少花一些钱。

马斯克周三在《纽约时报》DealBook 峰会上表示，自己在选举中投入大量资金，却没有看到相应回报，「这让我觉得自己相当愚蠢」。马斯克表示，支持共和党候选人的目标之一，是让华盛顿的权力保持平衡，而不是让总统、参议院和众议院都由同一个政党控制。他解释称，自己希望总统职位、众议院或参议院至少有一项由另一政党掌握。马斯克认为，美国选举并非单纯由资金决定，即使投入大量资金，对选举结果的影响也可能相对有限。

马斯克的表态与其此前对「让美国再次伟大」（MAGA）运动的支持有所区别。他在峰会上称，自己在意识形态上相当温和，并表示「我不是 MAGA」。他还说，自己并不完全认同共和党的政策主张，认为两党都有积极和消极的一面。

微信推出独立AI工具生成器：一句话做出小程序，直接在微信里用

动察 Beating AI 快讯，微信正在内测一款名为「做个小工具」的桌面应用。普通人不用写代码，只要用自然语言描述需求，就能制作自己的微信小程序。目前已推出 Windows 和 macOS 版本，仍需内测资格。

比如想做一个记账本、习惯打卡工具或待办清单，直接告诉 AI 想要什么功能，它就会自动生成界面和代码。不满意还可以继续对话修改。做好后能直接推送到微信，在手机或电脑上使用，不用额外安装 App。

微信其实早在今年 6 月就通过 AI 助手「小微」提供了类似功能，10 月又加入好友分享、安装后二次修改等能力。这次则把制作工具单独做成了电脑软件，方便用户在大屏幕上操作。

腾讯此前推出的 WorkBuddy 也能用 AI 开发小程序，但主要面向正式开发和运营，支持后端服务、提交审核和公开发布。「做个小工具」更偏向个人使用，比如给自己做个顺手的小应用，或者分享给朋友，不用走传统小程序的注册、备案和上架流程。

目前产品仍处于 Beta 阶段，尚未全面开放。

items.content:
BlackRock’s IBIT loses record $541M amid Anthropic market debut
BlackRock’s IBIT posted its largest daily outflow on record, taking three-session outflows near $900 million as BTC dipped amid a broader market selloff.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $582 million in net outflows on Thursday, led by a record withdrawal from BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).
IBIT posted $541 million in outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day withdrawal since launching in January 2024, according to Farside Investors data. The figure surpassed its previous daily record of $528.3 million, set on Jan. 30, 2026.
IBIT shares closed Thursday at $35.08, down 0.8% for the session. The shares have fallen 24.2% over the past month and 29.4% year to date, according to Yahoo Finance.
Thursday marked IBIT’s third consecutive trading day of outflows, totaling nearly $900 million. The latest streak followed a single day of inflows on Monday, which ended 11 straight sessions of withdrawals totaling roughly $2.35 billion.
The selling brought US spot Bitcoin ETFs’ November outflows to $3.47 billion, pushing their 2026 net withdrawals to approximately $3.11 billion, according to SoSoValue data.
Bitcoin (BTC) traded at around $61,875 at publishing time, down 3% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. The crypto asset was down 9.8% over the past seven days.
The ETF withdrawals coincided with a broader market selloff Thursday, as Anthropic’s highly anticipated stock market debut failed to sustain gains in AI-related stocks, including Nvidia, amid concerns over high valuations and heavy spending on artificial intelligence.
Related: Bitcoin price ignores Anthropic debut as ANT share price dips below $100
