items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.34 billion—above SpaceX's $75 billion initial offering but below its $86.25 billion expanded IPO.
- Google, Nvidia, and five other companies committed a separate $26 billion. Together with the new IPO shares, Anthropic expects $104.8 billion in net proceeds after fees.
- Behind the deal: explosive customer spending, $900.9 billion in infrastructure commitments and an OpenAI IPO potentially coming in 2027.
Anthropic has priced the largest initial IPO share sale in history at $81.34 billion, topping the $75 billion SpaceX first sold in June. But SpaceX still has the larger completed IPO after an additional share sale.
The Claude maker sold 980 million shares at $83 on Wednesday and is set to begin trading Thursday on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.
The price beat the original $70-to-$78 range, while the company increased the offering from 825 million shares. Demand was about six times the number available before pricing.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perps on Decrypt.
At $83, Anthropic is valued at roughly $1.5 trillion including stock options and other potential shares, though its value based on outstanding shares is closer to $1.1 trillion.
Where the $107 billion goes
The headline $81.34 billion isn't all money for Anthropic. About 956.35 million new shares bring $79.38 billion into the company before fees. Another 23.65 million shares, worth $1.96 billion, are being sold by its seven co-founders—roughly $280 million each. Anthropic receives none of that founders' cash, according to its final prospectus.
On top of the public sale, seven technology companies are buying $26 billion of nonvoting stock in a separate private placement. Google and Nvidia are putting in $10 billion each, AMD $2.5 billion, Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft $1 billion each, and TSMC $500 million.
The public offering and private placement total $107.34 billion in gross share sales, including the $1.96 billion going to founders rather than Anthropic.
The $104.8 billion net figure is for both transactions, not for the IPO alone. Anthropic gets $79.38 billion from its newly issued public shares, plus $26 billion from the private placement: $105.38 billion before costs. Subtract roughly $580 million in company-paid underwriting fees and estimated offering expenses, and the prospectus estimates $104.8 billion net.
That said, it could rise to about $117 billion if underwriters buy all the extra shares allowed. Anthropic plans to spend the money on operations, hiring and, above all, computing infrastructure.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley led a 22-bank underwriting group, with roughly $550 million in underwriting commissions. The company also offered access through brokers including Fidelity, Schwab, Robinhood, and SoFi, but retail investors received less than 20% of the offering.
The winners—and who still controls Anthropic
Amazon remains the largest disclosed shareholder after the transaction with about 14.6% of the company, followed by Google at roughly 13.4%.
Early financial backers also hold enormous paper fortunes. Bloomberg estimates put Lightspeed's stake near $28 billion, Iconiq's above $26 billion and Menlo Ventures' around $22 billion. Ashton Kutcher's Sound Ventures reportedly holds shares worth almost $11 billion. Those figures are estimates of stock value, not cash they received at the IPO.
Investors, however, aren't buying much control. A special share class gives the founders' holding company 50.1% of shareholder voting power, while the Long-Term Benefit Trust can appoint a majority of the board.
So, Anthropic can raise historic sums while keeping key decisions largely away from ordinary shareholders.
The business growing almost too fast to measure
Anthropic generated $33.24 billion in revenue during the first nine months of 2026, including $16.96 billion in the third quarter alone—the latest reported quarter. Its $81 billion annualized revenue run rate at the end of October projects recent customer spending over a year; it isn't money already earned.
Roughly 250 organizations now spend at least $10 million annually with Anthropic, and more than 1,900 spend at least $1 million, using trailing 12-month figures. Its net revenue retention reached about 900%.
In plain English, the same eligible customer group spent nine times as much in the latest three-month period as it did a year earlier. That measure excludes fixed-price Claude subscriptions.
But the business still depends on a few major accounts and distribution partners. Its five biggest customers generated about 25% of revenue over the first nine months of 2026, while cloud marketplaces accounted for 44%. In other words, companies like Amazon, Google and Microsoft can invest in Anthropic, provide the machines it runs on and help sell access to Claude.
Even the product changes at extraordinary speed: Claude models released during the six months through September made up more than 80% of third-quarter revenue. At the end of September 2026, Anthropic had about 5,300 employees and was generating more than $6.6 million in trailing annual revenue per employee.
An enormous business with an even bigger bill
Rapid growth doesn't mean easy profits. Anthropic posted a $567 million operating loss in the third quarter of 2026, after a $974 million operating profit in the second quarter. Over the first nine months, its operating loss totaled $1.26 billion. Those numbers tell a very different story from its much bigger headline net loss.
In the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic posted a $104.04 billion net loss, including $94.3 billion in noncash revaluations of convertible financing and related instruments. Yet it generated $6.57 billion in cash from operating activities during the same period. That is not free cash flow, which also accounts for capital spending, but the distinction matters: a $104 billion accounting loss does not mean $104 billion of cash burned.
The latest balance sheet, dated September 30, 2026, shows $95.6 billion in cash and equivalents plus $36.3 billion in short-term investments—$131.85 billion combined. Convertible notes payable stood at $130.50 billion at their accounting value, with some converting into shares around the IPO.
The final prospectus estimates $232.35 billion in cash and short-term investments on a pro forma, post-transaction basis. That last figure is a modeled balance after the offering and related adjustments, not cash the company held on September 30.
The more consequential number may be what it has promised to spend next. Anthropic disclosed about $900.9 billion in commitments, overwhelmingly for computing and infrastructure, stretching as far as 2045.
It separately estimates another $150 billion to $175 billion in payments under arrangements without fixed dollar amounts. Together, that points to potentially more than $1 trillion—but it is not a bill due today, and some contracts are conditional or can be terminated.
Some $70.7 billion of the stated commitments fall due in the 12 months after September 2026. That explains why even an IPO this large is not necessarily excessive capital for a frontier AI company. Every breakthrough attracts customers, but serving them requires more chips, power, and data centers.
What the SpaceX record means for OpenAI
There is a technical catch to the record. SpaceX's June IPO initially sold $75 billion in shares, but the final deal reached $86.25 billion gross after underwriters bought more shares—about $85.675 billion after fees, according to SpaceX's SEC filing.
Anthropic's $81.34 billion beats SpaceX's initial deal, not its final gross total. The extra $26 billion from Anthropic's private placement cannot be counted as public IPO proceeds. Its own option covers another 147 million shares worth about $12.2 billion; if exercised in full, its public IPO would reach $93.54 billion, comfortably above SpaceX's final figure.
Now attention turns to OpenAI. The ChatGPT maker recently raised $11 billion at a reported $1.25 trillion valuation and has indicated it will not list before 2027. Anthropic's debut offers a public-market test of what investors are willing to pay for AI revenue, while exposing the cost of generating it.
The interesting part isn't just that a five-year-old AI lab topped SpaceX's initial IPO. It's that it assembled more than $100 billion in combined public and private financing, started generating cash from operations—and still faces a potential trillion-dollar computing bill.

Foresight News 消息，NEAR 发文表示，在 9 月 Bitget 遭黑客攻击后，其安全系统 SHIELD 检测并拦截了试图通过 NEAR Intents 洗钱的相关资金流的 99.7%，金额超过 5000 万美元。另外，NEAR 援引独立链上追踪数据称，币安漏洞利用事件发生后两天内，攻击者通过跨链桥和兑换平台跨链转移了价值约 1.94 亿美元的 TRON 代币，其中约 17.1 万美元通过 NEAR Intents。NEAR 表示，截至 11 月 3 日，SHIELD 已拦截约 96% 试图通过 NEAR Intents 的币安事件相关资金流。SHIELD 根据资金在来源链上的公开交易历史，结合反洗钱数据库、第三方情报及合作伙伴信号，在交易执行前筛查并阻止高风险资金流。该机制仅作用于 NEAR Intents，可针对特定链、代币或地址采取限制，不影响 NEAR 底层协议的无需许可属性。

Anthropic IPO料造就数百名亿美元富豪，员工人均持股价值约4400万美元

动察 Beating AI 快讯，据《财富》报道，按 Anthropic 每股 83 美元的 IPO 发行价计算，公司 5300 名员工合计持有的股权估值约为 2320 亿美元，折合人均约 4400 万美元。

至少 400 名早期员工的身家将达到 1 亿美元或以上，其中部分人可能加入公司七名联合创始人的行列，成为亿万富豪。非创始人员工在首个交易日最多可出售个人持股的 10%，公司公布 2026 年业绩后，另有 35% 的个人持股将获得出售资格。

此次 IPO 对 Anthropic 的估值为 1.5 万亿美元，按上市估值衡量，规模位居历史第二，仅次于 SpaceX 的 1.77 万亿美元。不过，按募资额计算，Anthropic 的 810 亿美元超过了 SpaceX 的 750 亿美元。

七名联合创始人的持股比例相对均衡，预计每人的身家将大致翻倍至约 199 亿美元。七人均已承诺将个人所持 Anthropic 股权的 80% 用于慈善事业，相关承诺对应的价值可能超过 1000 亿美元。

与此同时，CEO Dario Amodei 曾在今年 1 月发表的文章中警告，AI 带来的巨额财富可能集中到足以破坏社会的程度。他将 AI 热潮与美国镀金时代相比较，认为处于 AI 经济繁荣前沿的人，应愿意放弃部分财富与权力，并向社会回馈。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- The Nov. 18 census linked 7.16 million BTC to public keys or scripts already on-chain, equal to 35.6% of unspent bitcoin at block 975,019.
- About 73% of the tally came from historical matches, including roughly 1.93 million BTC in script-hash formats.
- Planning a future quantum migration would require checking which spending paths depend on public keys that are already visible.
A Bitcoin census published Nov. 18 linked 7.16 million unspent BTC to public keys or scripts already visible on-chain. It counted some outputs because they contain key data by design and others because their hashes matched tables built from earlier on-chain data. Together they accounted for 35.6% of the BTC in unspent outputs at block 975,019.
Researcher duncan0k published the census on Delving Bitcoin, tallying 7,164,754 BTC out of 20,109,207 BTC in unspent outputs. About 1.94 million BTC qualified by format alone, across pay-to-public-key, Taproot and bare multisig outputs. Those formats put key data in the output itself. The census counted them in full, including a small amount in outputs that failed its key validity check.
The other 5.23 million BTC, about 73% of the tally, came from matching hashes in unspent outputs to older blockchain data. About 3.30 million BTC of that sat in two formats that use a hash of a public key. Another 1.93 million BTC sat in two script-hash formats, which record a fingerprint of the instructions for spending the coins.
What the Bitcoin census counts as a script match
A script-hash match is a clue to how the coins can be spent. When it identifies a revealed script, a reviewer can check which signatures a spending path requires and whether the corresponding public keys are already visible. Some paths require no signature at all. Those distinctions matter if future quantum computers become capable of breaking the signatures Bitcoin uses today.
The extraction rules describe two ways the scan counted script-hash balances. A pay-to-script-hash output can match a previously revealed script or an entry derived from a known public key. The other script-hash format uses a separate table that also includes some hashes derived from Taproot script data.
The researcher compared those rules with draft BIP 362, a proposal to classify exposure in existing Bitcoin outputs. Compared with the draft version reviewed, the scan skipped some revealed scripts and included some broader matches. The net effect is unmeasured. Keys or scripts behind outputs outside the tally could still have been disclosed off-chain or in on-chain locations the scan skipped.
Glassnode’s May study measured a different kind of visibility. It reported 6.04 million BTC, or 30.2% of issued supply, using visibility of the public key needed for a spend as its test. The November census includes script matches and divides by BTC in unspent outputs. Measuring a change over time would require a common definition and denominator.
To turn the new census into priorities for a future migration, researchers would need to examine the matched outputs and identify where a spending path depends on a visible, usable key.
items.title: Over 7 million Bitcoin could face a quantum security reckoning after new discovery

Food was also a lot of effort (and on the busy days women would be next to the men), but there is a lot more down time for men to do other needed work. The primitive sexism above isn't required when you rebu...

[jmathai]: I think this topic and related explorations are interesting as it pertains to rebuilding communities. A related project is Open Source Ecology (terrible name), which aims to make the tools necessary to rebuild society accessible to everyone. items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Anthropic-linked futures traded around $104 on Nov. 19, about 25% above the company’s $83 IPO price.
- Token Terminal tracked a record $186 million in open interest on Hyperliquid before the listing, with nearly three traders long for every trader short.
- Block Scholes found that moves in tech stocks, gold, the dollar and Treasury yields lined up with much of Bitcoin’s decline.
Crypto futures tied to Anthropic traded about 25% above the company’s IPO price on Thursday. The bets swelled during a Bitcoin selloff, but research from Block Scholes points to a broader retreat from risk rather than clear evidence that investors sold Bitcoin to buy Anthropic.
Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 on Nov. 18, above its initial $70 to $78 range. The base offering totaled $81 billion, including shares sold by existing holders, and valued the company at about $1.5 trillion. It surpassed SpaceX’s June IPO. Anthropic set Nov. 19 as the expected Nasdaq debut for its shares under the symbol ANT.
Ten offerings reproduced from an App Economy Insights graphic. Gross proceeds at IPO, rounded to the nearest $1 billion in the image; not corporate valuations. Excludes over-allotment options and secondary listings. Agricultural Bank of China and ICBC include both Hong Kong and Shanghai tranches. Historical exact amounts differ slightly because of rounding and source conventions.
Across 19 venues, the median price for Anthropic-linked perpetual futures was about $104 at 14:18 UTC on Nov. 19, roughly 25% above the $83 offer price, OptimistFi reported. The contracts track a reference price and do not give holders ownership of Anthropic shares.
Bitcoin had tested support near $62,000 twice by Thursday as traders watched for signs of returning demand.
What drove Bitcoin’s selloff?
In research shared with CryptoSlate, crypto derivatives analytics firm Block Scholes found that Bitcoin’s selloff broadly tracked weakness across other markets.
The firm's research analyst, Thahbib Rahman, examined Bitcoin's relationship with the Nasdaq-100 between January and September and found that a 1% move in the technology-heavy index corresponded, on average, with a 1.03% move in BTC in the same direction.
Block Scholes estimated an 11% Bitcoin decline from the Nasdaq-100’s performance alone. Including changes in gold, the US dollar and Treasury yields raised the model’s estimate to 14%, still short of the 22% drop the firm used for comparison.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $3 billion in net outflows in November through Nov. 18, according to daily fund-flow data from Farside Investors.
The firm's analysis of previous stock market listings also challenges the capital-flight narrative.
Among 17 US IPOs that raised at least $900 million this year, Bitcoin declined during the preceding 50 days in nine cases, showing no consistent pattern of selling ahead of major offerings.
Crypto traders valued Anthropic at up to $1.8 trillion before its listing
While Bitcoin has struggled, cryptocurrency derivatives markets have experienced a surge in trading tied to Anthropic's valuation.
Token Terminal reported that traders had speculated on Anthropic through perpetual futures on Hyperliquid for more than a year.
These markets valued the AI company at approximately $339 billion a year ago. By Nov. 18, the implied valuation had climbed to between $1.7 trillion and $1.8 trillion, well above the $1.5 trillion valuation established by the IPO.
Cash-settled Hyperliquid perpetuals, not Anthropic shares, through Nov. 18, 2026. tradeXYZ and Paragon per-share contracts converted assuming 18B shares; Entropy and Ventuals quote valuation directly. Ventuals history between annotated $339B opening and $1.61T close approximated from the screenshot ($20B rounding). Entropy and tradeXYZ daily history comes from independent Hyperliquid data, not Token Terminal exports. Entropy Nov. 16-17 is screenshot-estimated; Nov. 18 is annotated. Paragon has only a Nov. 18 figure. IPO $1.5T is a rounded retrospective benchmark; null means unavailable.
Token Terminal data showed that open interest in Anthropic-linked perpetuals reached an all-time high of $186 million on Nov. 18, with all the previous week's net growth concentrated on trade[XYZ], which launched its Anthropic market on Oct. 26.
Daily trading volume peaked at $261 million on Nov. 10, coinciding with the announcement of Anthropic's initial IPO pricing range.
Bullish participation also accelerated. On Nov. 18, Token Terminal recorded 5,567 traders holding long positions, compared with 1,996 holding short positions, a nearly three-to-one ratio.
On OKX, Anthropic’s pre-IPO perpetual initially traded near 130 USDC when the company’s roadshow began, about 67% above the top of the proposed range. The run-up followed earlier leveraged bets on Anthropic’s IPO in September.
The contract subsequently declined toward 98 USDC as bankers raised the offering price, before recovering above 103 USDC following Wednesday's final pricing announcement.
Erald Ghoos, CEO of OKX Europe, told CryptoSlate that the divergence reflected a disagreement between traditional financial institutions and crypto traders over the company's valuation.
Ghoos said:
“For 10 days, traders and bankers disagreed about what Anthropic is worth. The bankers moved up to $83. Traders still think that's too low, by about 24%.”
The executive pointed to SpaceX's June listing, when pre-IPO derivatives traded within 4% of the company's eventual first-day closing price, while the stock's IPO price was approximately 16% below that close.
Block Scholes also reported growing activity on Hyperliquid, where Anthropic-linked perpetuals averaged approximately $75 million in daily trading volume since Nov. 5, up from $7 million in September.
However, those contracts represented only about 1% of Hyperliquid's overall trading volume and roughly 3% of the increase in non-crypto trading since September.
The benchmarks for Anthropic’s first day on Nasdaq are the $83 IPO price and the roughly $104 futures quote. The gap is what traders bet on, not what public-market investors paid.
items.title: Anthropic’s crypto futures traded 25% above its $81 billion IPO price as Bitcoin slumped 22%

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
STRC, the stock that Michael Saylor’s Strategy wants to hold near $100 while paying ultra-high dividends, closed Wednesday at its lowest finish since August 20 and 3.9% below that $100 target.
It’s falling despite a war chest of expenditures by Strategy, including last week’s $228 million STRC buy-back, and depleting its STRC rescue fund by 89%.
Saylor proclaimed in May that keeping STRC near $100 per share was “the company’s number one business objective.”
As usual, shareholders of Strategy’s MSTR common stock suffered dilution to provide rescue funds for STRC preferreds, including $206 million of last week’s $228 million buy-back.
As of November 15, only $332 million remained of the $3 billion that Strategy’s board of directors authorized for STRC repurchases; 89% is gone.
Michael Saylor’s bull market never came
On October 29, Saylor declared, “We’re at the beginning of the next bitcoin bull market.” Since then, BTC has fallen 19%. Worse, MSTR is down 36%.
Strategy owns 850,849 BTC that it bought for $64.2 billion. At Wednesday evening’s price, those coins were worth about $53.3 billion for an unrealized loss of $10.9 billion.
Worse, Strategy has spent more than $1 billion in expenses operating this unrealized loss-generating colossus.
Notably, and although corporate cash does not reduce an unrealized capital loss, the company does have $4.9 billion in cash that it could — but probably won’t — use to offset roughly half of that loss.
All of these failures, for context, exist because Saylor believed BTC would somehow achieve a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) near 30%.
Instead, over the past five years, BTC has only rallied 7% in total.
MSTR has only rallied 24% over the same time period — rewarding patient investors with less than a single year’s worth of Saylor’s 30% annual target, despite faithfully waiting half a decade.
Read more: Michael Saylor’s STRC has been off parity for five months
$1 billion to operate a company generating $10+ billion unrealized losses
Saylor posted on Wednesday, “Seller exhaustion will come long before Saylor exhaustion.”
It helps that Saylor, unlike his common shareholders, receives executive perks regardless of the underperformance of MSTR, STRC, and BTC.
Saylor, unlike his shareholders, is in the business of selling stock. He wants people to buy what his company sells: MSTR.
Strategy has a scheduled investor Q&A with Saylor and CEO Phong Le on Thursday at 5pm New York time.
Protos reported on October 1 that 64% of an earlier, $2 billion STRC rescue fund was expended as of Strategy’s September 28 filing. Strategy subsequently increased its authorization by $1 billion and spent roughly $1.4 billion more, enabled mostly by MSTR dilution.

items.author: Andjela Radmilac
items.content:
Quick Take
- Anthropic priced its record $81 billion IPO at $83 per share ahead of its Nasdaq debut.
- The ECB warned that IPO booms have historically been followed by weaker stock returns and could complicate AI financing.
- Bitcoin traders are watching for broader market volatility as Anthropic begins trading and AI stock valuations face scrutiny.
Anthropic priced its $81 billion IPO at $83 a share Wednesday. The company behind Claude said it expected trading to begin on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. If the stock opens above $83, investors who got shares in the offering will have an immediate gain on paper. Anthropic won't get any extra cash from that move.
The net result is that Anthropic has effectively raised $81.3 billion from its public offering, with a further $26 billion private placement. This creates a $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation despite growing concerns over AI infrastructure spending and financing risks.
The European Central Bank warned Wednesday that stock returns have tended to weaken after a rush of companies going public. Its concern is what happens when the rush ends: AI companies may still have data centers to finish and bills to pay, but could find it harder to raise cash if stock prices fall and lenders pull back. For Bitcoin and the broader crypto industry, the question is whether a pullback in AI shares becomes a wider selloff in risk assets, not whether the IPO itself takes money out of crypto.
Why a rush of IPOs gets the ECB's attention
US initial public offerings brought in about $44 billion in 2025. In its November financial stability review, the ECB cited a July analyst forecast of about $225 billion for all of 2026, alongside its staff's separate $212 billion estimate from early November. Both were made before Anthropic set its final price.
Rounded annual US IPO proceeds. 2025 is reported historical activity; the two 2026 bars are separate full-year forecasts, not additive amounts or completed offerings. The ECB staff estimate was prepared in early November using actual January–October proceeds, a seasonal forecast, and preliminary Anthropic inputs. The market-analyst projection dates to July. Both predate Anthropic’s final Nov. 18 pricing.
It's easier to see why offerings tend to bunch together from the company's side. If investors are willing to pay more for each share, a company can raise the same amount of cash by selling a smaller piece of itself. Other companies see those terms and have a reason to get their own deals done before demand cools.
The ECB compared the size of each quarter's IPOs relative to the economy with what the broader stock market returned over the next two years. In the US, higher issuance went with weaker returns, but the relationship accounted for only about a tenth of the variation. It tells us more about the conditions in which companies choose to sell shares than it does about where Anthropic will trade this afternoon.
Selling shares gives a company cash it doesn't have to repay. If the price drops, shareholders take the loss, and the company keeps the money it already raised. The trouble starts when a business still needs money to finish building and has fewer ways to raise it. Borrowers still owe interest, and AI companies can still owe rent for computing space they no longer need. When a data-center operator borrows against its tenants' payments, the people buying those data-center bonds are counting on the tenants to keep paying.
The ECB’s review of AI borrowing extends that risk beyond shareholders: if lenders start doubting projects will bring in enough cash, they can charge more or stop funding new ones, even as falling stock prices make raising money by selling shares more expensive. The ECB said the issuance surge and the rise of passive investing do not currently pose a systemic risk.
Where the $81 billion goes
When a company goes public, it sells newly created shares to raise money, and people who already own shares can sell some of theirs in the same deal. Anthropic will be doing both.
Its final terms cover 980 million shares at $83 each. About $79 billion goes to Anthropic for the new shares and $2 billion goes to existing shareholders, before fees in both cases. That excludes an option for the banks running the deal to buy up to 147 million additional shares. Anthropic also arranged a separate $26 billion private placement with strategic partners, contingent on the IPO closing.
Gross proceeds at the $83 offer price: $79.38 billion for Anthropic and $1.96 billion for selling stockholders, totaling $81.34 billion before underwriting discounts and other expenses. Calculated from the final share allocation. Excludes the underwriters’ option to buy 147 million additional shares; does not represent money raised through subsequent Nasdaq trading.
- Anthropic: new sharesUSD 79.38B97.6%
- Selling stockholders: existing sharesUSD 1.96B2.4%
Those banks are the underwriters. They take indications of how many shares investors want and what they're willing to pay, then help the company set the price and decide who gets shares. Under the deal's underwriting terms, the banks agree to buy the shares from Anthropic and the selling shareholders and resell them to investors. They're paid through a discount: the banks pay the sellers less per share than the investors pay. If you got an allocation, you were assigned a number of shares at $83. If you buy after trading starts, you pay the market price, and the money goes to the investor selling you the shares.
The money Anthropic gets from selling new stock gives it more room to pay for the equipment and computing capacity it needs to run Claude. Its IPO filing puts expected payments on contractual commitments at $71 billion over the 12 months after Sept. 30, including $4 billion tied to arrangements with conditions or termination rights. Those are primarily commitments for computing and infrastructure, not a loan coming due or a bill the IPO was specifically set up to pay.
The company also reported $147 billion in liquidity as of Sept. 30, before the IPO and private placement, so the commitments do not by themselves indicate an immediate cash shortfall. They give a sense of why access to funding counts long after the first trade. The stock is due to start trading Thursday, while Anthropic expects the offering itself to close Friday if the usual conditions are met.
What to watch when Anthropic starts trading
Anthropic is due to trade under the ticker ANT. Nasdaq's regular session starts at 9:30 a.m. New York time, but the stock doesn't have to open at that hour. The exchange runs an opening auction for IPOs, collecting buy and sell orders and finding the price at which the most shares can change hands. The first trade tells you how that initial batch of orders matched. The closing price will show whether buyers were still willing to pay as much after a session of trading.
Index funds can bring another set of buyers later. These funds aim to match a specified list of stocks, so when an index adds a company, the funds that follow it generally adjust their holdings. MSCI says Anthropic would enter its broad investable market indexes at the Nov. 30 close, effective Dec. 1, if it qualifies for early entry. Which funds would buy depends on the exact index each one tracks.
The ECB found that companies already on the market tended to sell more stock when index funds owned a larger share of them. Its researchers think the prospect of those buyers arriving soon after listing could help some companies raise more at their IPO, too. They didn't estimate how much of Anthropic's $83 price came from that expectation.
Crypto traders already have contracts tied to Anthropic's share price. The Nasdaq debut gives them an actual share price to compare those contracts with. Bitcoin‘s 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq-100 stood at 0.7 in Talos's Nov. 12 report, pointing to sensitivity to the same shifts in investor risk appetite. But a move in both on Thursday wouldn't establish that investors sold Bitcoin to buy ANT.
Even a strong first day would tell us only what buyers were willing to pay for Anthropic now. The ECB's warning is about whether AI companies can still raise cash on reasonable terms when investors are less eager, and the bills are still coming due.
items.title: Anthropic hits $1.5 trillion valuation in record IPO as ECB warns AI funding could dry up

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Some 21% of Gen Z adults own crypto, compared with 16% who have an employer retirement plan and 3% of baby boomers who own crypto, according to SoFi’s survey.
- Only 13% of all Americans own crypto, 62% are firm skeptics, and 77% call it a “side quest” they don’t have time or energy for.
- SoFi argues that offering crypto through banks would boost adoption, with 63% of current investors saying they’d trade more at their primary bank.
For many young Americans, crypto is coming before the 401(k).
Some 21% of Gen Z adults own cryptocurrency, compared with 16% who hold an employer-sponsored retirement plan like a 401(k), according to a survey released Thursday by SoFi Technologies.
That’s seven times the rate of baby boomers, just 3% of whom own crypto. Crypto was Gen Z’s most widely held investment in the survey, ahead of stocks, bonds ,and real estate.
The online survey of 2,064 U.S. adults was conducted by SoFi and YouGov from Oct. 15 to 28. SoFi, a nationally chartered bank that sells crypto alongside checking and investment accounts, developed the report with Culture Co-op.
Gen Z respondents described crypto less as a gamble than a strategy. They were nearly three times as likely as the general population to call it one of the best ways to build future wealth, 21% vs. 8%, and 61% said they see it as a financial advantage unique to their generation.
Only 20% of Gen Z crypto owners said they bought in because it “sounded interesting,” compared with 34% of crypto investors overall. Diversification (32%) and easier international payments (29%) ranked higher.
Part of the gap reflects age. Many respondents in their late teens and 20s don’t yet have access to an employer retirement plan.
Across the broader population, the picture is far cooler. Only 13% of Americans own crypto, and 62% are firm skeptics. Three in four say crypto feels intimidating to get into, and 77% agreed with the statement, “Cryptocurrency feels like a financial side quest that I don’t have the time or energy for.”
Even owners feel out of their depth: 82% of current crypto investors said they should know more about it than they do, and 11% admitted knowing little to nothing.
“Nobody feels the gaps in their financial education more sharply than someone who has just bought Bitcoin,” said Natalie Brunell, host of the Coin Stories podcast and a contributor to SoFi’s crypto newsletter.
The findings echo a recent survey conducted by Ipsos for the DeFi Education Fund, which found that 22% of Americans have ever owned or used crypto but only 13% used it in the past year.
SoFi argues that putting crypto in the same app as banking is the key to wider adoption. Half of respondents open to crypto said having their primary bank offer it would be a tipping point, and 63% of current investors said they’d trade more if they could do it at their bank.
SoFi has been building out that model, launching a tokenized deposit that pays 4.4% and moves like a stablecoin, as well as a bank-issued stablecoin running on Polygon’s payments infrastructure.
The survey also challenges the crypto “tech bro” stereotype. Black and Hispanic respondents own crypto at more than twice the rate of white respondents, 22% to 9%. Miami led the 10 cities surveyed at 20% ownership, while San Francisco matched the national average at 13%.

items.author: Bennett Tomlin
items.content:
Anthropic’s IPO today will be one of the largest in history, both in terms of the amount raised and in the valuation of the firm itself.
The AI giant expects to offer its shares at a price of $83, valuing it at over $1 trillion, upsized from its original filings.
Additionally, Anthropic is offering an additional placement of its Class N (non-voting) shares to certain partners that would raise an additional $26 billion.
In total, if underwriters also take advantage of their opportunity to purchase additional shares, then the prospectus predicts the Anthropic IPO will have net proceeds of “approximately $117.0 billion.”
Anthropic’s valuation at the time of IPO will be less than SpaceX’s.
Read more: Anthropic was keeping its IPO share price secret — footnote reveals $71.43
Anthropic’s founders have structured things so that they’ll maintain more than 50% of the votes in the firm, using an entity called Founder LLC.
This is despite the fact that they’ll own a much smaller portion, aided by the extra votes of their special Class F shares.
The founders also have their own Class A shares that also give them additional votes.
Anthropic’s Financials
Anthropic will be heading into this IPO with massive losses totaling over $100 billion for the year so far. These are mostly accounting-driven and related to convertible notes.
When you take Anthropic’s adjustments into account, the last two quarters have both had a positive adjusted net income.
Anthropic has also claimed that its revenue has passed what it spends on compute, though for the most recent quarter its compute bill grew approximately 77%, while its revenue grew “only” 47%.
However, in absolute terms, its revenue still grew faster than the spending on compute.
Anthropic’s partnerships do have a cost, though.
In many cases, the company has committed to spending tens of billions with these firms like Amazon, Google, and Broadcom.
Interestingly, for the year so far, Anthropic discloses that approximately 5-7% of its revenue came from customers who were eventually found to be breaking the rules, and it warned, “Customers may evade our controls, and customers whose access is restricted or terminated may re-register under new accounts.
“As a result, revenue from such customers may continue or recur notwithstanding our enforcement efforts.”
Anthropic further disclosed that its “top five customers represented approximately 25% of our revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.”
It also disclosed that approximately 71% of its revenue came from the US.
Read more: Anthropic outranks most IPOs in history
Super-intelligence
One of the fascinating changes that has come about as this S-1 has been amended is related to its usage of “Super Intelligence.”
The original S-1 didn’t use the term “Super Intelligence” or “SI” to describe any part of its business. Its only use of the term being the name of the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence.
However, its most recent amended version does use the term.
Now it notes, “For purposes of this prospectus, to avoid confusion, we use the terms ‘super intelligence,’ ‘SI,’ ‘artificial intelligence,’ and ‘AI’ interchangeably.
On September 29, 2026, the US president issued Executive Order 14434, which directs federal executive departments and agencies to use the terms ‘Super Intelligence’ and ‘SI’ in place of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI.'”
What are the risks?
Anthropic’s S-1 for this IPO includes many risks, some of which are boilerplate, but it also notes some interesting risks.
These include:
- “Our models have in the past behaved, and may in the future behave, in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways, including by taking harmful actions that no user or third party directed”
- “The political environment and our engagement with policymakers and public positions on AI regulation and safety could subject us to heightened scrutiny, political backlash, or disproportionate regulatory action”
- “Our sales to government entities and highly regulated organizations are subject to challenges and risks”
- “Unfavorable media coverage regarding our business, our models, platform, and applications, the impacts of AI, and the AI industry more broadly could adversely affect our business”
- “Many of the risks we face are interconnected and may compound or trigger cascading adverse effects across our business, which could amplify their overall impact.”
SpaceX
One of the inevitable comparisons for Anthropic is SpaceX, another massive recent IPO in the AI industry.
For one thing, both firms have connections to another AI heavyweight, OpenAI.
Elon Musk, who leads SpaceX, was previously the OpenAI co-chair and would eventually merge xAI into SpaceX.
Similarly, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was previously OpenAI’s vice president of research.
Daniela Amodei, the president and chair of Anthropic, was previously OpenAI’s vice president of safety.
SpaceX and Anthropic are also linked because Anthropic buys substantial amounts of compute that Anthropic purchases from SpaceX.
Read more: DoorDash has outperformed SpaceX by 48% since IPO
More than one-third of SpaceX revenue for quarter three came from this “Customer B,” its unnamed customer who’s spending lines up with Anthropic.
The two firms are also similar in other ways, even raising similar amounts in their IPO.
In both cases, the founders have kept voting control of their firms.
Both even had similar revenue in quarter three of this year.
FTX
People have inevitably brought up Sam Bankman-Fried’s theft from his customers when they talk about Anthropic.
One of the dozens of investments he made with stolen funds was in Anthropic. The initial increase in value of this firm was one of the things that made it possible for customers to receive back the amount they had in dollar amounts on the day of bankruptcy despite the billions in misappropriated funds.
Caroline Ellison and Nishad Singh also had equity in Anthropic but forfeited it after they pleaded guilty.
Read more: Manifund hires Caroline Ellison while fighting FTX over $1.5M
Those shares would, of course, be worth even more now than then, but that doesn’t change the fundamental nature of the crime.
Protos will be following this Anthropic IPO as it develops over its first day.

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- The International Organization of Securities Commissions warned that a sufficiently capable quantum computer could undermine the cryptography that protects financial markets.
- IOSCO said such machines don't yet exist, citing conservative estimates of 2030 to 2035, while some industry participants urged firms to plan for five years.
- It flagged blockchains as particularly hard to migrate, with post-quantum signatures 35 to 40 times larger and upgrades requiring hard forks.
Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) said in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.
"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais said in a statement.
The 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.
Blockchains face a heavier lift
IOSCO said the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day."
Swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report said. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.
Because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO said. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.
Wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has said. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.
The report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.
Layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report said.
Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.
'Crypto-agility'
IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to update cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.
Most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.
No surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO said it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.
Quantum hardware is advancing quickly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has said it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Christina Comben
items.content:
Ethereum’s new DeFi security tool raises questions over censorship
Phylax’s system lets decentralized protocols block potentially harmful transactions, but raises questions about potential censorship and Ethereum’s concentrated builder market.
Phylax’s new security system could help decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols stop malicious transactions before they settle.
That may bolster crypto’s defenses against North Korean hackers and United States-sanctioned actors, but it may also introduce a way to freeze smart contract functions without explicitly giving anyone the power to do so.
And that’s the kind of control that raises concerns the system could end up as a centralized tool for law enforcement rather than decentralized finance.
“The question is not just whether there is risk, but if it’s acceptable risk,” says Stefanie Boss, co-author of research on censorship resistance and compliance behavior in Ethereum’s consensus mechanism.
“In this case, I’d lean toward that it is acceptable, as the goal is to make the network safer and more aligned with the network and application values,” she says.
A security mechanism with a potential freeze risk
Announced on Nov. 10, Phylax’s integration with block builder Titan Builder, allows Ethereum applications to define rules that exclude transactions that may produce harmful outcomes during block construction.
Titan, which Phylax says produces one in every two Ethereum blocks, checks transactions against those rules before including them in its blocks.
The idea is to prevent exploits from settling rather than relying on monitoring systems or emergency interventions after an attack has begun. “Our mission: stop users from losing money to hacks and errors in DeFi,” the announcement said.
Related: Fears of AI-driven DeFi hack epidemic overstated for now — but not for long
In a blog Phylax uses the scenario of a vulnerable vault that could mistakenly release $1 million to a user whose shares are only worth $1,000. With the system in operation, a circuit breaker could cap the amount leaving the vault in a single transaction, preventing the funds from being drained.
Similar safeguards could also potentially limit losses in major hacks like the $6.3 billion Binance hack or the $380 million Bitget exploit, where malicious actors drained exchange wallets and were able to move large amounts of crypto through decentralized protocols.
Phylax says hacks should not settle. Source: Phylax Systems.
While preventing malicious transactions would be a win for the crypto space, digital assets lawyer Gabriel Shapiro warned that applications using the system could become effectively freezable if builders stopped providing the required attestations.
He explained that smart contracts can be configured to reject transactions unless they are included in blocks from builders that have performed the required security checks. If those builders stopped providing attestations, protected functions could keep rejecting transactions until they resumed.
Related: DeFi TVL drops 39% in 2026 amid market downturn and record hack activity
Phylax founder and chief executive Odysseas Lamtzidis says protocols can avoid that risk by allowing transactions to go through even when the system’s security checks are unavailable.
“The sane default we provide and suggest to protocols is a fail-open behavior,” he tells Magazine.
But that safeguard is optional, leaving individual protocols to decide how much priority to give security over availability. “Some protocols might choose to prioritize safety over liveness,” Lamtzidis says.
He also says protocols can decide whether their smart contracts are immutable or can be changed through governance.
Shapiro says fail-open protections should be mandatory and changes to the safeguards should be subject to time delays to prevent protocols from removing them immediately.
Ethereum’s builder concentration problem
There is also a broader concern about whether the system could reinforce Ethereum’s already heavily concentrated block-building market.
Fan Zhang, an Ethereum researcher, says Phylax’s technology is only becoming practical now because of that concentration. “We finally have a way to implement this effectively,” he says, “but sadly only because of how centralized Ethereum’s builder market has become.”
Zhang says Phylax’s approach has “appealing security benefits, especially in the age of AI bots being able to find bugs faster than ever.”
But he warns that introducing additional code at such a critical point in transaction processing creates new failure modes, including implementation errors and builder signing-key theft, loss or impersonation.
“I think the community is very concerned about centralized builders and is making efforts to address them. So I’m concerned that these efforts may undermine each other,” he adds.
Related: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack
Ethereum researcher Sen Yang tells Magazine, “If major protocols rely on a small number of builders for security enforcement, this could give those builders a competitive advantage and further exacerbate market concentration.”
Phylax announces its circuit breaker system. Source: Phylax Systems
He says Ethereum’s proposed enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS) upgrade, slated for inclusion in the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade, may reduce reliance on third-party relays, “but it does not directly address builder market concentration.’’
Yang says transactions excluded by dominant builders could still be included by non-censoring builders, potentially causing delays rather than permanent exclusion.
Where does security become censorship?
Phylax argues that its system does not introduce a new authority over Ethereum transactions because applications themselves define the rules. The technology is “explicitly opt-in,” Lamtzidis says.
He compares the checks to conditions already written into smart contracts. “It’s no different than a ‘require()’ statement,” he says. “Censorship implies arbitrary decision-making or coercion.”
Zhang makes a similar distinction between applications voluntarily filtering transactions and external parties imposing censorship. “Applications willingly signing up for filtering is fine, as a user can walk away from such applications,” he says. “It’s externally forced censorship that’s the problem. That’s where I’ll draw the line.”
Boss says rules targeting a transaction’s outcome are less concerning than those targeting who is making it. “In this case, it is also result-driven, which is often considered less risky,” she says.
She considers the security objective legitimate, arguing that “the harm of those hacks is much higher than the harm of this type of exclusion.”
But she warns that rules could also be used to enforce sanctions or politically motivated exclusions.
“It is important to ensure that there are proper safeguards in place to make sure that these rules will remain fair and designed for security,” she says.

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin rebounded from roughly $62,000 on Nov. 15 and 18, with the second session closing nearer its low.
- Glassnode’s relative loss reading reached levels seen near past lows, while CryptoQuant put 30-day net losses at $8 billion.
- Easing daily losses, a narrower Coinbase discount and sustained spot buying would strengthen the case that the rebound can hold.
The Bitcoin rebound from just above $62,000 was weaker the second time. The bounces came on Nov. 15 and 18, and the second session closed closer to its low. By then, a CryptoQuant measure showed the steepest losses since mid-August on older coins that moved. The next question is whether spot buyers can absorb that pressure for more than a day.
The Nov. 15 and Nov. 18 lows were $62,006 and $62,063 on CoinGlass’s Binance BTC/USDT daily candles, which start at midnight UTC. Bitcoin finished the first day at $65,351 and the second at $63,068.
In a Nov. 19 analysis for CryptoQuant, Woominkyu put 30-day net realized losses at $8 billion, well short of two earlier 2026 readings. Glassnode’s Nov. 17 report found losses at levels it had seen around past market bottoms when measured against a year’s worth of realized profits.
How the two loss gauges work
Both gauges start from an estimate of what investors gained or lost when coins moved. Glassnode compares realized losses with profits taken over the previous year. On that relative measure, the weekend selloff reached readings Glassnode associated with lows in 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023.
CryptoQuant’s series tallies profits and subtracts losses over a rolling 30-day period. On that measure, net losses hit $30 billion on Feb. 20 and $18 billion on June 30. Even with a smaller monthly reading, losses were concentrated in the latest selloff. The four days from Nov. 15 to Nov. 18 produced $5 billion in net losses, more than half the 30-day figure.
A burst of losses can look extreme against a year’s profits while the month’s net dollar loss stays smaller than it was in a previous selloff. Earlier gains still in the 30-day window can offset part of the recent losses. Neither gauge sets a threshold Bitcoin has to reach before the price can stabilize.
Woominkyu’s Nov. 19 CryptoQuant Quicktake lists net losses of $30 billion on Feb. 20, $18.4 billion on June 30, and $8.4 billion in its latest reading.
That pressure reached coins that had been idle for more than 155 days. CryptoQuant’s long-term-holder spent output profit ratio fell to 0.73 on Nov. 18, its lowest since mid-August, according to Woominkyu’s analysis. The reading implies roughly 73 cents in value when those outputs moved for each dollar of value when they were created. The series measures only older outputs that moved, including transfers that can occur without a trade on an exchange.
The spot market gave a more tentative signal. Glassnode saw Bitcoin briefly trade at a premium on Coinbase around the Nov. 15 low before slipping back to a discount. Woominkyu put the Nov. 18 reading for CryptoQuant’s Coinbase Premium Index at minus 0.14%. That index compares the dollar price on Coinbase with the USDT price on Binance. It helps gauge relative buying pressure across venues using prices alone.
Glassnode also reported that buyer-initiated spot trades outweighed seller-initiated trades over the day leading into its Nov. 17 snapshot. Sustained buying in completed spot trades would give the rebound more weight. Standing buy orders can still be withdrawn.
What would make the Bitcoin rebound hold
The New York Fed calendar scheduled initial jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey for 8:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 19. Because the reports share a release time, a move in the two-year Treasury yield could reflect either or both. The yield was 4.80% on Nov. 18, unchanged from the day before in the Treasury’s daily series.
Bitcoin can respond quickly to a change in rate expectations. Daily on-chain readings take longer to fill in. If Bitcoin’s price stays above the recent lows, watch whether daily net losses ease and the older-coin ratio moves back toward 1, where spending and creation values are equal. A narrower Coinbase discount alongside sustained spot buying would add evidence that buyers can absorb the supply. A daily close near $62,000 while losses deepen and the discount persists would leave the rebound on weaker footing.

items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[xorcist]: Isn't this what something like psnup (or pdfbook or similar tools) does, which you probably already have at your command line, at least if you've printed things like man pages or latex documents? It was pretty normal to use and saved lots of paper when you could print your documentation 8-up, but it let you rotate, scale and place each page arbitrarily. I believe users of the more GUI-oriented operating systems like Windows or Mac eventually got it integrated in their printing dialo...

[staplung]: For the curious, the generalized process of reordering and potentially rotating pages so that when printed and folded (and optionally gathered into signatures) is called impositioning. There is specialized software with a variety of options that will do this for an input document. Bookbinder JS is a nice web-based tool that will do this for you too, though I'm not sure it covers the exact folding algorithm described in this article.  https://momijizukamori.github.io/bookbi...

[addled]: My high school geometry teacher would let us use an index card of notes during exams. She had a student years prior show her this folding technique and asked if he could use it for the test.  Not only did she allow it, but she taught it to every class going forward for those that wanted to put in the extra effort. My buddies and I spent so much time trying to come up with modifications to use more area of the page.  Some of them even worked!

[baud9600]: I’m bothered that this piece doesnt mention pocketmod, which I think is where the folding idea came from? The fold image looks very similar! I used this 20 years ago and still do sometimes:  https://pocketmod.com/

[bthallplz]: I really love this form factor and how inexpensive it could be to print small books. Does anyone have any suggestions for ways to estimate how many words could fit per page while still being decently readable, depending on different fonts a person uses? A step further: a markdown editor with a preview of how the printed out document would read would be nice.

阿里电话会：或下调20GW数据中心目标及资本开支，预计2028年下半年现金流转正

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，阿里巴巴管理层在第二财季财报电话会上表示，受全球不同区域算力政策变化影响，公司长期 20GW 数据中心建设目标存在下调可能，整体资本开支计划也可能相应降低。同时，阿里将加快以平头哥为核心的国产算力供应链建设。管理层预计，2027 年及 2028 年上半年将是本轮算力投入的高峰期。在国产算力供应链持续放量、并按既定节奏推进的假设下，公司有望于 2028 年下半年实现现金流转正。2028 年之后，随着国产算力供应链规模化扩张，阿里预计将逐步走过 AI 基础设施投入强度最高的阶段。

本季度，阿里资本开支为 505 亿元，低于上一季度的 677 亿元，但同比大幅增长，主要受到算力规模爬坡、芯片等组件价格上涨，以及增加 CPU 算力储备以应对 AI 智能体需求等因素推动。同期自由现金流净流出 345 亿元，去年同期净流出 218 亿元，主要原因是云基础设施投资增加。

增长目标方面，管理层表示，全球算力供应新规对明年产品和服务的影响仍存在较大不确定性，但国产算力推进进度超出此前预期。阿里给出的 2028 财年云业务增速目标为 30%—45%；随着 2028 自然年国产算力产品持续放量，云业务增速有望重新恢复至 50% 以上。公司同时重申，2030 自然年外部云收入目标为 1000 亿美元，长期利润率超过 20%。

本季度，阿里 AI、云与算力服务板块收入同比增长 53% 至 610 亿元，外部客户收入同比增长 64% 至 470 亿元，连续第十个季度加速增长。剔除算力设备解决方案后，外部客户经常性收入同比增长 67% 至 370 亿元。AI 相关产品收入达到 179 亿元，连续第十三个季度实现三位数增长。

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors are flat ahead of ANT IPO, stocks up big; BTC at $63.8k
- ANT jumps to $105 on Hyperliquid pre-IPO debut, starting at $83
- Gemini ships Gemini 4 Neon, new top model; speculation of RSI
- Fed Governor Waller calls for 50 bps hike in December to “shock people”
- Variational announces $110M raise at $1.5B valuation
Gemini Tops the Benchmarks as Anthropic Prices at $83
Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, its fourth frontier model release in three weeks, and on the eve of the heavily anticipated Anthropic IPO.
This isn’t just a normal model release. For one, it’s incredibly good. Neon posts 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 59 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 57 for GPT-6.2 Sol. It takes the Vals Index at 70.9%, AutomationBench at 56.3% against Opus 5.5’s 42.5%, and GraphWalks long-context retrieval at 95.2% against Opus 5.5’s 66.8%.
Beyond just the outperformance, Google has been releasing at a pace nobody else is matching. It dropped Argon in mid-October. Carbon on October 28. Hydrogen last week. Google owns its silicon, its data centers, and its distribution, and it is using all three to iterate faster than labs that rent compute. And it has some speculating that Google has already achieved RSI (recursive self-improvement), the final step ahead of super intelligence.
So Google has caught up at the top of the AI race. Just in time for the ANT IPO.
Anthropic will be priced at $83, 6.4% above the top of its $70 to $78 range, valuing the company around $1.5 trillion fully diluted. On the 825 million shares in the original terms, that’s roughly $68.5 billion raised, and about $94.5 billion counting the separate $26 billion private placement from its compute suppliers. It trades Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. Notably, ANT has been trading on Hyperliquid in the $90-$100 range for the past week but popped to $105 this morning.
The valuation math is a 55% step-up from the $965 billion May round and about 25% below the $2 trillion Anthropic was reportedly chasing in September. Revenue ran $33.2 billion through nine months against $2.5 billion a year earlier, a 13x increase. Annualize that and $1.5 trillion is roughly 34 times sales.
That’s a steep raise given the macro backdrop and the Fed calling for more hikes for longer. AI stocks have been shaky over the past month and even moreso since Jensen Huang left Nvidia. Not the most confident market headed into the 2nd $1T+ IPO of the year.
So what does it mean for today’s price action? Personally, I expect a pop to the $95-$105 level that Hyperliquid has been pricing out for weeks, and it likely sees a spike higher. But there will be massive volatility, and it’s very likely to trade under that $83 level over the coming days and weeks. Especially given the new (surprise) headwinds from Google with its outperforming model.
We will find out soon enough. Good luck to everyone trading it today.

Investigation: Sky (Formerly MakerDAO) Peg Stability Module Processed $518M in Transactions Linked to Illicit Wallets, Including $101.9M Tied Directly to North Korean Hackers

According to CoinDesk, an investigation by crypto risk analytics firm Inca Digital found that the Peg Stability Module (PSM) of Sky (formerly MakerDAO) has processed $518 million in transactions involving 422 wallets linked to illicit activities—including hacks, phishing attacks, and sanctioned entities—with $101.9 million directly tied to North Korean hackers. Within 10 days following the 2025 Bybit hack, associated wallets converted $91.5 million in assets through the PSM.

Currently, Sky's PSM holds approximately $2.7 billion in USDC within a single Ethereum address; if Circle were to blacklist that address at the request of law enforcement, the entire reserve could be frozen, potentially impairing redemptions and the peg stability of DAI and USDS. In response, the Sky Frontier Foundation stated that the flagged transactions do not mean all funds were stolen assets, noting that the volume accounts for less than 0.06% of PSM's over $930 billion in cumulative volume and occurred almost entirely via third-party DEX aggregators rather than Sky's official website, which implements wallet screening. — link

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi courts against the unknown perpetrators of its October 29 hack.
- The order can be served via the blockchain and is backed by a constantly updated list of 26,000 wallet addresses holding stolen assets.
- About $2.85 billion linked to the hack has been frozen so far, and U.S. prosecutors have won authorization to seize or restrain $1.2 billion of the frozen funds.
Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order against the hackers behind last month's attack on the exchange, which the FBI has blamed on North Korea.
The injunction was issued by the courts of the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) against the unknown perpetrators, Binance's lawyers at Gibson Dunn confirmed, according to City AM.
The order breaks new legal ground. It can be served directly via the blockchain, and market participants will be notified of a "living list" of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets, Gibson Dunn partner Kendall Day said. That will enable "those assets to be frozen rapidly even as they are laundered at pace," Day said.
Binance has also secured proprietary injunctions and delivery-up orders, including against parties holding frozen assets who are not accused of wrongdoing, according to City AM. Decrypt has reached out to Gibson Dunn for comment.
"We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers," Dugan Bliss, Binance's deputy general counsel, said in a statement reported by Bloomberg.
Chasing the stolen funds
The FBI has attributed the October 29 hack to TraderTraitor, a group linked to North Korea, which has denied involvement. The attackers gained access after an engineer was phished through a fake job offer, according to Bloomberg. The Secret Service has joined the FBI's investigation.
About $2.85 billion in funds connected to the hack has been frozen, including by Ripple and World Liberty Financial, according to Bloomberg. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $2.7 billion shortly after the attack, and the Justice Department said last week it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain $1.2 billion of that.
The hackers have used thousands of wallets and multiple blockchains to launder the rest, and wallets linked to the hack began moving Ethereum again this week after two weeks of inactivity.
Binance has said it fully covered the $6.3 billion in customer assets affected and absorbed the losses itself.

Anthropic或面临巨额抛压，数十亿股将陆续解禁

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据彭博社报道，Anthropic 上市首日允许创始人、员工及其他现有股东额外出售最多 3.16 亿股。未来数月，随着限售期分批届满，以及公司于 2027 年初公布 2026 财年业绩，数十亿股内部持股将陆续解除限售，后续买盘能否承接潜在供应成为市场关注焦点。

Anthropic 非创始人员工在首个交易日最多可出售个人持股的 10%，在 2026 财年业绩公布后可再出售最多 35%。不过，获准出售或股份解禁并不意味着股东必然减持，实际流入市场的股份数量仍取决于其出售意愿及届时股价。Anthropic 此次 IPO 最终定价为每股 83 美元，高于此前 70 至 78 美元的发行区间。按包含未归属股权激励在内的完全稀释股本计算，公司估值达 1.5 万亿美元。

彭博社评论员 Chris Hughes 认为，此次定价基本公允，但未给新股投资者留下明显折价。包括风险投资者 Jack Selby 在内的市场人士此前已警告解禁带来的供应压力，相关预期理论上已反映在发行价中；但若股东集中兑现收益，而承接资金不足，股价仍可能承压。与此同时，今年 6 月上市的 SpaceX 也将迎来现有股东减持窗口，两家公司的股份供应释放在时间上存在重叠。为筹集数据中心及 AI 基础设施建设资金，部分科技巨头也从回购股票转向增发融资，Meta 上月的股权融资即为一例。

高盛策略师预计，2027 年美国股票净供应量增幅或创 2000 年以来新高。不过，高盛认为，供给增加虽然会压制估值，但尚不足以终结美股牛市，因为科技巨头以外的其他行业回购活动仍然稳健。Anthropic 已向投资者表示，若条件允许，希望避免上市后短期内再次进行股权融资，更倾向于借助上市便利通过债务市场募资。面对庞大的 AI 算力基础设施支出承诺，其实际融资路径仍将取决于经营现金流与资本市场环境。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms
Hong Kong’s securities regulator said Hyperliquid has no local license and may have promoted its trading services to investors in the city.
Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid, a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures, to its Alert List on Wednesday.
The SFC said Hyperliquid lacks a license to operate in the city.
The entry names both Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong, while identifying the exchange’s trading site. The SFC said it suspects Hyperliquid of running a trading platform in Hong Kong, claiming to run one there or actively marketing its services to the Hong Kong public.
The SFC’s list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms now has 69 entries.
Cointelegraph contacted Hyperliquid for comment but did not receive an immediate response.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore added Hyperliquid to its Investor Alert List on June 26. The list includes firms that investors may mistakenly believe the central bank regulates. Hyperliquid said at the time that it never claimed to hold a Singapore license.
Related: Crypto.com to withdraw Hong Kong consumer app citing regulatory changes

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
GTA VI publisher racks up nearly 3x Nvidia’s tokenized stock volume
Tokenized Take-Two shares drew $249.5 million in DEX volume Wednesday, nearly three times the $88.1 million for tokenized Nvidia shares.
Tokenized shares of Grand Theft Auto VI publisher Take-Two Interactive recorded nearly three times the trading volume of tokenized Nvidia shares on decentralized exchanges (DEXs) as the blockbuster began its global rollout.
Trading volume for tokenized Take-Two (TTWO) shares surged 578% to $249.5 million on Wednesday, up from $36.8 million a day earlier, according to Token Terminal data. Tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) recorded $88.1 million in DEX volume despite ranking first by market cap at $399.4 million.
The surge made TTWO the most-traded tokenized stock tracked by Token Terminal that day, accounting for roughly 42% of the $590.7 million in DEX volume.
Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based assets that track the value of publicly traded shares, allowing investors to gain exposure through crypto trading platforms. Their onchain trading volumes do not represent transactions in the underlying shares on traditional stock exchanges.
Take-Two shares on the Nasdaq rose 6.2% to close Wednesday at $216.61, according to Yahoo Finance. Shares gave back some of those gains Thursday, falling 4% to $208 in premarket trading as of 7:02 a.m. ET.
GTA VI, which Citi analyst Jason Bazinet estimated cost about $1.4 billion to make, ends a 13-year wait for a sequel to GTA V. PlayStation and Microsoft’s Xbox both said it was the most preordered game in the history of their respective stores.
Backpack leads tokenized TTWO trading
Most of the tokenized TTWO trading was in a Solana-based asset offered by Backpack Securities, a platform operated by crypto exchange Backpack. The token accounted for about $239 million, or 96%, of the day’s trading volume.
Over the past 30 days, tokenized NVDA shares recorded about $2 billion in DEX trading volume, compared with $808.1 million for tokenized TTWO shares.
The GTA VI launch has also attracted crypto scammers. Blockchain security company Blockaid said in a Wednesday X post that it had flagged more than 8,800 GTA-themed tokens on Solana as malicious, suspicious or spam, alongside hundreds of social media posts promoting fake airdrops and preorders.
Separately, four US senators questioned the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Monday about potential gaps in investor protections and anti-money laundering safeguards under its new tokenized securities exemption.
Related: Fed’s Waller cites Binance hack in warning over tokenized finance
items.title: GTA VI publisher racks up nearly 3x Nvidia’s tokenized stock volume

items.author: Gino Matos
items.content:
Quick Take
- NYSE owner ICE is partnering with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US through a regulated trading venue.
- Trade[XYZ] controls 97.6% of HIP-3 trading volume, handling $4.9 billion daily, but its offshore liquidity will not automatically transfer to the US.
- ICE must attract enough buyers and market makers to build a liquid US market, with regulatory approvals and trading depth still uncertain.
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the New York Stock Exchange’s owner, is working with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US.
The proposed venue would have to attract its own buy and sell orders, Hyunsu Jung, CEO of Nasdaq-listed Hyperion DeFi, told CryptoSlate.
Jung said firms quoting on both the proposed US venue and existing overseas markets could help keep prices close if the venues match orders and handle funding similarly.
The amount a trader can buy or sell at those prices would depend on the orders available on the US market. Jung’s company builds on Hyperliquid and earns revenue from work in its ecosystem.
How a separate US market would work
ICE announced the agreement on Oct. 29 and said it would be the exclusive operator of the regulated markets, using a dedicated retail venue and clearing structure separate from its institutional futures business.
ICE also announced a minority investment in Trade[XYZ], subject to regulatory approvals, including approvals needed to support leveraged trading. ICE’s announcement sets out who would operate and clear the market, leaving the trading rules and exact order-book design unspecified.
Perpetual futures let traders take positions on the price of a reference asset through a contract with no set expiration date. Trade[XYZ] already offers contracts on equities, stock indexes, commodities and currencies to eligible customers outside the US.
ICE expects customers who pass identity checks to access the proposed market through participating futures brokers, formally known as futures commission merchants, and also expects its joint venture with OKX to help distribute the contracts.
That route depends on separate approvals for the venture’s broker-dealer and futures commission merchant businesses.
The existing HIP-3 design gives each builder-deployed venue its own order books and margining on Hyperliquid’s shared trading infrastructure.
In its November quarterly filing, Hyperion DeFi described ICE and Trade[XYZ]’s plan in the context of HIP-3, an optional extension that lets operators control access. The filing tied the plans it discussed to regulatory approvals, finalizing the extension, and making it available on the live network.
An order book records what buyers and sellers are willing to trade at each price, so a buy order posted outside the US would be available to traders on that book. To complete a trade on a separate US venue, a customer would need a matching order on the US book.
If a comparable contract traded at a higher price on one venue, a firm able to trade both could buy on the cheaper venue and sell on the more expensive one. Those trades would tend to bring the two prices closer.
A market maker that takes the other side of a customer’s trade in the US could manage some of the resulting exposure overseas if it can access both venues.
Jung said margin and leverage rules for futures broker accounts would help determine how much liquidity firms can provide. Margin is the collateral a firm sets aside to support a position, and the more collateral a trade requires, the more of a firm’s capital it ties up.
Trading is already concentrated
Trade[XYZ] recorded over $4.9 billion of the $5 billion traded across tracked HIP-3 venues in the 24 hours through Nov. 18, representing 97.6% of the total. EntropyIO, the next-largest venue by volume, accounted for 2.3%, according to UnderHyper’s venue breakdown.
UnderHyper’s measure of rolling dollar volume counts completed trades across the HIP-3 venues it tracks.
Jung attributed Trade[XYZ]’s lead to listing key markets early and making them available in the Hyperliquid interface traders already used.
ICE hopes to reach US customers through brokers and distribution partners, but the size of that customer base and how often it trades will become clear only if the US venue opens.
If the US venue opens, traders will be able to judge its liquidity by the gap between the best buy and sell prices and how much they can trade near those prices. The test for ICE will come when traders try to move a large position near the price they first saw.
items.title: NYSE owner targets Hyperliquid’s $5 billion trading boom, but the liquidity may not follow

美国成立「威胁阻断中心」，将联合交易平台与支付机构追踪诈骗资金

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，美国国土安全部与司法部于当地时间 11 月 18 日宣布启动「威胁阻断中心」（TDC），打击针对美国民众的网络诈骗和加密资产盗窃。该中心将为逾 30 家联邦机构及 440 多个州和地方合作单位提供共享的调查工具和情报。

调查人员将与加密货币交易平台、支付服务商和社交平台共享线索，以便拦截欺诈转账、冻结涉案资金或移除诈骗账号。执法部门将继续调查，并依法申请法院授权查扣资产。

TRM Labs 是该中心的主要私营部门合作伙伴，其 Ardence 平台将用于处理受害者报案、追踪加密资金并梳理犯罪网络。采购记录显示，TRM Labs 于今年 7 月获得约 9466 万美元的合同，履行期至 2027 年 8 月 29 日。

FBI 数据显示，2025 年共收到 181,565 起涉及加密货币的投诉，报告损失超过 110 亿美元，其中加密投资诈骗约占 72 亿美元。FBI 自 2024 年启动的预警行动已通知逾 8000 名受害者，估计帮助避免逾 5 亿美元的进一步损失。

Solana Unveils 2027 Roadmap, Doubling Compute Capacity and Cutting Unit Consumption by 80%

Following the Alpenglow upgrade, Solana core development team Anza has outlined its 2027 technical roadmap for Solana across four pillars: Performance (doubling network compute capacity and cutting compute unit consumption by 80% for token account transactions); Expressivity (adding vector processing for models running fully onchain, raising the per-transaction account limit from 64 to 96, and reading account data directly rather than copying it to reduce data movement per transaction); Market Structure (building on Alpenglow with faster block distribution and introducing Constellation for clearer ordering rules and greater validator competition); and Resilience (simplifying the protocol with fewer special cases to make future changes safer). — link

Sky稳定币兑换模块被曝涉5.18亿美元非法关联交易，27亿枚USDC储备面临潜在冻结风险

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，链上风控机构 Inca Digital 的一份调查显示，Sky Protocol 的锚定稳定模块（PSM）曾处理 422 个与黑客、钓鱼活动或受制裁实体等有关联的钱包的交易，累计约 5.18 亿美元，其中 1.019 亿美元与朝鲜相关活动直接关联。这两项数字统计的是关联钱包经该模块进行的交易额，并不意味着所有资金均已被认定为赃款，也不代表 Sky 遭到攻击。

调查发现，在 Bybit 于 2025 年 2 月遭遇约 15 亿美元资产失窃后的 10 天内，曾收到相关被盗资产的钱包通过 Sky 的 PSM 完成了约 9150 万美元的交易。另一家链上调查机构 Nominis 应 CoinDesk 要求分析了涉及 320 多个链上地址的 560 多笔交易，也确认了相关钱包与朝鲜黑客活动的联系。

潜在冻结风险来自储备集中。PSM 为 Sky 旗下稳定币 DAI 和 USDS 提供兑换流动性，帮助维持美元锚定。调查称，相关储备约有 27 亿枚 USDC 集中在同一个以太坊地址。若 USDC 发行方 Circle 因法院命令或执法请求冻结该地址，正常储备也可能一并无法动用，导致模块的双向兑换中断，并给 DAI 和 USDS 的流动性及锚定带来压力。这是调查提出的风险情景，并非储备已被冻结。

Inca Digital 警告，即使储备未被冻结，交易所和机构合作伙伴也可能加强资金来源审查，或限制与 Sky 的业务往来。CoinDesk 举例指出，Galaxy Digital 持有价值约 1 亿美元的生息稳定币 sUSDS，而 Sky 生态内的 Grove 已向 Galaxy 提供 5 亿美元的信贷额度。Coinbase 则对相关 USDC 储备余额支付奖励，但其发言人表示，这些资产由客户自托管，Coinbase 无权调动。
