items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Testnet5 enforces four proposed Bitcoin rules from block one, giving mining pools a way to test their block-building software.
- The minimum difficulty rises from 1 on Testnet4 to roughly 1 million on Testnet5 to curb rapid early mining.
- Bitcoin Core and Sparrow Wallet still have open Testnet5 proposals, with early node sync and wallet tests already reported.
Bitcoin miners have a new network, Testnet5, where they can test their software against four proposed changes to Bitcoin’s rules, with support in Bitcoin Core and Sparrow Wallet at the patch stage.
The Bitcoin Improvement Proposals repository added the record of Testnet5’s first block to the network specification on Nov. 17, three days after the block was mined.
What Bitcoin miners can test
The four changes are collectively known as BIP54, or Consensus Cleanup. Bitcoin Inquisition’s signet already enforces them, but producing blocks there also requires miners to satisfy a signing challenge in addition to proof of work.
On Testnet5, independent miners and pools can use their own software to build blocks and see whether other nodes accept them without that extra requirement.
Two of the four rules limit how much work certain blocks can impose on nodes and how miners can use timestamps to influence difficulty. One caps certain signature operations in ordinary transactions to limit how long a block can take to verify.
The other restricts timestamps at the start and end of each difficulty period to prevent miners from artificially driving the difficulty down.
A third rule rejects transactions that measure exactly 64 bytes after removing witness data, closing an ambiguity in proofs of transaction inclusion. The fourth makes each new mining reward transaction unique by requiring its locktime to equal the block height minus one and requiring that locktime to take effect.
Pool operators can use Testnet5 to check that their software, which usually builds the reward transaction, applies the new rule.
Testnet4 let miners drop to minimum difficulty if a block’s timestamp was more than 20 minutes after the previous one, except at the start of a difficulty period. BIP95 says competing blocks mined under the exception caused frequent short reorganizations, where one set of recent blocks replaced another.
Testnet5 removes the 20-minute rule altogether and raises the minimum difficulty from 1 to about 1 million. The specification’s authors chose the higher floor to slow early block production before difficulty adjusts, while keeping it low enough for a single specialized mining machine to keep the test chain running.
Early testers can build the Bitcoin Core patch and sync by manually connecting to a peer, its author reported. The proposal targets Core’s 32.x branch and still needs to be merged and shipped in a public release.
Bitcoin Core 32.1, the latest release as of Nov. 18, predates the Testnet5 integration build.
Sparrow’s wallet integration proposal opened late on Nov. 17, and would let users select Testnet5 in the wallet and add two public Electrum servers to connect to the chain.
A Sparrow collaborator reported on Nov. 18 that the wallet’s Silent Payments feature worked in tests against both servers. The proposal, which depends on an update to Sparrow’s Drongo library, remained open.
items.title: Bitcoin launches Testnet5 and gives miners a real trial of four proposed fixes

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，《Grand Theft Auto VI》（GTA 6）在全球正式发售上线，登陆 PlayStation 5 与 Xbox Series X|S 平台。

发售前夕，市场研究机构 Sensor Tower 估算的预售数据引发广泛关注，最新数据显示该游戏预售接近或超过 1700 万份、收入约 16.5 亿美元。其中 PS5 占比约 75%，Xbox 约占 25%。Take-Two Interactive（Rockstar 母公司）未公布官方具体数字，但在财报中表示预售「远超内部预期」。

与此同时，英国职场也因游戏发售出现明显波动。HR 软件公司 BrightHR 分析其覆盖超过 120 万员工、7 万家英国企业的缺勤数据并外推后指出，11 月与 12 月因 GTA 6 相关原因预订的年假约达 8.3 万天，预计给企业造成约 1240 万英镑成本（按每天约 150 英镑计算）。仅发售当天（11 月 19 日），相关年假成本约 314 万英镑，当天请假原因中约 4.63% 提到 GTA，请求量甚至超过蜜月等传统事由。部分员工在请假理由中直接写明「为 GTA 6 请假，拒绝就辞职」。

据 GMGN 数据显示，GTA6 相关 Meme 币 DacityCoin（DCTY）24 小时拉涨 38,100%，市值现报 1364 万美元，24 小时交易额达 6500 万美元。

据悉，Dacity Coin（DACITY）是一个基于 Solana 的 meme 币，其来源是在 GTA 6 此前的泄露画面中，出现了「AudaCity」品牌和相关特技任务（女主 Lucia 跳伞做宣传）。从网络流露出的游戏实机演示视频信息显示，GTA6 确实在游戏内部存在 DacityCoin（DCTY）相关游戏内容，但本意或仅是对荒诞 Meme 币炒作的写实映射。

BlockBeats 注：Meme 币交易波动巨大，多依赖市场情绪和概念的炒作，并无实际价值或用例，投资者需注意风险。

标普维持USDT锚定美元能力最低评级，高风险资产占比升至28%，Tether援引《大空头》反驳

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据 Cointelegraph 报道，标普全球评级（S&P Global Ratings）在最新稳定币稳定性评估中，将 Tether 发行的 USDT 维持美元挂钩能力的评分维持在最低档 5（弱），与 2025 年 11 月的评估结果相同。标普表示，截至 9 月 30 日，黄金、比特币、公开市场股票、担保贷款和公司债券等较高风险持仓相当于流通中 USDT 的 28%，高于一年前的 24%；「这些资产价值若大幅下跌，可能导致 USDT 抵押不足」。标普还称发现了更多薄弱点，但「评估不能低于 5」，因此未再下调。

Tether 向 Cointelegraph 回应称，「问题在于标普的框架，而不是我们的储备」，并提及电影《大空头》及 2008 年金融危机，称「他们自己的历史就能说明根本问题」。Tether 经 BDO 鉴证的 9 月 30 日储备报告显示，资产约 1915 亿美元、负债约 1835 亿美元，超额资产约 79.5 亿美元。

标普还指出，Tether 于 2025 年 1 月迁至萨尔瓦多后，当地监管要求 70% 储备可在 30 日内变现，但框架较为宽泛，仍可纳入黄金、比特币和贷款等相对高风险资产，且未要求隔离储备资产。此外，KPMG 虽于 2026 年 8 月确认已对 Tether 2025 年报表出具无保留意见，这是该公司首次「完整独立审计」，但经审计报表和审计师报告尚未公布；储备报告亦未披露托管机构和交易对手，鉴证仍为季度，而其他稳定币普遍按月披露。标普同时提到，USDT 在过去 12 个月保持了较好的价格稳定记录。

知情人士：英伟达董事会仍存3名「保黄派」，已缩小新任CEO考虑范围

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据 semafor 援引知情人士报道，尽管英伟达宣称不打算让被解职的 CEO 黄仁勋重返，但董事会中的一部分成员正在推动他的回归。

知情人士称，黄仁勋已与多位科技高管会面，并与至少一名董事会成员谈论了他回归的可能性。

与这名董事的对话发生在公司发布财报之前，也发生在黄仁勋周二发表公开声明之前。他在声明中表示，如果董事会认为回归符合「我们股东、员工、公司以及美国的最佳利益」，他愿意回到公司。

几小时后，英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯（Harvey Jones）在公司财报电话会议上表示，这家芯片制造商并未考虑让黄仁勋回归，且董事会已一致投票接受他的辞呈。

黄仁勋和英伟达的发言人拒绝置评。

一些知情人士表示，尽管有三名董事提出反对，但其他董事会成员已开始缩小寻找黄仁勋继任者的范围。

知情人士称，ARM CEO 雷内·哈斯（Rene Haas）和 Marvell CEO 马特·墨菲（Matt Murphy）都在考虑范围之内。其中一位人士透露，哈斯已与至少部分英伟达董事谈论过接任该职位的事宜，但他表示，在有人呼吁让黄仁勋重回掌舵位置的情况下接任该职位，他担心这会带来不好的外界观感。

ARM 和 Marvell 的发言人未立即回应置评请求。此外，鉴于 Marvell 正在处理与竞争对手 Lumentum 的大规模合并事宜，墨菲能否接任英伟达 CEO 一职也尚不清楚。

Kraken母公司Payward达成协议将收购Tribe Capital

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据 Payward 官方公告，综合金融服务与市场基础设施平台 Payward, Inc. 已签署最终协议，将收购创投及资产管理平台 Tribe Capital Management, Inc.。Tribe Capital 运用人工智能和数据科学，对早期及后期私募投资进行承销与资本配置，管理规模为 27 亿美元。交易财务条款未披露，尚需满足包括必要同意在内的惯例交割条件，预计于 2027 年第一季度完成。

Payward 表示，Tribe Capital 在投资寻源、承销、组合构建和基金管理方面的能力将补充其现有基础设施，并成为其资产管理条线的重要组成部分，该条线与交易、银行、服务及 AI 并列。公司计划在 Tribe Capital 现有投资平台基础上开发新的私募市场产品，并将投资发起、资产管理与托管、交易、抵押及代币化等能力衔接。Tribe Capital 联合创始人 Jonathan Hsu 表示，加入 Payward 使其有机会将 Tribe 的投资方法带入一家全球金融平台，并认为双方在投资方法与 Payward 的基础设施、分发及产品构建能力上契合。

公告还显示，Tribe Capital 成立于 2018 年，由 Arjun Sethi、Jonathan Hsu 和 Ted Maidenberg 创立，总部位于美国加州门洛帕克，通过集合基金和跟投工具投资早期及后期私募公司，投资组合涵盖 Shiprocket、SpaceX、Applied Intuition、Apollo.io 和 Kapital 等。Payward 称，其是 Kraken 以及 NinjaTrader、Breakout、xStocks、CF Benchmarks 等产品背后的基础设施层。本次交易中，Moelis & Company LLC 担任 Payward 的财务顾问，Jones Day 与 Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz 担任法律顾问，Morrison Foerster 担任监管顾问，Ropes & Gray 担任 Tribe Capital 的法律顾问。

items.content:
Trump administration unveils new center to choke off scam payments
Americans reported more than $17.7 billion in online fraud losses in 2025.
The Trump administration has unveiled a new Threat Disruption Center, aimed at stopping money flows to foreign criminal networks behind scams, cybercrime and sextortion schemes.
The Homeland Security Task Force’s National Coordination Center, co-led by the departments of Homeland Security and Justice, announced the launch of the unit on Wednesday. It seeks to help more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners track scams and work with banks and crypto platforms to stop payments to scam networks.
The Homeland Security statement said the center was created under a March 2026 executive order that directed federal agencies to work with private companies to combat online fraud and other cybercrime targeting Americans.
“Every hour between a victim’s report and a response gives criminals more time to launder stolen funds and identify their next target,” said Heith Janke, operations director of the FBI’s Criminal Branch.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs was selected as the center’s main private-sector partner. It will provide and maintain Ardence, the investigative platform the center will use to map scam networks and identify victims. TRM said it will also provide engineering and investigative support.
“These scammers rarely stop after one payment — they drain a victim’s savings, or their retirement, over months and years,” said Esteban Castano, co-founder and CEO of TRM Labs.
“Stepping in sooner changes everything: a warning before the next payment, a scam website removed before it victimizes another family, or stolen funds frozen while they can still be recovered.
The FBI received about 453,000 reports of online fraud in 2025, with reported losses exceeding $17.7 billion.
In September, the Justice Department estimated that overseas scam centers cost Americans about $10 billion a year through schemes including crypto and online investment fraud.
Related: US authorities dismantle crypto scam network that stole tens of millions
items.title: Trump administration unveils new center to choke off scam payments

BTCPay Server发布紧急更新修复nginx五项安全漏洞

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据 BTCPay Server 官方消息，该项目正在发布紧急更新，以应对 nginx 相关漏洞 CVE-2026-123007、CVE-2026-123634、CVE-2026-123633、CVE-2026-121810 和 CVE-2026-113425，并建议用户尽快升级。该项目称，此次为依赖项更新，下一版本的 BTCPay 仍在测试中；更新后可用 docker exec nginx nginx -v 核查，预期应显示 nginx/1.31.9。

升级方面，服务器管理员可在 Server Settings → Maintenance 点击 Update；大多数 Docker 部署可通过 SSH 执行 sudo su -，进入 btcpayserver-docker 目录并运行 btcpay-update.sh；Umbrel、Start9 等节点平台用户需待所在平台提供更新后尽快安装。若无法立即升级，核心贡献者 ndeet 提供了面向 Docker 部署的临时、非持久缓解方案：在 nginx 配置中关闭 HTTP/2，再检测配置并重载服务，直至相关 nginx 更新可用。

BTCPay Server 将此次预警归功于 Rob Hamilton、danielabrozzoni 及 Bitcoin Red Team 其余成员对开源生态的监测，并表示目前提及的 nginx 利用方式较为脆弱，迄今尚无公开确认的攻击，但作为开源项目将尽快为用户提供修复方案。

S&P Global Ratings maintained its stablecoin stability assessment of Tether's USDT, the world's largest stablecoin, at 5 (weak), the lowest on its five-point scale. The agency said higher-risk assets, including gold, Bitcoin, equities and loans, were equivalent to 28% of USDT in circulation as of September 30, up from 24% a year earlier, raising concerns about potential undercollateralization. S&P also cited limited disclosure of audited financial statements, reserve segregation and custodians. items.content:
花旗、PNC等美国银行更新协议，使用第三方AI代理的客户即便遭黑客攻击也需自行担责

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据 TechCrunch 报道，美国第三大商业银行花旗银行（Citibank）于本周更新在线用户协议，向使用第三方 AI 工具处理个人财务的客户明确，相关操作一旦出现问题将由客户自行承担，即便遭遇黑客攻击也不例外。

花旗发言人对 TechCrunch 表示，随着第三方 AI 工具日益普及，银行希望客户理解分享银行凭证或授权此类工具访问账户的风险，并强调选择向第三方 AI 代理开放账户访问权限的客户，需对该类代理所进行的活动负责。报道称，花旗此次更新不仅要求客户对 AI 代理的操作负责，还规定一旦 AI 工具泄露凭证或遭到黑客攻击，黑客利用账户实施的行为同样由客户承担责任。美国最大的两家银行摩根大通（JPMorgan）和美国银行（Bank of America）已于上月宣布类似政策；美国第八大银行 PNC 于 18 日更新了相关条款。另据 TechCrunch 所见邮件，大型银行 Citizens 本周也向客户发送邮件，警示其需对 AI 助手的所有操作承担责任。

报道指出，AI 代理可被授予银行及其他在线金融门户的登录凭证，用于分析消费和投资、提供建议，乃至处理交易和账单支付。金融机构表示，不会为自动助手发起的有意或无意交易承担撤销责任。Anthropic 本月早些时候推出的个人理财工具被明确标为「只读」，「不能转移、管理或投资用户的资金」。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Japan’s Nov. 18 auction drew competitive tenders worth 3.64 times the amount accepted, down from 5.84 for the same bond in October.
- The dollar-yen midpoint moved just ¥0.01 between the Bank of Japan’s two Tokyo readings, while overnight yen funding held steady.
- Japan’s Nov. 25 bond sale will test long-term demand, while yen funding and futures data matter more directly for Bitcoin leverage.
Demand fell at Japan’s Nov. 18 auction of a 20-year government bond, with investors offering to buy 3.64 times the amount the Finance Ministry accepted in the competitive auction, putting pressure on traders who borrow yen to hold Bitcoin.
The average accepted yield rose, while the yen barely moved between the Bank of Japan’s two 5 p.m. Tokyo readings.
In the Nov. 18 results, the ministry recorded ¥1.914 trillion in competitive tenders for issue 198 and accepted ¥525.8 billion. At the October auction, it received ¥3.139 trillion and accepted ¥537.1 billion.
Demand fell by much more than the amount sold in the competitive auction, and the average accepted yield rose 3.3 basis points to 3.756% from 3.723%.
Competitive coverage fell from 5.84× on Oct. 20 to 3.64× on Nov. 18 for Japan’s 20-year issue 198.
At 5 p.m. in Tokyo, the midpoint of the Bank of Japan’s dollar-yen quote was 159.35 yen per dollar on Nov. 18, up one hundredth of a yen from 159.34 on Nov. 17.
Money-market broker Tokyo Tanshi reported a weighted average unsecured overnight call rate of 1.227%, unchanged from the previous day. The rate measures one-day borrowing in Japan’s call money market, for which the Bank of Japan publishes a daily series.
What would put pressure on Bitcoin positions
A trader borrowing yen short-term to hold Bitcoin faces higher costs to renew the loan if funding rates rise. If the trader sells Bitcoin for dollars and leaves the yen debt unhedged, a stronger yen makes repaying the loan in dollar terms more expensive.
Bank for International Settlements researchers documented that feedback during the August 2024 unwind in leveraged currency and equity trades.
Bitfinex reported that aggregate Bitcoin futures open interest fell to 645,750 BTC over Nov. 14 and 15, 8% below Nov. 11. The futures total shows how much exposure was outstanding but gives no breakdown by funding currency.
BIS research showed that although it identified $271 billion in yen-denominated bank loans to non-bank borrowers outside Japan in the first quarter of 2024, it could not determine how much was used for carry trades.
The Finance Ministry plans to offer about ¥300 billion at the Nov. 25 reopening of a 40-year bond, the next test of long-dated demand.
A stronger signal for Bitcoin would be rising short-term yen borrowing costs or a sustained strengthening of the yen, alongside shrinking futures exposure and evidence that traders cutting positions had yen liabilities.
items.title: Japan bond yields surge to 3.75%, hiding a quiet Bitcoin trap

items.content:
谷歌Gemini 4 Neon发布：跑分反超Carbon，排名全球第三

动察 Beating AI 快讯，谷歌发布 Gemini 4 Neon，定位介于旗舰模型 Carbon 和轻量模型 Hydrogen 之间。它主要面向复杂编程、数据分析和长时间运行的 AI Agent，主打接近旗舰的能力和更快的任务处理速度。

独立评测机构 Artificial Analysis 的测试显示，Neon 在最高推理档位下取得 61 分，超过 Carbon 高推理档的 60 分、Claude Opus 5.5 的 59 分和 GPT-6.2 Sol 的 57 分，排名全球第三。

Neon 最明显的优势是速度。在各自最高推理档位下，它完成一项任务平均需要约 21 分钟，Carbon 则需要约 36 分钟，耗时减少约 40%。Neon 的输出速度达到每秒约 110 个 Token，接近 Carbon 的两倍。

编程方面，Neon 在 Terminal-Bench 4.1 上取得 65.2%，与 Opus 5.5 的 65.8% 几乎持平。它还针对 Google Antigravity 做了适配，可以充当总指挥，调度多个 Hydrogen 子智能体并行工作。在 SWE-sweep 测试中，Neon 使用简易智能体框架时得分为 12.8%，换成 Antigravity 框架后达到 39.0%。

Neon 支持 100 万 Token 上下文。API 每百万输入 Token 收费 3 美元，输出 15 美元，比 Claude Opus 5.5 和 Carbon 的原价（4 美元、20 美元）便宜 25%。不过，Carbon 目前还在打五折，因此 Neon 暂时反而更贵。等到 12 月 1 日 Carbon 恢复原价，Neon 才会比它便宜。

Neon 已在 Gemini API、AI Studio、Gemini 应用和 Antigravity 上线。Google AI Pro 和 Ultra 订阅用户均可使用，而 Carbon 在 Gemini 应用和 Antigravity 中仅面向 Ultra 用户开放。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Fed officials saw October rate hold as a ‘close call,’ minutes show
The latest FOMC minutes suggest greater appetite for higher rates than the Fed’s 10–2 vote indicated, with markets now pricing in a December hike.
A few Federal Reserve officials who supported holding interest rates steady in October considered the decision a “close call,” according to minutes released Wednesday, as policymakers signaled that further hikes would likely be needed to bring inflation back to 2%.
The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10–2 in October to keep its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4%. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored a quarter-point increase. The minutes showed that a few participants who supported holding rates steady still viewed the decision as a “close call.”
“The minutes suggest broader support for an October hike than the 10–2 vote alone implied — and that was before payrolls and CPI both came in hot,” Lewis Huang, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitget, told Cointelegraph.
With markets overwhelmingly expecting a December rate hike, attention is shifting to whether the Fed will raise rates by a quarter or half percentage point.
“With a December hike already fully priced in, the focus shifts to the size of the move and the policy path beyond December,” said Huang.
CME FedWatch has put the odds of a December quarter-point hike at about 90% and a half-point increase at about 10% at the time of writing.
Bitcoin was trading around $62,300 after the minutes were released. Huang said a further rise in Treasury yields and the dollar would add pressure to Bitcoin, which was already trading below its 200-week moving average near $68,000.
“For Bitcoin, a break below the weekend low near $62,000 could extend the sell-off,” Huang said.
Fed officials flag AI inflation and financial stability risks
Fed officials also raised concerns about the inflationary impact of AI investment, with many participants noting that demand for related equipment was straining supply and pushing up consumer technology prices. Several warned that the pressures were spreading beyond industries directly involved in data center construction.
Related: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December
Officials separately discussed the financial risks if AI investments disappointed.
“Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures,” the minutes show. “A few participants remarked that AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms.”
Fabian Dori, chief investment officer at Sygnum Bank, said markets were already pricing in a series of hikes into next year.
“That likely keeps long-term yields and the dollar firm, and the question for Bitcoin is whether debasement concerns and advancing institutional adoption can outweigh it,” Dori said.
Magazine: How to preserve wealth and access funds during a national emergency
items.title: Fed officials saw October rate hold as a ‘close call,’ minutes show

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据美通社报道，富途控股（Nasdaq: FUTU）旗下全资信托机构富途信托宣布推出「数字资产家族信托」，协助香港高净值家庭及家族办公室将主流加密货币与传统金融资产纳入同一信托架构，统筹规划数字财富的持有、托管衔接、日常管理及跨代传承安排。该服务主要面向香港税务居民家庭及家族办公室，信托内综合资产门槛为等值 300 万美元起。

据介绍，该信托围绕两项安排设计。其一为「股币同构」统一治理，客户可将获接纳的比特币（BTC）、以太币（ETH）等主流数字资产，连同港股、美股、ETF 等传统金融资产纳入同一信托架构，并按需衔接香港持牌证券商、银行及持牌虚拟资产交易平台等专业机构。其二为保留投资权、交易与提资分离，在香港法律许可的范围内，客户可通过信托契约设置保留权力或授权机制，继续参与或指示获准范围内的投资决策；但投资交易权与资产提取权严格分离，任何提款或分配均须遵循信托程序。

富途信托行政总裁林伟彬表示，很多客户清楚如何操作数字资产，却未必有机会用家人听得懂的方式完整交代账户、授权与传承意愿，希望通过清晰的持有架构、专业托管与接续机制，为客户与家人预留长远安排。

特朗普政府成立网络犯罪威胁中心，打击加密货币诈骗等非法活动

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据彭博社报道，特朗普政府周三宣布成立新的网络犯罪威胁中心（Threat Disruption Center），以打击针对美国民众的加密货币诈骗及其他网络犯罪。该中心将作为国土安全特别工作组的技术资源与协作平台，由 30 多个联邦机构及 440 多个州和地方合作伙伴组成，主要负责处理受害者举报、追踪诈骗资金流向、识别犯罪分子使用的加密钱包及寻找其他潜在受害者。

作为该计划的一部分，美国政府向区块链分析公司 TRM Labs 授予一份为期一年的合同，金额约 9500 万美元，用于提供技术支持，包括作为主要调查工具的 AI 平台。目前已有超过 60 名 TRM 员工参与该项目。TRM Labs CEO Esteban Castaño 表示，政府希望利用 AI 近乎实时地筛查受害者举报，并及时发现有助于追回受害者资金的行动机会。

根据美国联邦调查局（FBI）数据，2025 年网络犯罪造成的损失接近 210 亿美元，同比增长约 25%，其中加密货币相关损失占比超过一半。该合同于今年 7 月以非竞争性方式授予 TRM Labs，其竞争对手 Chainalysis 随后提起诉讼，指控合同授予过程存在不合理之处，但诉讼已于 9 月被驳回。

美联储会议纪要释放明确鹰派信号，几乎所有官员预期后续加息，理事沃勒呼吁考虑12月加息50个基点

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，美联储于凌晨公布的 10 月货币政策会议纪要显示，几乎所有与会官员认为，为确保通胀及时回落至 2% 目标，未来几个月进一步上调联邦基金利率目标区间可能是适宜的。这一表态被市场解读为明显鹰派，进一步巩固了 12 月加息预期。与此同时，美联储理事克里斯托弗·沃勒（Christopher Waller）当天在公开表态中态度更为激进，明确提出可考虑在 12 月一次性加息 50 个基点，或向市场发出更清晰的加速收紧信号。⁠

根据会议纪要，10 月 27 日至 28 日举行的联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）会议最终以 10 票赞成、2 票反对的结果，决定将基准利率维持在 3.75% 至 4% 的区间不变。理事丽莎·库克（Lisa Cook）和克利夫兰联储行长贝丝·哈马克（Beth Hammack）投下反对票，主张当时即加息 25 个基点。纪要指出，支持维持利率不变的官员中，部分人认为这一决定是「险胜」（close call）。与此同时，「几乎所有」与会者判断，根据其对通胀和劳动力市场的基准展望，未来几个月进一步加息「可能是合适的」。少数官员还表示，如果后续通胀数据表现不利，12 月会议甚至可以考虑加息幅度超过 25 个基点。⁠

纪要还显示，人工智能（AI）基础设施建设成为本次会议的重要讨论议题。官员们认为，相关需求可能成为通胀的重要来源，同时也可能带来潜在的金融稳定风险。多数官员强调，当前通胀压力仍然广泛存在，需通过进一步收紧政策加以应对。

在会议纪要公布前后，沃勒于 11 月 18 日接受 CNBC 采访时发表了更为鹰派的看法。他表示自己「非常非常担心通胀」，认为通胀「方向错了，而且正在扩散」，并非仅集中在少数领域。沃勒指出，如果美联储希望真正将通胀拉回目标，就需要采取更积极的行动，要么在 12 月一次性加息 50 个基点，要么明确向市场释放 2027 年将加快加息节奏的信号。他进一步表示，可能需要「给市场一个冲击」（shock people），打破企业和消费者将 3% 左右的通胀视为正常水平的心理预期，否则仅逆转去年的降息可能还不足以实现目标。⁠

市场目前对 12 月加息 25 个基点的预期已非常充分，而对 50 个基点加息的定价仍较低。分析人士认为，本次会议纪要与沃勒的表态叠加，进一步强化了美联储继续收紧的路径，但最终 12 月会议的具体决定仍将取决于后续通胀数据的表现。当前利率水平、AI 相关投资对经济的影响，以及通胀扩散程度，仍是官员们重点关注的变量。

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，埃隆·马斯克通过视频连线出席在纽约举行的《纽约时报》DealBook 峰会，当时他在中国。在与《纽约时报》安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金对谈时，马斯克谈到本轮美国中期选举捐款时说：「花了这么多钱却没看到什么成效，我觉得自己挺傻的，又或者，如果没有这笔投入，情况可能会更糟。」他表示，如果能让时间倒流，自己会少花一些钱，「这当然表明，美国选举并不只取决于金钱。显然，你可以把很多钱投入选举，但效果相对有限，我认为这次就是如此。」

Anthropic IPO信息速览：定价83美元高于指导区间，总募资超千亿美元成史上最大IPO

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，人工智能公司 Anthropic（Claude 母公司）已完成首次公开募股（IPO）定价。本次 IPO 将发行价定在每股 83 美元，高于此前设定的 70–78 美元区间。同时，公司扩大发行规模，最终出售约 9.8 亿股，合计募资约 813 亿美元，一举超过 SpaceX 今年 6 月的纪录，成为历史上规模最大的 IPO 之一。

除公开募集外，Google、Nvidia、Microsoft、AMD 等科技巨头还将以相同价格通过私募方式认购约 260 亿美元股份（主要为无投票权类别），进一步强化其在 AI 生态中的布局。

Anthropic 的市值将取决于总流通股数，但这一股价将使其估值超过此前 1.4 万亿美元的目标。该股预计将于周四在纳斯达克开始交易，股票代码为「ANT」。

此次上市是对 AI 行业的一次重大考验，该行业近期经历了一系列冲击，包括在中期选举投票中感受到的剧烈反弹，以及上周英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋的离职。市场本就因担忧利率上升将使许多数据中心开发商和新型云服务商（neoclouds）的债务变得难以承受而紧张不安。

根据招股说明书，截至 9 月 30 日的九个月内，Anthropic 表示其营收为 332.4 亿美元，较去年同期增长约 1200%。该公司报告称，该九个月期间净亏损 1040 亿美元，但其中大部分是由于可转换票据和衍生负债的公允价值变动。文件显示，Anthropic 在 2025 年同期亏损 251 亿美元。

Anthropic 在一份修订文件中表示，截至 10 月底，其年化营收约为 810 亿美元，较上月增加 100 亿美元。

56%英伟达员工盼黄仁勋回归，副总裁巴克在继任候选人中支持度最高

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据韩联社报道，职场社区 Blind 利用其对话式人工智能服务 Blind Claire，对美国时间 11 月 12 日至 16 日期间 531 名美国英伟达在职员工在公开频道发布的 627 条相关帖子进行分析。结果显示，认为黄仁勋应当回归的意见占 56%，比例最高；若回归难以实现，24% 的意见主张提拔能够延续其商业愿景的内部高管，20% 主张引入外部人士。

在继任候选人的相对支持度上，若将黄仁勋的支持度设为 100，英伟达副总裁伊恩·巴克为 27，在候选人群中居首；曾任职英伟达的 Arm 首席执行官雷内·哈斯为 4.5，现任临时首席执行官、首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯为 4.0，黄仁勋长女麦迪逊·黄为 2.5。以人物正面提及比例计，黄仁勋为 72%，巴克为 60%，哈斯为 43%，克雷斯为 21%。巴克已在英伟达工作逾 20 年，主导过 GPU 计算平台 CUDA 的开发，并出席了英伟达三季度业绩电话会，但未直接回答分析师提问。

Blind 数据分析师表示，英伟达在职员工对首席执行官候选人的支持与对其个人能力的评价密切关联，要求重新任用黄仁勋的舆论，也源于认为无人能够替代其能力的不安。

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 19 日，据美联储公布的 10 月 27 日至 28 日货币政策会议纪要，联邦公开市场委员会以 10 票赞成、2 票反对，决定将联邦基金利率目标区间维持在 3.75% 至 4%。投票反对的委员为丽莎·库克和贝丝·哈马克，两人主张在此次会议上将利率目标区间上调 25 个基点。

会议纪要显示，在未来数月的政策前景上，几乎所有与会者认为，基于其对通胀和劳动力市场的基线展望，进一步上调联邦基金利率目标区间可能是合适的，这与 9 月经济预测摘要大体一致，目的是确保通胀及时回到 2% 的目标。两名与会者指出，如果后续通胀数据表现不佳，下次会议或可考虑加息超过 25 个基点。另有少数与会者表示，通胀可能比预期更为持久，届时或有必要转向更加紧缩的政策立场。部分与会者主张在 10 月会议上加息 25 个基点，认为当前政策立场不够紧缩；其中少数人警告，进一步推迟加息可能使高通胀趋于固化，或迫使日后采取更大幅度、更具干扰性的紧缩。

多数与会者支持此次维持利率不变，认为积累更多信息有助于确定适合的政策立场。其中少数人在支持维持利率的同时表示，这一决定较为艰难。许多与会者强调，应明确传达维持利率目标区间的决定并不意味着委员会削弱了及时将通胀恢复至 2% 的承诺。与会者表示，未来政策决定将取决于后续数据、前景变化及风险平衡。委员会同意下次会议于 12 月 8 日至 9 日举行。

items.author: Liam 'Akiba' Wright
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitwise sold 23.7 million XRP to fund third-quarter cash redemptions as its holdings grew by 126.3 million XRP.
- Franklin received 41.3 million XRP in kind and bought 26.6 million for creations, with zero third-quarter redemptions.
- The Nov. 17 ETF outflow estimates measure net withdrawals and leave the amount of XRP sold that day unresolved.
Bitwise’s quarterly filings show its XRP ETF sold 23.7 million XRP to meet cash redemptions from July through September 2026, even as the fund increased its holdings by 126.3 million XRP.
The quarter’s redemption sales slightly exceeded the 22.9 million XRP the fund sold for the same purpose in the entire first half of the year.
Bitwise’s holdings climbed from 286.8 million XRP at the end of June to 413.1 million at the end of September. The Sept. 30 quarterly report, filed Nov. 6, records both the XRP the fund sold for redemptions and the larger amount it added for new shares.
Subtracting the six-month XRP schedule from the nine-month schedule isolates what happened in the third quarter. Bitwise bought 87.9 million tokens to back newly issued shares and received another 62.3 million XRP in kind.
Together, those flows added 150.2 million tokens before the fund’s cash redemption sales and roughly 241,383 XRP transferred to pay sponsor fees. Bitwise reported zero in-kind redemptions for the quarter.
Bitwise created 13.75 million shares and redeemed 2.42 million, leaving a net increase of 11.33 million shares, an increase in shares that masks the gross redemptions that took place along the way.
The sponsor arranges a sale of the underlying XRP for a cash redemption and pays out the proceeds, less a transaction fee. In-kind redemption delivers the token itself to the authorized firm or its designee.
The Franklin Templeton XRP ETF’s third-quarter filing shows the firm issued 6.25 million shares in the quarter, including 3.8 million in kind and 2.45 million for cash. The fund received 41.3 million tokens in kind and bought 26.6 million for creations, and recorded zero share redemptions.
A separate Canary XRP ETF filing puts that fund’s cash redemption sales at 9.55 million XRP for the nine months through Sept. 30. Canary reported zero tokens delivered for in-kind redemptions over those nine months.
What Nov. 17 XRP outflows leave unresolved
In its Nov. 18 update, Crypto ETF’s fund table estimated $6.1 million in net outflows for Nov. 17 based on three of five tracked funds.
Alpha Finance’s daily figures also put the rounded net outflow at $6.1 million, with data for all five funds it tracks. Alpha Finance estimated $5 million in outflows from Canary and $1.1 million from Grayscale, compared with $4.9 million and $1.2 million in the Crypto ETF snapshot.
Canary’s daily share history shows 490,000 fewer shares outstanding on Nov. 17 than on Nov. 16. Bitwise’s fund data showed 36.44 million shares on Nov. 16 and 406.8 million XRP in its Nov. 17 holdings table.
If issuers break out the same categories in their next filings, it will be possible to measure sales for fourth-quarter redemptions and distinguish them from in-kind transfers and fees.
items.title: Bitwise offloads 23.7M XRP while silently stacking 126M more

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Michael Saylor's STRC fell to its lowest level since August despite Strategy spending $2.7 billion on buybacks.
- Strategy spent $1.4 billion buying STRC near $100, yet shares have plunged toward $95, pushing the annualized yield to roughly 12.5%.
- With just $332 million in buyback capacity left, Strategy faces questions over further repurchases as Peter Schiff warns of potential Bitcoin sales.
Strategy's (formerly MicroStrategy) STRC preferred stock plunged to its lowest level since August on Wednesday despite the company's multibillion-dollar repurchase campaign.
The Michael Saylor-led company's preferred shares fell to $95.51 before recovering to $96.16, according to Strategy's data. The decline left STRC roughly 4% below its $100 stated amount, pushing its annualized yield to approximately 12.5%.
Regular-session, unadjusted daily closes through Nov. 17. Nov. 18 is an incomplete trading day: final $97.00 point is a timestamped 12:39 p.m. ET intraday quote. The $100 series is STRC stated amount, and displayed prices are verified against Stock Analysis.
The selloff comes despite Strategy spending about $2.67 billion repurchasing STRC shares since July to stabilize the security near $100.
An earlier analysis found that the company spent about $1.4 billion on repurchases between Sept. 28 and Nov. 15, with weekly average purchase prices ranging from $99.06 to $99.93.
That accounted for more than half of its total repurchase spending, even as the discount to STRC's stated amount had nearly disappeared.
Open $98.50, high $98.69, low $95.50, latest available quote $97.00 at 12:39 p.m. ET. Bars are dollars below STRC’s $100 stated amount, and negative numbers are discounts.
This sustained intervention has left just $332.2 million available under its $3 billion preferred-stock repurchase authorization, raising questions about how much more capital Strategy will commit if selling pressure persists.
Strategy CEO defends STRC's dividend coverage
Despite the renewed weakness, Strategy CEO Phong Le has defended STRC's financial structure and its ability to generate income for investors.
In a Nov. 17 statement, Le said:
“STRC is Digital Credit: high income, low volatility, and 44 years of dividend coverage. Built for income investors as TradFi and DeFi converge.”
His assessment contrasts with economist Peter Schiff, who warned that the security's continued decline could eventually force Strategy to sell Bitcoin.
Schiff said:
“Despite the buybacks, $STRC is collapsing. At $96 the current yield is 12.5% and rising.”
Schiff argued that Strategy would have to exhaust its cash reserves to support the stock before selling Bitcoin to finance additional repurchases. He suggested raising or suspending dividends as an alternative.
However, Le's 44-year coverage assertion reflects Strategy's broader Bitcoin-backed financial capacity.
The company's latest disclosures showed that its $4.75 billion dedicated dollar reserve and $151.2 million in unrestricted cash provide approximately 3.4 years of coverage for preferred dividends and debt-interest obligations.
Strategy also held 850,849 BTC as of Nov. 15, providing another source of liquidity through potential asset sales.
The company has already authorized Bitcoin sales to support its preferred-stock obligations and repurchase programs, although it has recently relied more heavily on common-stock issuance.
items.title: Strategy’s STRC stock crashes to $95 despite promise of 44 years of dividends

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Ledger confirmed tampered hardware wallets in Berlin, is investigating two suspected units in Dubai, and found one affected Nano Gen5 in Southeast Asia, calling it “the same incident.”
- Every confirmed device carries the same modification designed to capture recovery phrases. Ledger says there’s no flaw in its chip or operating system, and no confirmed case from ledger.com.
- Ledger expects more devices to surface. It’s urging affected buyers to move funds to new wallets and is offering X-ray inspections at its factory in France.
The tampered Ledger wallets aren’t just a Southeast Asia problem anymore.
Ledger said Wednesday it has confirmed tampered hardware wallets in Berlin and is investigating reports of two more in Dubai, expanding a probe it had previously described as a localized incident in Southeast Asia.
“Our findings since then show tampered devices outside Southeast Asia. It is the same incident,” the company said in an update on its support site.
The investigation began last month after customers who bought devices from reseller CryptoBilis reported losses. Onchain investigators traced a suspected drain of about $87 million from hundreds of victim wallets across Ethereum, Tron, and Bitcoin.
Ledger said at the time that all confirmed cases were tied to CryptoBilis, and it later asked resellers in seven Asian markets to pull devices from sale.
Every device Ledger has confirmed shows the same kind of physical modification, designed to capture a user’s recovery phrase during setup. A recovery phrase, typically a string of 24 words, is the master key to a crypto wallet: anyone who has it can drain the funds.
Our investigation into the hardware implant incident we disclosed Oct 15th is ongoing, and we published an update: https://t.co/wx6mfQPr99
There is no flaw in Ledger's secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on https://t.co/vQ4QWa1D0f
We…
— Ledger (@Ledger) November 18, 2026
Ledger maintains there’s no flaw in its secure chip or operating system and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com.
In Germany, Ledger said a few tampered units were localized to Berlin, and it urged anyone who bought a Ledger device there since January 2026 to contact support.
In Dubai, it’s working with distribution partners to learn how two suspected units entered circulation. Those devices were bought at a Virgin Megastore location, according to multiple reports. Ledger also found one affected Nano Gen5 among the Southeast Asian resellers it previously paused.
The company expects more tampered devices to surface, though it says the number remains small overall. Its Donjon security team is examining suspected devices, and Ledger has asked resellers to pause sales wherever inspections are ongoing.
Customers worried about a device should stop using it, Ledger said. It advises moving funds to a new wallet created on a device bought directly from ledger.com, without reusing the old recovery phrase or passphrase, since a tampered device can capture both. It also recommends filing a report with local authorities.
For a limited time, Ledger is offering physical inspections, including X-rays, at its factory in Vierzon, France.
“We will never ask for your recovery phrase,” the company said on X.
The last few months have been a rough stretch for hardware wallet markers overall. Rival manufacturer Trezor said this week that hackers who breached a third-party shipping partner likely took information tied to about 27,000 orders. That’s the company’s third such breach in as many months.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Coinbase's AI defenses blocked $4.7 million, or 91%, of attempted crypto transfers tied to an Elon Musk deepfake giveaway scam.
- The system stopped a customer's $100,000 payment, but the same user later bypassed its protection with a false explanation for a $5,000 transfer.
- The incident exposes a weakness in AI fraud prevention as exchanges struggle to protect customers who insist on sending money despite scam warnings.
Coinbase said its AI defenses blocked $4.7 million in attempted cryptocurrency transfers tied to an Elon Musk deepfake scam.
The crypto exchange said on Nov. 17 that its automated fraud-prevention system stopped about 91% of the money customers tried to send to scammers promoting a fake Tesla cryptocurrency giveaway.
The fraudsters had created a lookalike YouTube livestream during a Tesla demonstration, using an AI-generated impersonation of Musk to promise viewers twice the cryptocurrency they deposited into designated wallets.
More than 500,000 people watched the fraudulent broadcast, while hundreds of Coinbase customers attempted to transfer millions of dollars within roughly two hours.
Unlike conventional account compromises, the customers were willingly authorizing the transactions, believing they were participating in a legitimate promotion.
Coinbase said its AI system intercepted suspicious payments in real time, engaging customers before their funds could leave the platform without requiring human intervention.
Coinbase AI stops $100,000 transfer but misses customer's second attempt
Despite preventing most attempted transfers, Coinbase disclosed an incident that illustrates the difficulty of protecting customers determined to complete suspicious payments.
Will Megson, Coinbase's vice president of product working on risk, revealed that one customer initially attempted to transfer $100,000 to the scammers.
The exchange's AI agent identified the suspicious transaction, explained the fraudulent giveaway and convinced the customer to abandon the payment.
However, the customer subsequently returned and attempted another transfer, this time for $5,000.
When questioned about the transaction, the customer falsely claimed the funds were intended for their daughter. The AI accepted the explanation and allowed the payment to proceed.
Megson acknowledged how difficult it is to distinguish legitimate payments from fraudulent transactions when customers provide misleading explanations.
The episode highlights a limitation of automated fraud detection: even when an exchange correctly identifies a scam, customers can still circumvent protections by changing their transaction details or misrepresenting their intentions.
Coinbase's system combines machine-learning models that identify suspicious transactions with an AI agent that examines the payment's context and questions customers about potential fraud.
The agent also assigns each response a confidence score before it reaches the customer.
The exchange said the system had not previously encountered the specific combination of a deepfake giveaway and a live product demonstration, but recognized familiar warning signs, including promises of guaranteed returns and irreversible payments.
Meanwhile, Coinbase said it is expanding its AI-powered fraud prevention efforts through improved detection models, automated reviews of suspicious transactions and faster identification of emerging scam techniques.
items.title: Coinbase AI blocks $4.7 million scam, but a simple lie exposes its weakness

items.author: Cointelegraph by Isabelle Castro
items.content:
Tether invokes The Big Short in swipe at S&P over USDT reserve risks
S&P Global made no downward adjustment in its latest Stablecoin Stability Assessment, as 5 is the lowest available score.
S&P Global Ratings has kept Tether’s USDt at the lowest level on its stablecoin stability scale as riskier assets take up a growing share of the token’s reserves.
In a report published Nov. 18, S&P scored USDt’s ability to hold its dollar peg at 5 (weak). The assessment is unchanged from November 2025.
Higher-risk holdings, including gold, Bitcoin (BTC), public equities, secured loans and corporate bonds, were equivalent to 28% of USDt (USDT) in circulation as of Sept. 30, up from 24% a year earlier. “A significant drop in the value of these assets could lead to USDT being undercollateralized,” S&P said in the report.
“The problem is S&P’s framework, not our reserves,” Tether told Cointelegraph. “Their own history shows the underlying problem,” it added, referencing The Big Short, the film about the 2008 financial crisis.
Tether’s Sept. 30 reserve report, attested by BDO, showed approximately $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities, leaving roughly $7.95 billion in excess assets. The agency added that it found further weaknesses but made no downward adjustment “because our assessment cannot be lower than 5.”
S&P questions reserve oversight safeguards
Among the additional weaknesses highlighted by S&P was the regulatory oversight of El Salvador, where Tether relocated in January 2025.
According to the report, the National Commission of Digital Assets of El Salvador (CNAD), the regulatory body which oversees Tether in the country, requires 70% of the reserves to be held in assets that can be liquidated within 30 days. The company said they considered the framework “broad,” allowing for the inclusion of relatively high-risk assets like gold, BTC and loans.
The S&P also pointed to the lack of a requirement to segregate the reserve assets, unlike those expected by regulators in the US and Europe. As there is no publicly available information about segregation, the report states, there is no insight into how they are insulated from broader corporate risks.
USDT’s breakdown of reserve assets. Source S&P Global
Audit disclosure remains a concern
In August 2026, KPMG confirmed they had issued an unqualified opinion on Tether’s 2025 accounts, in the company’s first “full independent audit”. The issuer highlighted that the audit supported the financial statements issued by the company.
However, S&P said the audited statements and the auditor’s report have not been published, which limits its ability to check the underlying information. Reserve reports also do not name the custodians and counterparties holding Tether’s assets, S&P said, and attestations remain quarterly while other stablecoins generally report monthly.
Related: Tether backs Bolivian fintech bringing USDT payments to food delivery and banking
At the time of S&P’s initial downgrade in 2025, Tether disputed the result. CEO Paolo Ardoino wrote on X, “we wear your loathing with pride,” pointing to past financial collapses as “proof” that traditional systems are broken.
Although the stability rating remained at 5, S&P ended the Nov. 18 report noting that Tether had maintained a good history of price stability, particularly in the last 12 months.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- All four chatbots provided information for potentially deadly attacks in under 12 hours, a congressional watchdog found.
- Investigators verified the feasibility of the plans but did not carry out attacks, and the tests cannot rank the models' safety.
- Senator Maggie Hassan wants hearings on AI safety as technology companies contend with a surge of software vulnerabilities and patches.
Four of the most widely used AI chatbots helped government investigators develop potentially deadly attack plans in less than 12 hours, despite safeguards intended to stop exactly that kind of request.
OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini and Grok all supplied usable information during covert testing by the Government Accountability Office, according to a report released Wednesday. Investigators posed as attackers, then checked the responses against real locations, available materials, and expert assessments.
Two systems assisted with plans involving improvised explosives in crowded U.S. cities. Two others supplied information for attacks on electrical infrastructure, according to the watchdog, which withheld the models' assignments and operational details to prevent copycat attempts.
Senator Maggie Hassan, the New Hampshire Democrat who requested the investigation, warned that a terrorist could obtain "a concrete playbook for how to carry out a deadly attack" in less than 12 hours, according to her statement.
Safeguards that didn't hold
The chatbots initially activated protections, including refusing requests, removing harmful information or suspending accounts. Investigators bypassed those barriers with common jailbreak techniques, which manipulate an AI system into ignoring its safety rules.
The GAO checked suggested locations, researched whether materials were available and consulted specialists about the plans' feasibility. Some answers contained errors, including misplaced roads on a map, and investigators did not construct explosives or execute an attack.
In the report, "viable" means somebody would likely be able to follow the information supplied, not that an attack was demonstrated to succeed. Each model was tested on one assigned scenario, and the agency said the results were not statistically representative or suitable for ranking the companies.
OpenAI and Google said the tests involved older models, while Anthropic acknowledged that determined users can sometimes extract harmful material. The companies described continuing improvements to safety systems, though the GAO concluded those protections failed in its tests.
This is not really new. The findings follow a previous research showing eight of 10 popular chatbots assisted simulated teenage users planning violent attacks. The separate study tested 720 responses and found the bots provided actionable help roughly three-quarters of the time.
AI's other security problem
The GAO findings arrive amid outages affecting banks, Microsoft services and the National Security Agency. Officials say the disruptions were separate incidents, not evidence of a coordinated AI-driven cyberattack, even as the rush to repair software flaws has created its own problems.
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton connected the NSA's outage to patching work. Officials described the recent breakdowns as maintenance-related, although individual organizations offered different explanations for their failures.
AI tools now find vulnerabilities faster than human teams can test and deploy fixes. Last month, the AI-assisted discovery of critical PHP flaws pushed website operators into an urgent patching campaign; the software powers a large share of the web.
The sheer volume is becoming another problem. VulnCheck data reveals there have been more than 100,000 software vulnerabilities logged this year by November 13, more than twice the total for 2025. Engineers still have to evaluate and deploy fixes without breaking the systems they are meant to protect.
That acceleration cuts both ways. Defenders gain powerful tools for finding weaknesses, but hasty repairs can disrupt essential systems, and malicious users may gain faster access to attack planning.
Hassan said she will make AI safety legislation an early priority when she takes over the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee in January. She plans hearings examining risks to public safety and critical infrastructure; the GAO itself made no formal policy recommendations.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Palmer Luckey revealed SLAB, a proposed ocean platform designed to last 1,000 years and allow American industries to operate outside certain state and local regulations.
- Luckey says the project received funding at a $1 billion valuation in 2017, but has not disclosed its location, construction status or operating timeline.
- In an exchange on X, Luckey said he wants people to access medicine currently illegal in the United States, raising questions about the limits of offshore regulation.
Palmer Luckey, the billionaire founder of Oculus and defense technology company Anduril, is spending over a billion dollars to have a private island where he can do things without worrying about U.S. laws.
He wants to build a massive industrial platform in the ocean where American businesses can operate without some of the regulations they face on land. And he has apparently been working on the idea for nearly a decade.
In an X post published Wednesday, Luckey revealed a project called SLAB, a proposed seastead with a 1,000-year design life that he says could support industries ranging from metal processing and oil refining to medical research and treatment.
Selling Oculus to Facebook in 2014 gave me money for helicopter flight lessons and developing a seastead called SLAB with a 1,000 year design life.
The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing,… pic.twitter.com/aJkd0eOgLF
— Palmer Luckey (@PalmerLuckey) November 18, 2026
His goal, he wrote, is to create an industrial base cheaper than land and free from state and local laws that he believes are crippling critical American industries. Luckey described the project as a way to strengthen the United States rather than escape it, calling it a "relief valve" for outdated regulations.
“Me and a few close friends cashed it up at a $1B valuation back in 2017, and while it still has a long way to go, there has been significant progress towards my goal of reviving manifest destiny and westward expansion,” he wrote.
Luckey said he used proceeds from Facebook's 2014 acquisition of Oculus to finance the project.
The announcement included an AI-generated illustration of a gigantic offshore platform, rather than photographs of an operating facility so it’s hard to know which type of endeavor he’s dedicating his time and money to.
Luckey said he decided to disclose SLAB after learning that journalists were preparing to describe it as a floating AI data center. He rejected that characterization as incomplete, saying the project was considerably older and "way cooler than that."
Medical treatments outside US regulations
Luckey provided a more specific indication of his ambitions in a heated exchange with journalist Joshua Topolsky, who questioned whether creating an offshore community was a sensible way to modernize medical research.
Topolsky argued that regulatory reform could happen without constructing an island in the ocean and challenged Luckey to identify which existing rules had prevented him from pursuing medical advances.
Luckey responded that he would rather build a place where people could save their families with "safe but currently illegal medicine ASAP" than wait for lawmakers to reform the system.
He accused political interests and large pharmaceutical companies of obstructing change, arguing that conventional reform would require legislation capable of securing support from 60 senators.
Does moving offshore actually escape American law?
Luckey's plan also faces a significant legal complication: moving an operation into the ocean does not automatically place it outside American jurisdiction.
When another X user asked how close SLAB could operate to San Francisco without falling under its jurisdiction, Luckey answered, "Three miles."
That generally corresponds to the boundary of California's state-controlled coastal waters, according to the U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management.
That said, federal jurisdiction extends considerably farther. The United States has a 12-nautical-mile territorial sea and a 200-nautical-mile exclusive economic zone, where it retains authority over certain economic activities and the construction and use of artificial islands, according to NOAA guidance.
The applicable rules would depend on SLAB's location, whether it floats or is attached to the seabed, and how it is registered. Even vessels operating on the high seas remain subject to applicable maritime laws and the jurisdiction of their flag states, so it’s not as if he’d be living in an anarchist fairy tale.
Medical research presents its own complications, if that’s what he’s actually doing. The FDA requires foreign clinical studies submitted in support of U.S. drug approvals to meet good clinical practice standards, including independent ethical review and informed consent. Conducting treatment offshore would not, by itself, make an unapproved drug legal for sale in the United States.
Previous seasteading experiments have encountered similar jurisdictional disputes. A floating community off Thailand triggered a confrontation with authorities in 2019, while a subsequent project in Panama adopted boat registration to operate within an existing legal framework.
This is all, of course, speculation. Luckey has not publicly identified SLAB's proposed location, the specific regulations it would avoid, or the medical treatments he hopes to make available. He has also not announced a construction deadline or provided independently verifiable details of the project's current physical development.

Ledger warns Berlin customers as hardware wallet tampering investigation expands
Ledger advised customers who purchased devices in Berlin since January 2026 to contact support as it investigates suspected hardware implants in Germany and Dubai.
Ledger has warned customers who purchased hardware wallets in Berlin since January 2026 to contact its support team as the company investigates reports of tampered devices in Germany and the United Arab Emirates.
In a Wednesday update, Ledger said its investigation into a hardware wallet tampering campaign had identified several suspicious devices in Berlin. The company also acknowledged reports of tampered devices in Dubai, where two customers recently reported losing a combined $604,000 in cryptocurrency.
Ledger said the incidents were connected to the same distribution-channel tampering campaign first investigated in Southeast Asia in October, when the company asked authorized reseller CryptoBilis to suspend sales and shipments amid reports of cryptocurrency thefts. Ledger also confirmed that one Ledger Nano Gen 5 had been affected in the region.
According to the hardware wallet maker, all confirmed tampered devices contained similar physical modifications designed to capture users’ recovery phrases during setup. The company said it had found no vulnerability in its secure chip or operating system and no confirmed cases involving devices purchased directly from its website.
Ledger is also offering physical inspections, including X-ray analysis, at its factory in Vierzon, France, for customers concerned their devices may have been compromised.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Germany's Bundestag approved a bill allowing customs to freeze suspicious Bitcoin holdings, including assets stored in self-custody wallets.
- Authorities could restrict crypto transfers for up to 180 days without controlling private keys, challenging the legal freedom of self-custody holders.
- Identifying wallet owners and enforcing transfer bans remain major hurdles, while the legislation awaits final approval.
Germany's parliament has approved legislation allowing customs authorities to freeze suspicious crypto holdings, including assets stored in self-custody wallets.
The Bundestag passed the bill on Nov. 12, advancing a broader government effort to combat money laundering and financial crime by expanding authorities' powers to investigate assets of questionable origin.
Under the proposed legislation, German customs could temporarily freeze significant assets, including cryptocurrencies, when factual evidence raises doubts about their lawful origin.
The approved committee text identifies assets worth more than €100,000 as a general benchmark for significant holdings. Authorities could also combine closely connected assets when determining whether they qualify.
Customs would initially have 30 days to investigate suspicious holdings, with a finance court authorized to extend the restriction by another 150 days if investigators demonstrate credible doubts about their origin and grounds for further investigation.
The legislation, however, has not completed its final approval process. As of Nov. 18, final consideration by the Bundesrat, Germany's chamber representing the states, and publication in the Federal Law Gazette remained outstanding.
Germany's Bitcoin freeze powers face a self-custody challenge
The proposed rules could have different consequences depending on whether investors hold their Bitcoin through centralized exchanges or control their wallets directly.
For assets held on an exchange, German authorities could issue an enforceable attachment order requiring the custodian to restrict withdrawals from an affected account.
The mechanism draws on Germany's existing tax enforcement provisions, which allow authorities to prevent third parties from releasing assets subject to a legally enforceable attachment.
However, enforcing similar restrictions against self-custody wallets presents a more complicated challenge.
Unlike centralized exchanges, self-custody wallets allow users to control the private keys needed to authorize Bitcoin transactions without relying on a financial intermediary.
Germany's proposed framework addresses such holdings by treating cryptocurrencies as attachable property rights.
Under Section 321 of the German Fiscal Code, authorities can attach certain property rights without involving a third party by serving the holder with a legal prohibition on disposing of them.
Applied to eligible self-custodied Bitcoin, this could prohibit an owner from transferring the affected assets without automatically removing their ability to authorize blockchain transactions.
Consequently, an individual could remain technically capable of moving Bitcoin despite being legally prohibited from doing so.
Germany's Blockchain Bundesverband highlighted this enforcement challenge in a submission on an earlier version of the legislation. The industry association explained that authorities must distinguish between cryptocurrencies held by custodians and assets controlled directly by individuals.
It also warned that identifying a blockchain wallet does not necessarily establish who controls its assets, particularly where multiple parties share transaction-signing authority.
These complications could make enforcing restrictions on self-custody wallets harder than freezing balances held by regulated exchanges.
The legislation also distinguishes temporary asset freezes from permanent confiscation, which would require a separate finance court decision establishing that the property originated unlawfully.
Should the bill complete Germany's legislative process, its effectiveness against self-custodied crypto holdings will depend on authorities' ability to identify wallet controllers and enforce legal restrictions without direct control of their private keys.
items.title: Germany moves to freeze Bitcoin for up to 180 days, even without access to private keys

items.content:
Bain Capital Crypto leads $110M Variational round at $1.5B valuation
Variational raised $110 million at a $1.5 billion valuation to expand Omni’s derivatives markets and increase trading limits.
Onchain derivatives trading platform Variational has raised $110 million in a funding round led by Bain Capital Crypto, valuing the company at $1.5 billion as it seeks to challenge traditional brokerages by connecting crypto traders with liquidity from established financial markets.
The Series B round also received backing from Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV and 50T Funds, according to the company’s Wednesday announcement.
Variational powers Omni, a platform offering leveraged exposure to more than 550 crypto and traditional markets. Unlike Hyperliquid, which maintains separate order books for its markets, Variational aggregates liquidity from onchain and off-chain sources, including Hyperliquid itself, a company spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
“Our unique model allows us to bridge off-chain liquidity to on-chain traders,” the spokesperson said, adding that liquidity from its unnamed tier-one market maker remains off-chain.
Since launching in early 2025, Omni has processed more than $475 billion in trading volume across over 100,000 accounts, the company said. Traditional markets now account for more than half of its daily trading volume.
Variational also launched its swaps product in September, which has since generated more than $80 billion in trading volume, according to the company.
Variational looks to compete with traditional brokerages
Despite traditional assets accounting for most daily trading volume, Variational’s customers remain primarily crypto-native retail traders, a company spokesperson told Cointelegraph. Asked about competing with traditional brokerages such as Robinhood and Interactive Brokers, the spokesperson pointed to the need to make the platform more accessible to users unfamiliar with cryptocurrency.
Related: Hyperliquid Strategies seeks futures registration for perps
“The platform needs to abstract away the ‘crypto’ feel,” the spokesperson said, adding that the company is developing email-based account registration and alternative deposit methods to remove the current requirements for crypto wallets and USDC.
Variational faces stiff competition in onchain derivatives trading. Hyperliquid recorded approximately $274 billion in reported trading volume over the past 30 days, compared with $82 billion for Lighter and $62 billion for Variational, according to DeFiLlama data at the time of writing on Wednesday. Variational also ranked third in open interest at approximately $688 million, behind Hyperliquid’s $5.7 billion and Aster’s $1.2 billion.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Bryan O'Shea
items.content:
Binance says it obtained $6.5B worldwide freezing order after hack
The court orders allow legal notices to be served via blockchain and provide for a continuously updated list of 26,000 wallet addresses linked to stolen assets, Binance’s lawyers said.
Binance said it has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts as it seeks to recover assets stolen in its record Oct. 29 hack.
The court orders target unidentified perpetrators of the attack and are intended to help issuers, exchanges and other partners freeze and return stolen assets, the company said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph on Wednesday.
The orders can be served via blockchain, according to M. Kendall Day of Gibson Dunn, which represents Binance. This allows legal notices to be delivered to wallet addresses rather than through traditional channels. Day said market participants would also be notified of updates to a “living list” of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets.
Binance said some businesses require formal court orders before they can release, transfer or return frozen funds. The injunction’s $6.5 billion amount is not a tally of recovered assets, and the statement did not disclose how much had so far been returned under the orders.
Binance also said it obtained orders requiring stolen assets to be handed over. Separate interim orders cover assets frozen by certain named parties against whom no wrongdoing is alleged.
Binance pursues stolen asset recovery
The legal action follows other efforts to secure the stolen funds in the wake of the hack, the largest-ever in the crypto industry. As Cointelegraph reported on Nov. 13, the US Justice Department said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in assets stolen from Binance. That amount was part of more than $2.7 billion frozen through government and private sector efforts, the DOJ said.
Related: Binance hack may push institutions to outside custody, FalconX exec says
As Cointelegraph previously reported, the attackers converted stolen stablecoins into assets such as Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH), which cannot be frozen, as they lack a central issuer. Blocking the stolen tokens also does not mean they’ll be returned to Binance.
Binance said last week it had since completed coverage of affected assets after committing more than $6.34 billion from its various treasury, Secure Asset Fund for Users and insurance funds. Still, replenishing customer assets is separate from recovering the stolen cryptocurrencies from the hack.
Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US
Binance pursues expansion across Asia
Separately, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told Reuters on Wednesday that the exchange plans to enter five Asian markets in 2027, prioritizing South and Southeast Asia. He did not name the markets and said details were expected in the first quarter.
Seker also said Binance did not need fresh capital to absorb the losses from the October hack.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Google is rolling out Genie 4 to eligible AI Ultra subscribers through Project Genie, after announcing the model in October.
- Users can change generated worlds during exploration, with AI-created ambient audio and interactive character dialogue.
- Project Genie also adds an AI creation assistant, a community gallery, and longer sessions for the older Genie 3 model.
Google is opening Genie 4 to eligible AI Ultra subscribers, letting people create digital worlds they can walk through, change with a text prompt, and even populate with characters that talk back.
The company announced Wednesday that its latest world model is rolling out through Project Genie, a browser-based experiment for generating interactive environments. Genie 4 was unveiled in October, but access until now had been limited to trusted testers.
Instead of rendering a finished video from a prompt, Genie generates the scene as someone explores it. With the fourth model, users can type instructions midway through a session to change the weather, introduce a character, or steer what's happening without starting over.
#1 Searched Person on Google 2026?
Genie 4 also creates sound alongside the visuals, from wind and footsteps to dialogue that reacts to events in the scene. Google says the model improves the way people move and objects respond to physical forces, though those claims come from its own demonstrations rather than independent testing.
Now, the not so nice thing you need to know. The update is part of the Google AI Ultra subscription, which costs $199.99 per month in the United States. Google says eligible Ultra users can access the new experience now, while AI Pro subscribers can join a waitlist.
A genie that keeps getting better
Genie has come a long way from the side-scrolling experiments Google showed in 2024. The first version learned from more than 200,000 hours of gameplay footage and could turn a single image into a simple playable 2D environment, as Decrypt reported at the time.
Genie 2 moved the research into three-dimensional spaces later that year, allowing people or AI agents to navigate generated environments with keyboard and mouse controls. Genie 3 took another step toward continuous, real-time exploration, and Project Genie opened in January to adult Ultra subscribers in the United States.
Those early sessions lasted just 60 seconds, and character controls or physical behavior could be unreliable. Google is now keeping Genie 3 available alongside the new model, with sessions extended to three minutes, support for 360-degree panorama images, and the ability to connect multiple generated worlds into longer journeys.
That three-minute limit applies to the updated Genie 3 experience; Google did not specify a comparable session length for Genie 4 in Wednesday's announcement. Users can choose between the models depending on whether they want Genie 4's stronger visuals and audio or Genie 3's longer explorations.
The technology is not the same as a traditional game engine that builds a stable level with fully defined rules. Genie predicts what a world should look and sound like as it changes.
Google acknowledges that objects can drift or change between views, complex physics remain difficult, and generated speech or text may be inaccurate. It says Project Genie's audio and video carry SynthID watermarks and that inputs and outputs undergo safety screening.
Google has not announced when Genie 4 will become available to AI Pro subscribers beyond the new waitlist.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
Nvidia’s interim CEO has cautioned that the recently reported biggest top line in the company’s history — a record $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue — shouldn’t be considered as “filed” with the SEC.
The company has also admitted that its unpaid invoices have more than doubled from January to $81 billion.
Fueling suspicions about the quality of that $115.8 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported an SEC probe of Nvidia’s shareholder disclosures.
Short-seller Michael Burry also posted a list of doubts about Nvidia’s financials, while another famous short-seller, Carson Block, opened a new short-sale.
Nvidia furnished, not filed, its quarterly earnings
Merely “furnishing” this press release without certifying its contents, Nvidia disclaims associated liability for violations of SEC Sections 11, 12(a)(2), and 18.
Moreover, Nvidia’s extraordinary accounts receivable figure requires equally extraordinary faith that Nvidia’s customers will actually pay what they owe — especially with its stock trading at 20 times earnings.
The company “furnished” earnings numbers but declined to actually file a Form 10-Q yesterday, even though Nvidia has filed a formal 10-Q within a day of earnings for each of its last nine quarterly earnings reports without fail.
As opposed to “filed” earnings, “furnished” earnings carry no liability under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act, so shareholders cannot invoke it to sue over false statements, as they could over a filed report.
Sarbanes-Oxley officer certifications attach to 10-Q forms, not furnished exhibits. Those signatures attest that the financials are fairly presented.
For now, the record quarter exists only as furnished exhibits, not a certified report. Specifically, the AI chipmaker furnished Q3 results yesterday afternoon via an attachment to Form 8-K, a non-certified form.
As of publication time, Nvidia still hasn’t filed the Form 10-Q that normally would have arrived yesterday. Interim CEO Colette Kress wrote, “We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks,” giving no particular reason for the delay.
Read more: YouTube beat Wall Street to the Nvidia scandal
Nvidia investors noticed
Shares momentarily rallied more than 5% after the bell, but they were trading 2% lower than yesterday’s close by 1pm. Some analysts lowered price targets, with UBS cutting its price target by $20/share, Summit Insights cutting from Buy to Hold, and other bearish actions.
Since at least 2025, every other “Magnificent Seven” stock has filed its 10-Q within one day of furnishing earnings.
Although Nvidia’s supplemental data shows China revenue, including Hong Kong, up 272% from $2.97 billion a year ago to $11 billion this quarter, the document itself cautions that Q4 forecasts assume $0 China data center compute revenue.
As an additional concern, the otherwise highly detailed press release conspicuously fails to name Jensen Huang, the company’s CEO who resigned days earlier.
Instead of being upfront, Nvidia merely mentioned “leadership transition and the search for a new chief executive officer,” as well as the board committee’s vague investigation that commenced with an incredible assertion that “the board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised” as a result of Huang’s conduct.

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- CoinShares sold its entire corporate treasury position in Ethereum and half its Solana, freeing up $19.3 million.
- CEO Jean-Marie Mognetti framed it as capital discipline, not a bearish bet; these were small treasury positions, not client assets, and CoinShares still manages billions in both tokens.
- The sale landed amid a sharp market downturn, but the firm posted a strong quarter and is set to join the Russell indices in December.
CoinShares, one of Europe’s largest digital-asset managers, has sold its entire corporate treasury holding of Ethereum and half of its Solana.
It’s a move that might look like a loss of conviction but is really about something more prosaic: funding a stock buyback.
The decision, disclosed Tuesday in the firm’s third-quarter results, freed up $19.3 million, comprising $16.6 million from the Ethereum sale and $2.7 million from offloading half its Solana.
ETH price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
That covers nearly half of the $40 million share-repurchase program the Jersey-based firm’s board approved in October, and the company was explicit that the proceeds are being “reallocating that capital towards share repurchases.”
CEO Jean-Marie Mognetti framed it as capital discipline rather than a bearish call. “We took the same approach to preparing for the share repurchase program,” he said, noting the sales give the company “the flexibility to act when conditions allow.”
In other words, CoinShares is converting idle treasury crypto into dry powder to buy back its own stock, which it can do under an authorization allowing repurchases of up to 25% of shares outstanding over five years.
The timing is notable. The sale lands during a brutal stretch for crypto markets. Bitcoin was trading around $63,200 on Wednesday, down from six-figure levels earlier in the cycle, while Ethereum sat near $1,770 and Solana around $74, both well off their recent highs.
Spot Ethereum ETFs, meanwhile, have bled cash for days, shedding $29.1 million on Nov. 17 to extend a multi-day outflow streak that has turned Decrypt’s ETF sentiment gauge “bearish.”
Those are precisely the risk-off conditions that have battered Bitcoin treasury firms and pressured the broader sector. For a company whose stock is poised to join the Russell indices in December, deploying capital into buybacks at depressed prices is a conventional play, even if the optics of a crypto manager selling crypto invite a second look.
In terms of scale, these were small corporate treasury positions, not client assets. CoinShares’ total assets under management recovered to $7.4 billion by quarter-end, up from $5.5 billion three months earlier, and its core business of digital-asset investment products is untouched by the treasury move.
The firm actually swung to a strong quarter, posting $39.6 million in net income as net inflows accelerated to $125 million and its lending and trading desks rebounded.
So the sale isn’t CoinShares souring on Ethereum or Solana, assets it still manages billions in on behalf of clients. It’s a treasury-management decision by a newly profitable, soon-to-be-index-listed company choosing to return capital to shareholders rather than let a modest crypto position sit on its balance sheet.

items.author: Oluwapelumi Adejumo
items.content:
Quick Take
- Backpack secured CFTC approval for a US futures exchange and clearinghouse, with plans to unite its global crypto derivatives business.
- The move could challenge offshore exchanges' dominance by giving American traders access to deeper international liquidity and better execution.
- Backpack has yet to disclose its launch date, initial contracts or which overseas traders can access its unified marketplace.
Crypto exchange Backpack has secured US regulatory approval to launch a futures exchange aimed at uniting American and international trading liquidity.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) designated Backpack's TLD Markets as a regulated futures exchange on Nov. 16, three days after approving its affiliated clearinghouse, TLD Clearing.
The approvals establish the regulatory foundation for Backpack to offer leveraged crypto perpetual futures to American traders while connecting them to the company's international trading operations.
However, Backpack's ambitions extend beyond entering the American derivatives market. The company wants to consolidate its global trading business under a single US-regulated exchange, eliminating the separation between domestic and overseas customers.
Backpack CEO Armani Ferrante said:
“There will be no Backpack international vs Backpack USA. Our entire platform will be operating on our CFTC regulated venue.”
The move represents a significant shift for a company that began in Chicago nearly four years ago before expanding its operations overseas.
Ferrante recalled that Backpack was “forced offshore” early in its development, prompting the company to establish operations across international markets while pursuing regulatory approval.
He described the CFTC approval as the culmination of nearly four years of work to return to the United States.
Backpack targets global crypto liquidity under US regulation
The proposed structure could reshape how American traders access cryptocurrency derivatives, particularly perpetual futures, which allow investors to maintain leveraged positions without a fixed expiration date.
Historically, regulatory restrictions have separated American crypto derivatives markets from much of the trading activity concentrated on offshore exchanges.
This fragmentation can limit available liquidity, widen the difference between buying and selling prices, and increase the cost of executing large transactions.
Backpack wants to address this by bringing eligible American and international traders into a shared order book, allowing their buy and sell orders to interact within the same regulated marketplace.
Under such an arrangement, an American trader seeking to purchase Bitcoin perpetual futures could potentially execute against sell orders submitted by overseas participants.
A larger pool of competing orders could improve market depth, narrow spreads and reduce the price impact of substantial trades.
Backpack US President Mark Wetjen said the initiative could help shift “price discovery from offshore unregulated venues to the United States.”
The company also plans to offer round-the-clock trading, support fiat and cryptocurrency collateral, and introduce cross-margining, allowing eligible positions to share available collateral.
The exchange will operate through TLD Markets, while its US-registered clearinghouse, TLD Clearing, will handle qualifying transactions.
Backpack's international reach provides an existing business to support this ambition. The company says it serves customers across more than 150 countries and regions and has processed over $450 billion in trading volume.
However, the extent to which that activity will move onto the US-regulated platform remains unclear.
Backpack has not disclosed its initial perpetual futures contracts, which overseas participants will be eligible to access the unified order book, or when trading will begin. Its US website is also currently accepting waitlist registrations.
items.title: Backpack’s US approval could threaten offshore exchanges’ grip on crypto futures trading
